author: phaware-artie
body:
## Problem

The rig-level Reviewer role (Jira P23-2376) replaces the externally-hosted Augment review app with an in-town agent that posts GitHub PR reviews under a dedicated identity. The foundation for that role — its config, role plumbing, the priority-badge output contract, and the review-posting commands — needs AI review coverage before more of the role is built on top of it.

This change already landed on `main` via a refinery fast-forward (commit `d6b15b74`) **without** going through the normal PR/Augment-review path (a separate refinery bypass, reported to the Mayor). This PR exists **solely to obtain that missing Augment review coverage** for the merged code — it is review-only and will be closed unmerged; any findings will be addressed on a fresh MR branch.

## Solution

The change adds the `reviewer` role end-to-end at the foundation level: role registration (`AllRoles`/`RigRoles`, `reviewer.toml`, role template, theme, cmd role detection) and a tap-guard that confines the role to its only sanctioned write surfaces (it blocks `gh pr review`, `gh pr merge`, `git push`, `gt refinery pr`, and thread resolution).

The per-rig review configuration is added to both `MergeQueueConfig` copies: a `review` block (perspectives, finding caps, `max_rounds`, `parallel`) plus `reviewer_local`/`reviewer_token_env`, with validation and a `ReviewIterations()` resolver (`review.max_rounds` → `pr_review_loop_max` → default) so the number of review iterations is configurable per rig.

The review-posting contract is implemented in tested Go: `parseThreadPriority` is widened to accept a neutral shields.io priority badge (with a shared emitter so emitter and parser cannot drift), a new `PRProvider.SubmitReview` posts a single COMMENT review with inline threads, and an `internal/reviewer` package holds the findings model, body/summary formatter, embedded default perspectives, and a rig→town→builtin perspective resolver. The `gt reviewer post`/`checkout`/`perspectives` commands wire it together.

Dispatch (`gt reviewer request`/`done` + worktree/session lifecycle), refinery patrol wiring, and crew integration are intentionally deferred to follow-ups so this foundation stays reviewable.

Design-Ref: docs/design/reviewer-role.md

body:
## Summary

Wires the merged cost & usage telemetry core (PR #535) into result recording for **#511 Part 1**. The `DbListener` now sums prompt/completion tokens per suite and prices them via the static `config/local_models.yaml` table, persisting `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens` and `estimated_cost_usd` on the `test_runs` row (both DB backends). This makes external-provider spend observable — the foundation the planned Superset cost panel (Part 2) and PM budget alarm (Part 3) read from.

Closes part 1 of #511 (telemetry recording). Parts 2 (Superset panel) and 3 (PM sweep alarm) will follow as their own phase-PRs on the same issue.

## How to review

**Start here:** `src/rfc/db_listener.py` — `on_suite_end()` now aggregates token usage and computes cost before building the `TestRun`. That's the behavioural core.

**Key changes (review order):**
1. `src/rfc/db_listener.py` — sums `prompt_eval_count`/`eval_count` across the suite's tests and calls `estimate_cost(...)` with the loaded pricing table (critical).
2. `src/rfc/cost_estimator.py` — new `load_pricing_table()` file loader; fail-open to `{}` on a missing/unreadable config or absent PyYAML (critical — the skip-and-log behaviour).
3. `src/rfc/test_database.py` — three new `test_runs` columns + `TestRun` fields, on both the native sqlite3 and SQLAlchemy backends, with idempotent ADD COLUMN migrations (schema; read carefully but mechanical mirroring between backends).
4. `tests/*` — token aggregation, priced vs free-tier cost, no-metrics zero case, cross-backend round-trip, and the file-loader unit tests (mostly mechanical).

**What to ignore:** the per-backend INSERT/column edits in `test_database.py` are symmetric boilerplate — the judgement calls are the per-run-aggregate design (kept off `test_results` to preserve the lean-table refactor) and the fail-open pricing load.

## Evidence of testing

<details>
<summary>pytest output</summary>

```

```
</details>

<details>

## Critical changes

**Database schema (with migration):** `test_runs` gains `prompt_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0`, `completion_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0`, `estimated_cost_usd REAL DEFAULT 0` on both backends. Existing databases are upgraded by idempotent `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` migrations (sqlite `try/except`, Postgres `IF NOT EXISTS`), so no manual migration is required. Defaults are concrete zeros (no NULLs), so old readers are unaffected.

**Listener contract:** `TestRun` gains three fields with zero defaults; all construction sites use keyword args, so this is additive. No public keyword signatures change. New public function `cost_estimator.load_pricing_table()`.

author: brandon-fryslie
body:
## What

Reskins the **Observe** movement's `bind` node from the `.bd-*` wiring diagram into the **CRT oscilloscope in X-Y (Lissajous) mode**, making the movement cohesive with its `trigger` sibling (PR #22). Closes the last child of `mit-styling-aj1.6`.

- **CH1 scroll → X axis, CH2 animation → Y axis.** A phosphor dot rides the `y=x` diagonal because *both coordinates ARE the one real `p`* — a straight diagonal IS the proof scroll and animation are bound 1:1 (the `animation-timeline: scroll()` idea).
- Reuses `trigger`'s CRT shell (`.sc` + `.sc-trace` + chrome); only the trace geometry, a faint dashed ideal guide, and the projection crosshairs are added (`.xy-*`).
- Removes the now-dead `.bd-*` CSS block.

## How it honors the laws

- **`[LAW:one-source-of-truth]`** — `x` and `y` are the *same* `p`; the lock is read off `Δ = |x−y|` (structurally `0.00`), never a second fabricated signal. The diagonal is a *consequence* of the data, not an asserted decoration.
- **`[LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow]`** — `paint(p,n)` writes state only; the dot's glow is a CSS `@keyframes` the global reduced-motion kill stops. No imperative animation branch.

## Verification (Chrome DevTools MCP, full scroll range)

Swept `p` across `[0,1]`:

| p | dot (left, top) | clip reveal | crosshairs | readout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.03 | (3.04%, 96.96%) | 96.96% | vx=hz=3.04% | X 0.03 · Y 0.03 · Δ 0.00 |
| 0.63 | (63.15%, 36.85%) | 36.85% | vx=hz=63.15% | X 0.63 · Y 0.63 · Δ 0.00 |
| 1.00 | (100%, 0%) | 0% | vx=hz=100% | X 1.00 · Y 1.00 · Δ 0.00 · LOCKED 1:1 |

Dot rides the diagonal exactly; clip reveals the trace up to the dot; `vx`/`hz` equal-length by construction; note flips at `p≥0.5`. No page console errors (only an environmental `favicon.ico` 404 from the dev server). Visually distinct from the azure radial gauge; cohesive teal CRT signature with `trigger`.

## O que foi feito

Redesign visual do app num sistema coeso (tema dark, marca violet, cantos menos arredondados, sem glow/blur):

- **Feed** — `EventCard` reescrito com hero (capa + bloco-data + status + organizador como assinatura), prova social (`EventAttendeesStack`) e RSVP inline. Variante sem foto com gradiente da marca.
- **Perfil** (próprio e de outro) — header com avatar + ring, stats inline, grade de eventos em 2 colunas, categorias preferidas e estados vazios (próprio / outro / privado).
- **Evento** (detalhe) — hero imersivo sob a status bar, bloco-data no canto, meta hierárquica (local + data/hora), descrição e seção "quem vai".
- **Mapa** — card de preview vira mini-hero (capa + bloco-data + status + local · distância + prova social); controles (zoom + mapa de calor + locate) numa pílula única; criação unificada de **evento** e **rolê** num seletor (`MapCreateButton`); chips de categoria (`MapCategoryChips`, sincronizados com o filtro); pins com prova social condicional (organizador quando há capa, pilha de participantes quando não — some ao abrir detalhes) e distância até o evento.

## Por que foi feito

Unificar a linguagem visual em todas as superfícies, com hierarquia mais clara, prova social consistente e uma estética dark mais polida — alinhada à preferência do produto (menos arredondado, sem brilho/blur).

1. `pnpm exec expo run:ios` (ou `expo start`).
2. **Feed**: cards com e sem foto; tocar no organizador abre o perfil.
3. **Perfil**: próprio (CTA de editar, grade) e de outro (incl. privado / sem eventos).

author: mbasmanova
body:
Summary:

Splits the TPC-H optimizer test into two, one per concern. `TpchPlanTest` asserts plan shape and runs with no data — it drives the optimizer off injected statistics, so it works anywhere without generated tables. `TpchResultTest` checks query results against a small generated dataset. Previously one suite mixed both, forcing the plan-shape checks to depend on real data.

Plan-shape tests get their cardinalities from a new `TestConnector::addTpchTables(scaleFactor)`, which registers the TPC-H tables with statistics derived from the spec — row counts, per-column distinct counts, and value ranges — and zero rows. `QueryTestBase` gains a `configureTestConnector()` hook so a suite can pick stats-only or data-backed tables.

Verifying the filter predicates in `TpchPlanTest` required a fix to the plan matcher: the `Filter` matcher dropped the aliases its child bound, so a column aliased on a scan could not be named in an aggregate above a filter. A filter does not rename columns, so it now passes the child's symbols through.

Also restores `count(distinct ps_suppkey)` in q16, which now plans in the multi-node case.

author: akcorca
body:
**Step 3 (final) of the query/review unification.** Now that `nose query <paths> base=<ref>` runs review's exact detection (#387), `nose review` is deprecated — same scan-deprecation playbook (#375): it still works, but `query` is the one surface.

## What's in
- **TTY-gated nudge** on `nose review` → `nose query <paths> base=<ref>` (interactive-only; piped/CI/test runs never spammed).
- **`capabilities`** moves `review` from `commands.stable` to `commands.deprecated` (joining `scan`); stable is now `[capabilities, il, query, semantic-pack, stats]`.
- **Parity test** `query_base_matches_review_findings`: on one git fixture, `review --format json` and `query base= --format json` report the identical set of `(family_id, fire_eligible)` — the deprecation is *earned*, not asserted. (Holds by construction: both call `detect_divergences`.)

## Docs
review.md deprecation banner; usage.md task-table + command-list point at `query base=`; CHANGELOG (review under Changed-breaking + Deprecated). Capabilities test asserts `deprecated = [review, scan]`.

## The unification, complete
One verb (`query`) with orthogonal composable axes — **filters × OR × negate × group × since × base × views × gate**. `scan` and `review` are now both deprecated aliases over the same dataset/detection. This is the [Capabilities over features](https://wiki.g15e.com/pages/Capabilities%20over%20features) end-state: maximal capability, minimal surface.

Closes the 4 & 5 design+build (Axis A #386 temporality → Axis B #387 diff-scope → this). Local preflight green: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, full tests, awiki. Still **0.9.1** — release held.

Performance foundation for v0.2.0. Replaces the per-particle radial-gradient + `save`/`restore` + double-arc draw block with **cached offscreen-canvas sprites blitted via `drawImage`**.

### What changed
- **New `src/sprites.ts`**

author: austinywang
body:
## Summary

Adds a less-destructive sibling to Ghostty's **Cmd+K** (`clear_screen`), which wipes **both** the visible screen and the scrollback. The new **Clear Screen (Keep Scrollback)** action clears only the visible screen and **preserves scrollback history**, bound by default to **Cmd+Shift+K** (verified unbound in both Ghostty defaults and cmux). Cmd+K behavior is unchanged.

## Approach (cmux-only — no Ghostty submodule change)

The action delivers **Ctrl-L (form-feed) as ordinary keyboard input** to the focused terminal — exactly as if the user pressed the key — via the same path as the existing `sendCtrlFToTerminal` action:

- At a shell prompt: the shell clears the viewport and redraws the prompt while leaving scrollback intact. Ghostty's native `^L`-at-a-prompt heuristic (`Terminal.zig`, see ghostty #905) even scrolls the cleared screen into scrollback when shell prompt markers are present.
- In a full-screen TUI (vim/less/htop): the program simply repaints.

Because this is plain keyboard input rather than an erase sequence injected through the PTY-output parser, it **never mutates the terminal behind the running program's back**, so it is safe on the alternate screen. (An earlier revision injected `ESC[22J` directly; autoreview correctly flagged that it bypasses Ghostty's alternate-screen safeguards, and there is no libghostty C API to detect the alternate screen from the embedder.)

## Shared behavior path

One model path behind every entrypoint:
`TerminalSurface.clearScreenKeepingScrollback()` → `TerminalPanel.clearScreenKeepingScrollback()` → `TabManager.clearFocusedTerminalKeepingScrollback()`, invoked from:
- **Keyboard shortcut** (`AppDelegate` → `matchConfiguredShortcut(.clearScreenKeepScrollback)`), default **Cmd+Shift+K**.
- **Command palette** — `palette.terminalClearScreenKeepScrollback` ("Clear Screen (Keep Scrollback)").

The shortcut is fully customizable: registered in `KeyboardShortcutSettings` (Settings UI), supported in `~/.config/cmux/cmux.json` (`shortcuts.bindings.clearScreenKeepScrollback`), and mirrored in the `CmuxSettings.ShortcutAction` package (drift test stays green).

## Localization

`shortcut.clearScreenKeepScrollback.label` and `command.terminalClearScreenKeepScrollback.title` added to `Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` (English + Japanese). Web docs description added inline (en + ja) in `web/data/cmux-shortcuts.ts`. `web/data/cmux.schema.json` and the `cmux-settings` shortcut-actions reference updated.

## Testing

`cmuxTests/TerminalClearScreenKeepScrollbackTests.swift` drives a real Ghostty surface running a controlled raw-mode capture program, invokes the clear, and asserts the byte delivered to the PTY is a single Ctrl-L form-feed (`0x0c`) — i.e. ordinary input, not an injected erase sequence. Wired into `cmux.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` (verified by `scripts/lint-pbxproj-test-wiring.sh`). Follows the headless-CI `hasLiveSurface` guard pattern from `GhosttyDECCKMArrowKeyTests`.

author: vaibhaviphalle
body: ## Summary Phase 1.1 of the original spec. Turns "we have a project skeleton" into "we have a hashed, reproducible corpus on disk that downstream stages can chunk". > **Note:** this PR is **stacked on `cursor/foundation-scaffolding-02ce`** (PR #1). Until #1 merges, the diff against `main` will include both steps' changes; once #1 merges, this diff auto-recomputes to show only Step 2's additions. ## Step / Phase - [x] Step 1 — Foundation - [x] Step 2 — Corpus + Ingestion - [ ] Step 3 — Chunking - [ ] Step 4 — Embeddings + Index - [ ] Step 5 — Retrieval + Citation - [ ] Step 6 — Hybrid + Rerank + Enforcement - [ ] Step 7 — Eval + CI gate - [ ] Step 8 — API + UI - [ ] Step 9 — Polish ## What lands ### Declarative corpus registry — `config/corpus.yaml` 11 RFCs in scope: **6749, 6750, 6819, 7519, 7591, 7592, 7636, 8252, 8628, 8693, 9068** — covering OAuth 2.0 core, JWT family, modern flows (PKCE, device, token exchange), and the threat model. HTML/PDF (OIDC, SAML) and Markdown (Keycloak, Auth0) parsers are deferred to a follow-up so this PR stays reviewable. ### `src/auth_rag/ingestion/` | Module | Role | |---|---| | `models.py` | Frozen Pydantic models: `SourceSpec`, `Section`, `ParsedDocument`, `ManifestEntry`, `Manifest`. Every cross-module data structure goes through one of these. | | `corpus_config.py` | YAML loader + duplicate-`doc_id` check + validation. | | `downloader.py` | Resumable, hash-verified, atomic-write HTTP fetcher (httpx + tenacity). 50 MB per-file cap. Sidecar `.meta.json` per file. `AUTH_RAG_OFFLINE=1` kill-switch refuses any network in CI. | | `rfc_parser.py` | Section-aware parser exploiting the canonical RFC text format. Captures hierarchical section numbers (`4.1.1`), page boundaries (form-feeds + `[Page N]` fallback), parent section ids, and char offsets. Handles TOC, front matter, and authors-block edge cases. | | `scrubber.py` | Regex PII scrubber (emails + non-RFC-5737 IPv4). Idempotent. Preserves documentation IPs explicitly. | | `manifest.py` | Atomic JSON writer/reader with an **integrity hash chain** over `(corpus_version + entries)` excluding `fetched_at` — so re-running ingest on identical content reproduces the same hash (this becomes the index-rebuild key in Step 4). | | `pipeline.py` | Orchestrator: download → parse → scrub → persist → manifest. All-or-nothing: aborts before manifest write on any per-source failure. | ### CLI ``` auth-rag ingest [--config PATH] [--only DOC_ID] ``` ### Dependencies - `httpx ~0.27` added (lower CVE history than `requests`, modern timeouts/connection pooling). - `uv.lock` refreshed (233 packages, deterministic). ### Architecture record - **`docs/adr/0007-ingestion-architecture.md`** — *Accepted.* Documents the declarative-corpus + manifest-as-truth + section-aware-parsing rationale and the alternatives considered (no manifest / fixed-size chunking now / off-the-shelf RFC loaders). ### Licenses `LICENSES/README.md` records IETF RFCs under BCP 78 (public domain), with attribution placeholders for OIDC / SAML / Keycloak / Auth0 sources that arrive with the HTML/Markdown loaders. ### Tests (53 new) Six new test modules covering: - Pydantic model invariants (immutability, validators, round-trip). - YAML loader (valid, missing, malformed, duplicate ids, empty sources, **the real `config/corpus.yaml` itself**). - Downloader using `httpx.MockTransport` (offline by design): cache-hit skip, sha mismatch rejects + cleans `.part`, size cap, retry exhaustion, `AUTH_RAG_OFFLINE=1` enforcement. - RFC parser against a synthetic fixture that mirrors a real IETF RFC structure (header, TOC, numbered sections, form-feeds, footers): section count, titles, page numbers, parent-section ids, TOC dedupe, metadata (RFC#, category, stream), determinism, fallback path for unrecognized formats. - Manifest: round-trip, sort stability, hash invariance under `fetched_at`, hash variance under content change, tamper detection, malformed-JSON handling. - Scrubber: emails, IPv4, RFC 5737 doc-IP preservation, idempotency. - End-to-end pipeline: full download → parse → scrub → persist → manifest cycle on the synthetic RFC. Verifies emails are redacted, doc-IPs preserved, `--only` filtering works. ## How was this tested? Locally (matches CI exactly): ``` uv sync --frozen --extra dev → ok uv run ruff check . → All checks passed uv run ruff format --check . → 37 files already formatted uv run mypy src → Success: no issues found in 20 source files uv run deptry src → No dependency issues found uv run pytest -m unit → 86 passed, coverage 92.53% uv run pip-audit --skip-editable → No known vulnerabilities found uv run auth-rag ingest --help → ok ``` CI gates inherited from Step 1: `lint`, `test (3.11)`, `test (3.12)`, `pip-audit`, `secret-scan`. ## Eval impact N/A — eval pipeline lands in Step 7. The manifest hash designed in this PR is what the Step 4 indexer and Step 7 CI eval will key off of. ## Out of scope (intentionally deferred) - HTML / PDF / Markdown loaders (OIDC Core 1.0, SAML 2.0, Keycloak, Auth0). Lands in a follow-up before Step 4. - Persistent embedding/LLM cache (was previously planned via diskcache; deferred to Step 5/6 with a properly-scoped library choice — see prior CI fix commit). - Real-network integration test (would require either committed snapshot fixtures or hitting `rfc-editor.org` from CI; deferred to Step 9 polish). ## Checklist - [x] `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` pass - [x] `mypy src` passes (strict) - [x] `pytest -m unit` passes (86 tests, 92.53% coverage) - [x] `pip-audit` clean - [x] No secrets committed - [x] ADR added (0007) for the design decisions in this step - [x] README updated with Step 2 quick-start - [x] LICENSES recorded

author: alexander-turner
body:
## What & why

When an ephemeral ClaudeGuard session exits, the resume command Claude Code normally surfaces is gone — by design, because ephemeral mode destroys the config volume (`/home/node/.claude`) that holds the transcript, so there is nothing to reattach to. But the teardown was silent about it, leaving users to assume resume was broken.

This adds a one-line note on ephemeral exit explaining that history was discarded and how to keep it (relaunch with `CLAUDE_PERSIST=1`, which enables `claude-guard --resume` / `--continue`). The hint fires only when a session actually ran, so an interrupt during the build stays silent.

While in this code, the launcher's final launch path was split out of the already-large `bin/claude-guard` into a new sourced lib, `bin/lib/launch.bash`, matching the existing `bin/lib/*.bash` convention — leaving a short, readable call sequence in the wrapper.

## Security boundary impact

None. The fail-closed read-only-guardrail proof (`verify_guardrails_readonly` → refuse to launch if writable) moved file (into `bin/lib/launch.bash`) but its logic, error string, and `exit 1` path are byte-equivalent to the original inline code. The resume hint is purely informational and prints only after teardown.

## How it was tested

- [x] `pytest tests/test_claude_wrapper.py tests/test_sandbox_config.py tests/test_kcov_harness.py tests/test_ephemeral.py` — 418 passed.
- [x] `pre-commit run` on all changed files — shellcheck/shfmt/shellharden/ruff/codespell/secrets all pass.
- [x] Manual sandboxed-launch repro (fake docker): exit code passes through, `LAUNCHED-CLAUDE` reached, resume hint present for ephemeral / absent for persist, no spurious bug-report hint.
- New tests: the persistence-model parametrization now asserts the hint appears **iff** ephemeral (and `CLAUDE_PERSIST=1` is named), and the interrupt-during-build test asserts the hint is **absent** when no session ran (pins the `_session_launched` gate in both directions).

## Changes

- `bin/claude-guard`: add `print_ephemeral_resume_hint` + `_session_launched` gate (called from `_ephemeral_cleanup`); replace the ~150-line inline launch tail with a sourced lib and a short call sequence.
- `bin/lib/launch.bash` (new): `build_docker_flags`, `wait_for_worktree_sync`, `verify_guardrails_or_abort`, `warn_if_workspace_unwritable`, `build_ccr_flags`, `build_scrub_allow_flags`, `prepare_claude_auth`, `resolve_permission_mode`, `launch_claude`. Builders end with explicit `return 0` so a trailing falsy `[[ … ]] && …` can't trip the caller's `set -e`.
- `tests/_kcov.py`: enroll the new lib in `KCOV_EXCLUDED` (library-only, covered behaviorally through the wrapper suite).
- `tests/test_sandbox_config.py`: relocate the static-grep assertions for the moved logic to the new lib; the `--dangerously-skip-permissions` guard now checks both files.
- `changelog.d/`: added fragment.

**Follow-up commits (CI):**
- `fix(test)`: `tests/test_firewall_zombie_reaping.py` — the supervisor subprocess's flat 60s outer timeout was smaller than its own 30s inner settle-deadline plus the fork-heavy spawn/cleanup, so under `pytest -n auto` CPU contention the blunt outer timeout preempted the diagnostic inner deadline (opaque `TimeoutExpired`). Tie the two bounds to one source (inner 45s, outer = inner + headroom) and poll only the retired pids instead of rescanning all of `/proc`.
- `docs(claude)`: `CLAUDE.md` — never dismiss a red check as an "infra flake"; diagnose and fix the root cause (or hand off explicitly).

## Lessons Learned

- **What**: When extracting top-level bash into functions in a sourced lib, ensure each "builder" function does not end on a conditional (`[[ … ]] && …`, `((expr))`); end it with an explicit `return 0`.
- **Where**: any `language: bash` helper sourced into a `set -euo pipefail` caller (here, `bin/lib/*.bash`).
- **Why**: a trailing falsy conditional is harmless at top level (exempt from `set -e`) but becomes the function's return value once wrapped, so the bare function call aborts the whole script — a failure mode invisible until the extraction, and one that won't surface in a syntax check.

body:
## Problem

In proactive mode, `_check_silent` only suppresses a response when a line is **exactly** `SILENT`. If the model decides *not* to notify but writes prose like "nothing here warrants interrupting the user" **without** the keyword, that text gets sent to your Telegram verbatim as a notification — the opposite of staying quiet.

`main`'s proactive prompt still had the weak phrasing ("include the word SILENT … your reasoning will be logged but not sent"), which doesn't make clear that a keyword-less response *is* the notification.

## Fix

Hardens the `_MODE_LAYERS["proactive"]` instruction:
- Makes `SILENT` **mandatory** when not notifying.
- Explicitly warns that any response without `SILENT` is sent to the user verbatim.
- Tells the model to write `SILENT` rather than prose explaining why it's staying quiet.

Prompt-only change, no behavioral code touched. Ports the intent of `697dd4c` (from the now-deleted `claude/fix-issue-RVddk` branch) onto current `main`'s refactored prompt structure.

body:
## Problem

The backend Koyeb deploy failed at `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`:

```
warn: This version of pnpm requires at least Node.js v22.13
warn: The current version of Node.js is v20.20.2
Error [ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE]: No such built-in module: node:sqlite
  ... corepack/v1/pnpm/11.6.0/dist/pnpm.mjs ...
```

`backend/Dockerfile` uses `node:20-alpine` and ran `corepack prepare pnpm@latest`, which now resolves to **pnpm 11.6.0**. pnpm 11 requires **Node 22.13+** and imports the `node:sqlite` builtin (absent on Node 20), so the install crashes.

## Fix

- Pin both Docker build stages to `pnpm@10.32.1` — the version that generated the `lockfileVersion: 9.0` lockfile, fully compatible with Node 20.
- Declare `"packageManager": "pnpm@10.32.1"` in the root `package.json` so corepack (and Vercel's frontend build) use the same pinned version.

No application code or schema changes.

## What's automated

**Firefox Add-ons (AMO)**
1. Submit the extension manually once (human review required for new listings).
2. Generate API credentials at <https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/developers/addon/api/key/>.

**GitHub secrets** to set on the repo:
| Secret | Source |
|---|---|
| `CHROME_CLIENT_ID` | Google Cloud OAuth client ID |

author: cleanexpo
body:
## WS4 — Performance elevation (safe, measurable, reversible)

Conservative perf pass on live prod. This codebase is already heavily
optimized (LazyClientComponents in the root layout, ISR on the Authority
Hub, `optimizePackageImports`, `serverExternalPackages`, dynamic imports
across the dashboard, `preload="none"` on the homepage video, lazy
`jspdf`/`@remotion/player`), so source-discovery yielded **one** genuinely
clean, behavior-preserving win worth shipping. Padding with risky changes
was deliberately avoided.

### The win — defer Remotion core on `/dashboard/admin/remotion-studio`

The Remotion `Player` was already `next/dynamic({ ssr: false })`, but the
`SocialReel` / `ExplainerVideo` **compositions** were imported statically
at module top. Those compositions pull in the Remotion core runtime, so
webpack placed a **~128 KB chunk into the page's INITIAL First Load JS** —
even though the compositions only ever render *inside* the already-deferred
`<Player>`.

Converted the two composition imports to `next/dynamic({ ssr: false })`,
matching the existing Player pattern.

### Before / after (measured)

Measured from `.next/server/app/.../page_client-reference-manifest.js`
chunk references against the built static chunks:

| | Remotion-core chunk (`55eb4b32…`) |
|---|---|
| **Before** | `EAGER` — in initial First Load JS (**128 KB**) |
| **After** | `defer` — **0 KB** Remotion in initial First Load JS |

The compiled chunk is **byte-identical** (same content hash `55eb4b32…`) —
it simply moves from eager to lazy and now downloads alongside the Player.

### Why it's behavior-preserving & reversible
- Compositions are consumed only inside `<Player>`, which is itself
  dynamically imported with the same `ssr: false`. No render path changes.
- Revert = change the two `dynamic()` wrappers back to static `import`s.

### Verification
- `JWT_SECRET=… DATABASE_URL="" npm run build:vercel` → **✓ Compiled successfully**
- `npm run type-check` → **clean**
- `npm run lint` (`eslint . --max-warnings 0`) → **clean**
- `npm test -- --coverage` → **exit 0** · `Tests: 4157 passed, 4385 total` · enforced coverage floors intact

### Larger / riskier opportunities NOT taken (follow-up list)
- **Migrate Fontshare → `next/font/local`.** `components/ClientFonts.tsx`
  loads Satoshi via a client-side injected stylesheet (non-blocking, but a
  network hop + potential CLS). The component itself documents the upgrade
  path, blocked on placing woff2 files in `public/fonts/`. Eliminates a
  render-path font request. Not behavior-identical → separate PR.
- **Dashboard layout below-fold widgets.** `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`
  (`'use client'`, on every dashboard route) statically imports several
  non-critical widgets (`MascotTip`, `MonthlyStoryCard`, `AIPMFloatingButton`,
  and a `ProductTour` that's also lazy-loaded in `LazyClientComponents`).
  Lazy-loading these would shave the shared dashboard bundle, but it touches
  every authenticated route — needs its own focused PR + visual verification.
- **recharts (40 import sites).** Each chart page bundles recharts into its
  own route chunk. A shared lazy chart wrapper could defer it where charts
  are below-fold, but it's a broad 40-file change — too wide for one safe PR.

### Residual risk
Very low. Single admin-only page (owner-guarded). Compiled output identical;
only the eager/lazy chunk boundary changed. Worst case = revert two lines.

body:
Fixes two seed bugs that surfaced in production (ESPA wasn't showing in Brand Vault):

1. **Stray tenant** — the seed hardcoded tenant id `lhcapital`, creating a *second* tenant on a DB whose real admin user lives on a different (cuid) tenant. The seeded ESPA brand landed on the stray tenant, so it didn't appear for the real user. Now: if the admin user already exists, **reuse their tenant**; only create the default tenant on a truly fresh DB.
2. **Prisma 7 client** — the seed built its own `new PrismaClient()` with no adapter, which throws under Prisma 7 (the schema no longer carries the URL). Now imports the shared Neon-adapter client from `lib/db`.

Prod was corrected out-of-band (ESPA moved to the real tenant; the empty stray tenant deleted) — verified: 1 tenant, brands = LH Capital, The SIMRP, ESPA by BizPower. Re-running the seed is now idempotent and tenant-correct.

author: skeptomai
body:
Closes #347. **CRITICAL / host-destructive.**

## The bug
Running critest left `pelagos-cri`'s sandbox store inconsistent ("phantom" sandboxes — listed but `crictl rmp` says *not found*), and the kubelet's GC of those made pelagos **`unlink` the host's usr-merge `/bin -> usr/bin` symlink**, breaking SSH (login shell `/bin/bash` stops resolving). 2 of 2 critest nodes lost `/bin`; 0 of 4 non-critest nodes did. Restarting `pelagos-cri` (which clears the phantoms) stops the deletion.

## Mechanism & approach
A teardown/cleanup removal computed a base path from inconsistent sandbox/container state that was **empty or `/`-rooted**, so `<base>/…` resolved to a host path. (`PathBuf::join` also **replaces** the base when given an absolute component — `sandboxes_dir().join("/bin")` → `/bin`.)

I could **not isolate the exact trigger line** without reproducing it, and reproduction is host-destructive — it must only run on disposable cluster nodes, never a dev host. So the fix is **defense-in-depth that makes the whole class structurally impossible**, applied across every removal in the GC/teardown surface.

## The fix
- **`paths::is_safe_to_remove` + `guarded_remove_dir_all`/`guarded_remove_file`** — refuse (log + no-op) to remove any path that isn't a **strict descendant** of a pelagos-managed root (`/run/pelagos`, `/var/lib/pelagos`, rootless equivalents), and never a wholesale parent dir (`containers/`, `sandboxes/`, `images/`, `layers/`, `volumes/`, the roots themselves). Lexically normalizes `.`/`..` **without following symlinks**.
- Applied at every dynamic-path removal reachable from CRI GC / container teardown: overlay/dns/hosts teardown (`container.rs`), `pelagos rm` (`cli/rm.rs`), ephemeral overlay + state-dir cleanup (`cli/run.rs`), `pelagos sandbox rm` (`sandbox.rs`), OCI `delete` (`oci.rs`).
- **Reject empty / `/`-laden / `.`/`..` ids at the source** in `pelagos rm`, `remove_sandbox`, and the pelagos-cri state file removers, so an empty id can no longer collapse to a parent dir (wiping ALL containers/sandboxes) or escape it.

## Tests
- `paths::tests::test_guard_*` — `is_safe_to_remove` rejects `/`, `/bin`, `/usr`, `/etc`, the managed roots/parent dirs, and `join`/`..` escapes; accepts legitimate subpaths. `test_guarded_remove_refuses_unmanaged_dir` — functional proof the wrapper leaves an out-of-tree dir intact.
- `issue_347_no_host_destruction` (no root) — `pelagos rm` with path-like/empty names fails and the host `/bin` survives. Documented in `docs/INTEGRATION_TESTS.md`.
- `cargo test --lib` 377 pass; `cargo test -p pelagos-cri` 23 pass; clippy clean.

⚠️ **Do NOT re-run critest until this ships on the affected nodes.** Honest caveat: because the exact trigger wasn't isolated, this is a guard rather than a root-cause point-fix — but the guard covers the full removal surface and the unit tests prove it blocks every host path. If a phantom-sandbox repro can be captured on a disposable node, we can also point-fix the originating computation.

author: seonwooj0810
body:
Fixes #2618

## Problem
`FeignException.errorReading(...)` builds the exception by passing `request.body()` and `request.headers()` into the constructor parameters named `responseBody` / `responseHeaders`:

```java
return new FeignException(
    response.status(),
    format(...),
    request,
    cause,
    request.body(),     // <- responseBody slot
    request.headers()); // <- responseHeaders slot
```

As reported in #2618, this means that when an `IOException` is thrown while reading/decoding the response (see `InvocationContext.decode` and `ResponseHandler.handleResponse`), `FeignException.responseBody()` / `content()` / `contentUTF8()` / `responseHeaders()` return the **request** body and headers instead of the response. The maintainer confirmed in the thread that this looks like a bug.

## Fix
Read the response body into a `byte[]` and pass the **response** headers, mirroring the existing `errorStatus(...)` method. Reading is wrapped in a `try/catch (IOException ignored)` so a streamed or already-consumed body degrades gracefully to an empty body rather than throwing (consistent with `errorStatus`).

## Test evidence
Strengthened the existing `FeignExceptionTest.canCreateWithRequestAndResponse` to assert the *content*: the exception now carries the response body (`"response"`) rather than the request body (`"data"`), and exposes the response headers. Before the fix this assertion fails (`contentUTF8()` returned `"data"`).

```
./mvnw -pl core test -Dtest=FeignExceptionTest
Tests run: 14, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
BUILD SUCCESS
```

Verification done: (1) no in-flight PR (`gh pr list --search "responseBody"/"errorReading"` empty); (2) the only self-claim is a 2024-11-03 question that never produced a PR (>21 days stale); (3) code-focused change in `FeignException.java` + test; (4) confirmed the `request.body()` pattern still present on current master; (5) maintainer acknowledged the bug in-thread. Commit is DCO signed-off; google-java-format validation passes.

## Summary

The send button on the main chat input and the project workspace input was disabled whenever the textarea was empty, even when one or more files were attached. This blocked the "drop an image, hit send, ask the model to describe it" flow that ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini all support.

- Send is now enabled when either the trimmed text **or** the attachment list is non-empty, in both the main chat input and the project workspace input. The matching submit-handler guards were relaxed to match.
- The project workspace previously dropped attachments on the Redux handoff to the main chat (File objects don't survive a serializable store). A small module-level cache (`utils/pendingAttachments`) now carries the File objects across the navigation. The auto-submit pipeline takes them, compresses any accepted images via the existing `compressImage` helper, and ships them with the first message.
- The auto-submit `firedRef` was reworked into a per-cycle boolean (reset when `pendingAutoSubmit` goes false). The old prompt-string fingerprint would have falsely skipped a legitimate image-only message because an empty trimmed prompt equals the previous empty prompt.
- ImageGalleryView was intentionally left untouched — its quick-prompt flow is text-driven.

body:
## Summary

Adds a new `/api/stops/{stop_id}/departures` endpoint that returns upcoming departures for a stop, using real-time trip predictions when available and falling back to static schedule times.

### What changed

**1. GTFS static parsing** (`backend/services/gtfs_static.py`)
- Added `_parse_stop_times()` — parses `stop_times.txt` into a dict keyed by `trip_id` with ordered stop-time entries
- Added `_parse_trip_routes()` — parses `trips.txt` into a `trip_id → route_id` mapping
- Updated `parse_gtfs_static_bundle()` to include `stop_times` and `trip_routes` in the returned bundle

**2. SQLite cache** (`backend/services/gtfs_db.py`)
- Added `stop_times TEXT` and `trip_routes TEXT` columns to the `static_cache` table schema
- Added migration logic for existing databases
- Updated `load_cached_static()` and `save_cached_static()` to handle the new fields

**3. Departure query engine** (`backend/services/departure_query.py`)
- Added `_stop_time_to_timestamp()` helper — converts GTFS `HH:MM:SS` (including hours > 23) to Unix timestamps
- Added `get_stop_departures()` method that:
  - Finds all trips serving a stop from `stop_times.txt`
  - Checks for matching real-time trip updates
  - Uses predicted times when available, static schedule otherwise
  - Returns departures sorted by departure time with `type` field (`"predicted"` or `"scheduled"`)
  - Supports optional `limit` and `route_id` filtering

**4. In-memory cache** (`backend/services/cache.py`)
- Stores `stop_times` and `trip_routes` alongside existing route/stop data
- Added `get_stop_departures(stop_id, limit, route_id)` wrapper

**5. API endpoint** (`backend/api/routes.py`)
- `GET /api/stops/{stop_id}/departures` — returns `StopDeparturesResponse`
- Query params: `limit` (default 10), `route_id` (optional filter)
- Response includes `DepartureItem` with `minutes_away` computed from the departure time

**6. Tests** (`backend/tests/test_api.py`)
- Added `stop_times` and `trip_routes` data to `FakeCache`
- Tests cover: basic departures, limit parameter, route_id filter, and no-such-stop case

Closes #13

body:
## Summary

The deployed copilot over-refused: **28 of 32** answerable golden questions came back as
`no_verified_claims` refusals despite healthy retrieval (citation recall ≈ 0.89). Error-analysis on
the current `@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fast` model **falsified the committed report's
"verbatim-verification drop" (Cluster-A) diagnosis**: an instrumented probe showed `VERIFY_DROP=0` —
the model returned `{claims: []}` for 26/32 answerable questions, so the loss was at **generation,
not verification**. An isolating A/B spike pinned the cause to the `response_format: json_schema`
grammar-constrained decoding collapsing the small model onto an empty claims array
(`json_schema` 24/32 empty → `json_object` 0/32 empty, prompt/retrieval/verify held constant).

**Changes (all in `src/retrieval/generate/`, single-variable phases):**
- `response_format` `json_schema`→`json_object`, single-sourced across the REST + `env.AI`
  transports so they can't drift; removed the now-dead `RESPONSE_JSON_SCHEMA`.
- Hardened `parseGeneration` to coerce `json_object`'s free-form field variability (empty/null/
  missing) instead of crashing — `verifyClaims` stays the single content arbiter (unchanged).
- A two-shot answer/refusal exemplar (+ tightened "only answer if a passage DIRECTLY addresses the
  question") to hold refusal recall after emission was restored.
- A `repetition_penalty` trial was measured and **rejected** — it dropped citation-span validity by
  pushing the model off the verbatim quotes the guard requires.

**Measured (real adapters, `eval:delta`):** over-refusal **28→2**, answered **4→31**, refusal
precision **0.30→0.85**, refusal recall **1.0→0.92** (baseline 1.0 was a degenerate artifact of
near-total over-refusal), citation accuracy **0.71→0.82**, citation-span **0.60→0.77**, Promptfoo
gate pass **~30%→57%**. `EVAL_GATE_FLOOR` ratcheted **25%→50%**.

Residual: one no-answer over-reach + one repetitive answer — the deferred **Cluster-C text↔quote
entailment** gap (tracked in TECH_DEBT.md, DECISIONS D5). Spec + plan under
`docs/superpowers/`; full diagnosis story in JOURNAL.md.

`pg_stat_user_indexes`: the new `ix_silver_rt_feed_snapshots_provider_endpoint_srsid` = **0 scans, 1.9 MB**; the existing `source_realtime_snapshot_id` index = 17,402 scans.

## Why
The audit (a static read) correctly noted "no index leads with `(provider_id, endpoint_key)`" — but the real queries don't need that. They lead with `source_realtime_snapshot_id` (equality to the latest / `max()`), already served optimally by the existing single-column index. The only queries a composite would serve are non-selective scans where Postgres correctly prefers a Seq Scan. So the index is **1.9 MB + per-INSERT (~30s) write overhead for zero benefit** — carrying an index the planner never chooses is the exact anti-pattern this campaign removes.

## Change
Migration `0044` drops it `CONCURRENTLY` (autocommit_block, mirroring 0043/0021/0038). `downgrade` recreates it (restores 0043 for reversibility).

## Tests / verification
- Static contract test (`test_migration_0044_*`): revision chain, `DROP … CONCURRENTLY` in autocommit_block, downgrade recreates.
- Full offline suite **1029 passed**; `ruff` clean; single alembic head `0044`.
- CI `real-db-tests` applies 0043→0044 on a throwaway PG.
- Post-merge: re-confirm the index is gone on prod after `init-db`.

**Process note:** the audit's *perf* recommendations are now treated as hypotheses to EXPLAIN-verify on prod **before** shipping, not facts. (β — orphaned-R2 leak — is a correctness fix and stands independently.)

author: krinart
body:
## 📝 Summary

##  CDC replication metrics in `MetricsResponse`

Spidapter now scrapes the Prometheus endpoint on the running spiced instance at the end of each metrics poll and populates the new `cdc_replication` field with per-table CDC metrics: 
* source receive wait time
* apply burst duration and count
* linger wait
* rows applied
* and bytes applied. 

This works for both local and SCP runs. 

A new `dataset_acceleration_cdc_apply_burst_rows_total` counter was added to spiced to track the true number of records applied per burst, since the existing envelope count didn't capture the per-row volume.

## Optional `--metrics` port for local spiced

Passing `SPIDAPTER_METRICS_PORT` now wires the `--metrics` flag into the local spiced process, enabling Prometheus scraping in local benchmark runs.

## MongoDB scenario switches to Atlas connect mode

The mongodb-streams built-in scenario now connects to an existing MongoDB Atlas cluster via `MONGODB_ATLAS_URI` instead of provisioning a new EC2 instance. 

## Fix Arrow schema mismatch crashing MongoDB CDC coalescing

  Snapshot batches and live-stream CDC batches were built with different field nullability: for example, `_id` was declared non-null in snapshot data but nullable in CDC event batches. When `RefreshTask` tried to coalesce them, Arrow's `concat_batches` rejected the mismatched struct types and crashed the refresh task. The fix normalizes all change batch schemas (snapshot, live CDC events, and the ready-signal envelope) to all-nullable fields, so every batch that flows through the pipeline carries an identical struct type regardless of its origin.

## PostgreSQL and MongoDB EC2 tuning

* PostgreSQL cloud-init now configures memory-aware settings at instance startup: shared_buffers at 25% of available RAM, work_mem at 256 MB, effective_cache_size at 75% of RAM, and parallel query workers enabled. 
* MongoDB oplog size is increased to 10 GB to prevent oplog rollover stalls during long benchmark runs.

author: zachshallbetter
body:
## Why
An engine enhancement straight from the consumer spec (`FieldUI-Engine-Features.md` §3.1) and a documented failure. `sampleScalar` shipped in #456 as the smooth diffused density readout — but **without a gradient**. Callers finite-differenced it, and sampled too close in, that re-introduces the exact *flattening-at-a-source* the scalar exists to avoid — the failure the Garden notes name three times ("the density gradient flattens to ~0 right at a source … we fell back to explicit seek points"). The spec lists `sampleGradient` as the companion that makes the field "the basis for gradient-driven behavior."

## What
`FieldHandle.sampleGradient(x, y)` → `{ x, y }`: the **direction + steepness (1/px) of increasing density**, computed off the same diffused heatmap grid (`ScalarGridImpl.gradient`, central difference) normalized by the eased peak — so it stays **non-degenerate at a source**. Add it to a heading to climb toward matter; negate it to flee crowding.

- `Heatmap.gradient(x,y)` wraps the existing (tested) grid gradient, peak-normalized; `{0,0}` on an empty field.
- `FieldHandle.sampleGradient` delegates to it; `{ x: 0, y: 0 }` when the heatmap layer is off. Pure, read-only, maintained under `render: 'none'`.
- **Carried to every plane**: vanilla, `<field-root>`/`<field-cell>` (elements, CEM regenerated), three's `FieldLayer`. React/elements get it through the handle automatically.
- api-surface + `docs-api.ts` + engine-reference §22.10 + CHANGELOG updated.

## Verification
New test proves the gradient is **non-degenerate on a source's slope** *and* **points up-density toward it** — the property a nearest-body readout loses. Full gate green: typecheck · build · test · check:api · check:dist · check:readme · check:recipes · check:cem · check:links.

Additive to the unfrozen handle — no frozen symbol touched. **Swift parity** (sampleScalar + sampleGradient) tracked under #423.

- **Card family** (completes the merged Card/CardContent/CardActions): `CardHeader` (avatar + title/subheader + action slots), `CardMedia` (native `<image>`), `CardActionArea` (pressable wrapper).
- **Navigation**: `Tab`, `Tabs` (clones children to inject `selected`/`onClick`), `Breadcrumbs` (Link items + separators).
- **Selection controls**: `Checkbox`, `Radio` (shared `SwitchBase` + real `@mui/icons-material` paths via `createSvgIcon`), `Switch` (absolute track + thumb), `FormControlLabel` (control + Typography label, `labelPlacement`). Adds a `useControlled` hook and 4 icon paths.

## Review fixes applied on top of the patches (high-entropy)

1. **Tab label didn't inherit font/color.** A Lynx `<text>` does **not** inherit `fontSize`/`fontWeight`/`color` from a `<view>` ancestor, so `{ color: 'inherit', fontSize: 'inherit' }` rendered default text. Rewrote the label to carry resolved values itself (mirrors `Button`) and uppercase it (MUI `Tab` inherits `typography.button`'s `textTransform: uppercase`):
   ```ts
   tabLabelStyle(os, theme) -> { fontSize: button.fontSize, fontWeight, lineHeight: 1.25,
                                 letterSpacing, color: resolveTabTextColor(os, theme) }
   ```
2. **CardMedia used `display: 'block'`** → Lynx has no `block` value; switched to `display: 'flex'` (image fills the box).
3. **Switch thumb / SwitchBase hit-area used `borderRadius: '50%'`** → repo avoids `%` radii (Chip `'16px'`, Badge `${radius}px`); converted to px (`thumb/2`, `HIT_PADDING + icon/2`).

- **Tabs indicator** is a 2px bar inside each *selected* `Tab`, not a single sliding element (Lynx can't measure layout).
- **Breadcrumbs** collapse (`maxItems` "…") not implemented; prop kept for API compat.
- **onChange** reports the next checked value (no DOM event in Lynx).

body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** A ground-up redesign of the gateway `web/` console into a coherent "Operator Console" design system, because the prior UI was a thin shell over the config API with navigation dead-ends and no visual language.
  - **Design system + shell:** new token set + UI primitives (`Card`/`Button`/`Badge`/`PageHeader`/`StatCard`/`ConfirmDialog`/`ComboBox`), slim icon rail + mobile drawer, ⌘K command palette.
  - **Config (the bulk):** schema-driven master-detail navigator (searchable section→entity tree, `+Add` for empty/previously-unreachable sections), inline validation, reference/alias pickers, humanized labels — all preserving the existing schema-driven JSON-Patch / drift / `?tab=` contract (#6175), no hardcoded section/field names.
  - **Dashboard / Chat / Tools / Integrations / Cron / Doctor / Pairing:** real-metric dashboard with list+drawer; multi-agent chat workspace (tabs + split, panes stay WS-connected) with per-agent model switch; Tools page with a per-risk-profile allow/block matrix; Integrations as a launcher into config; Doctor fix-in-place modal + deep-links; pairing list with unpaired-vs-zero distinction.
  - **Four upstream fixes ported** onto the redesign (see *Incorporated contributions*).
  - **i18n / a11y / perf:** all user-facing strings routed through `t()` (+531 en keys); focus traps, keyboard nav, 44px targets, `ConfirmDialog` replacing native `confirm/prompt`; polling pauses on hidden tab; `apiFetch` coalesces concurrent identical GETs.
- **Scope boundary:** **Pure web — zero `crates/` changes.** No gateway/runtime/channel/provider/tool/schema changes. The daemon API contract is consumed as-is.
- **Blast radius:** the gateway web dashboard only. No change to the WS/HTTP protocol, endpoints, or config schema.
- **Linked issue(s):**
  - `Fixes #7157` — chat-bubble server-timestamp leak (fully resolved web-side).
  - `Related #6891` — cron edit 422 is fixed web-side; the issue also asks for more PATCH-editable fields, which needs a `CronPatchBody` (backend) change.
  - `Related #6488` — integration category labels now render human-readably in the UI; the issue's `category_label` API field + Rust test remain a backend item (see PR #6490).
  - `Related #7356` — the cron pause/resume button is built but inert until the gateway accepts `enabled` on `CronPatchBody` (tracked separately on `feat/cron-patch-gateway`).
  - `Related #7139`, `Related #7137` — partially groundworked (en keys present; chat primitives exist), not closed by this PR.
- **Labels:** `type: feature`, `web`, `risk: medium`, `size: XL`.

## Validation Evidence (required)

This is a **pure-web** PR — no Rust changed, so the cargo battery is N/A (intentionally skipped; `git diff --name-only master...HEAD` is 100% under `web/`).

Web battery:
```bash
cd web && npm run build      # tsc -b && vite build
# ✓ built in ~3.7s — 0 type errors (only the pre-existing >500kB chunk-size advisory)
```

- **Commands run and tail output:** `npm run build` clean on every commit; `git diff --name-only master...HEAD | grep -v '^web/'` → empty (pure web).
- **Beyond CI — what did you manually verify?** Two full multi-agent adversarial review passes of the new/changed surface → **0 blockers both passes**. Pass 1: 3 major + 2 minor fixed (ported `#7199` timestamp regex anchored + timezone-independent, model-switch catch identity guard, cron toggle in-flight feedback). Pass 2 caught a further major the first missed — a socket-rebuild stale-ref that could strand the agent page offline on a synchronous `connect()` throw (fixed in switchModel + clearAllMessages). All remaining minors/nits then fixed: origin-based timestamp strip (a `local` flag so typed input isn't clipped while #7157's server prefixes still strip), cron `agent` defensive default, mutually-exclusive `role="alert"` cron banners, watchdog timer hygiene. Every fix re-verified (resolved, no regressions, #7157 intact, tsc clean). Manually exercised against a live daemon (`:42617`): config save/navigate, multi-agent chat + model switch, Integrations routing, cron edit/toggle, Doctor deep-links, pairing. **Not** verified: the legacy Tauri desktop app (out of scope); the dormant `alias-ref` picker (no backend emits it yet — see #7594).
- **Known web-only limit:** the chat timestamp strip uses a client-side `local` flag; with `session_persistence` on, a message that literally begins with a `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS TZ]` token is re-stripped after a server-hydrated reload (the server can't distinguish web-verbatim from gateway-prefixed without a server-side flag). Cosmetic + rare; a complete fix needs a backend marker.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** cargo fmt/clippy/test — no Rust in the diff.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — consumes the existing daemon API; type additions (`alias_source?`, `category_label` doc) are additive/optional.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.**
- Upgrade steps: none. Drop-in replacement of the `web/` bundle.

## Rollback (required for `risk: medium`)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the merge, or redeploy the prior `web/` bundle — no server/state migration involved.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** web dashboard fails to load / blank route / console errors; daemon and all non-web surfaces are unaffected (pure web).

## Incorporated contributions

Four upstream fixes were ported onto the redesign. Human `Co-authored-by` trailers are on the relevant commits.

- **#7199** (@xianshishan) — strip leaked server-timestamp from chat bubbles. Co-authored; our port additionally fixes the upstream regex (anchored) and timezone gating.
- **#7191** (@NiuBlibing) — agent-scoped status + per-phase model-switch watchdog. Co-authored; adapted to our provider-ref resolution.

author: neo-opus-vega
body:
## Summary

Slice 2 of #13247 — wires the **interactive resize commit loop** into the standalone `examples/dashboard/dock/` example, atop Slice 1 (static render, #13255). Dragging a splitter now commits a `resizeSplit` through `DockZoneModel` and the layout re-projects from the new committed document — the first **runtime** exercise of the full model → operation → re-projection cycle in a standalone app.

`MainContainer` owns the committed dock-zone document (`this.dockModel`) as the single source of truth and drives `DockSplitter`'s two callbacks as a clean **reducer / view-sync split**:
- `applyDockZoneOperation` — the **reducer**: a pure `DockZoneModel.applyOperation` over the current document.
- `onDockZoneDocumentChange` — the **view-sync**: stores the committed document and re-projects, **deferred one tick**.

`items` is built in `construct()` (not static config) so each projection can carry the instance-bound callbacks. The deferral is load-bearing: the notify fires synchronously from the committing splitter's `onDragEnd`, so an immediate `removeAll()` would destroy that splitter mid-handler (a use-after-destroy on the rest of `onDragEnd`); `me.timeout(0)` + an `isDestroyed` guard push the re-projection past `onDragEnd`.

**NL support (operator-directed):** `neo-config.json` gains `useAiClient: true`, so the App-Worker AI Client (`src/ai/Client.mjs`) boots and an agent can connect via the Neural Link bridge to inspect + drive the live dock layout (`set_instance_properties` / `call_method` on the splitters / `undo`). The example becomes a real dogfooding + verification surface for the resize loop.

No `src/dashboard/` behavior change — this wires the already-shipped capability (#13225 drag-wiring, #13160 `resizeSplit` op).

Resolves #13278

Refs #13247 (parent), #13253 (Slice 1), #13255 (Slice 1 PR), #13225 / #13160 (capability — merged), #13158 (QT-parity docking-polish epic — its "interactive splitter resize" gap is delivered by #13225 / #13160; scope refresh confirmed by @neo-claude-opus)

Evidence: L2 (70 dashboard unit tests green incl. 2 new `DockSplitter` reducer + notify tests and the resize round-trip; example render browser-verified via the dev-server preview, console clean) → L2 required (#13278 ACs are the wiring + the owning-reducer pattern + the previously-uncovered callback paths + a visual render; an NL-driven end-to-end drag is broader than this slice's ACs — it is the post-merge validation the new `useAiClient` flag enables).

## Test Evidence

`UNIT_TEST_MODE=true playwright -c …unit.mjs test/playwright/unit/dashboard/` at head `513bf0d84` — **70 green**:

- **`DockSplitter.spec.mjs` (2 new)** — covers the two callbacks the example relies on, previously untested (only the local-document path was):
  - the owning `applyDockZoneOperation` **reducer** path is preferred over the local-document fallback (no `dockZoneDocument` supplied); the descriptor reaches the reducer with the splitter instance, and the reducer's returned document is adopted as the splitter's doc + threaded to the notify;
  - `onDockZoneDocumentChange` fires once on a successful commit with the committed document; it does **not** fire (and the local doc is left untouched) when the reducer rejects the resize.
- **Regression** — the existing `DockSplitter` (local-document path + size-vector rejection), `DockLayoutAdapter`, and `DockZoneModel` suites stay green.

**Render verified in-browser** (dev-server preview at `examples/dashboard/dock/`): the `construct()`-built projection mounts the full tree — 2 splits (root horizontal + side vertical), 2 splitter affordances, 3 tab zones, 4 panels (Strategy / Swarm / Terminal / Logs) — at the model's proportions (measured child widths 314 : 6 : 169 ≈ 0.65 : 0.35; side-split 0.6 : 0.4). **Console clean**, including with `useAiClient: true` enabled (the AI Client boots without a bridge present and does not error).

`node --check` clean on the edited `.mjs`.

## Post-Merge Validation

- Run the example, connect the Neural Link bridge, and drive a `resizeSplit` (e.g. `call_method` on a splitter, or mutate the model) → the layout re-projects with the new sizes; `undo` reverts it. This is the NL-driven end-to-end path the `useAiClient` one-liner enables.
- Manually drag a splitter in a browser → the adjacent zones resize and persist through the committed model.

## Deltas

- **NL support is operator-directed** (mid-flight) — `useAiClient: true` makes the example Neural-Link-drivable, which is both the dogfooding payoff and the end-to-end verification path that headless synthetic events can't reach. Verified the example still renders cleanly (no console errors) with the AI Client booting absent a bridge.
- **Synthetic pointer-drag does not drive Neo's `DockSplitter`** in the headless preview: it listens to Neo's synthesized `drag:start`/`drag:end`, which the main-thread DragZone produces from **trusted** pointer events — `isTrusted: false` synthetic events don't engage it. So the end-to-end drag is unit-covered (the loop callbacks) + compositionally sound (the deferred re-projection re-uses the same `project()` + `add()` path the verified `construct()` render uses), and NL-drivable post-merge — not preview-scripted.
- **Advanced QT-parity demos** (auto-hide/pin, perspectives, grouped tab-drag) are #13158's *capability* layer, not yet built in `src/dashboard/` — out of scope here; the example grows to demonstrate them as those land (coordinated with @neo-claude-opus; Slice 3 = the auto-hide demo, teed up once the #13256 model seam gets its UI).

body:
## Batch 2 — single task-weight ladder (instruction files)

**Stacked on #71's successor — base is the Batch 1 branch `coding-team-weight-asymmetry-fastlane` (PR #73), so this diff is only the 18 instruction files.** Merge #73 first, then this.

Fixes coding-team's process-weight asymmetry: every task used to pay maximum pipeline ceremony regardless of size. This introduces ONE quantified tier ladder and routes every gate through it, so trivial work pays trivial ceremony while risky/large work keeps full review.

### What changed
- **`phases/task-weight.md`** (new, 97 lines) — the single source of truth: a size-tier table (Trivial/Small/Medium/Large), a **7-class semantic risk superset** (security/trust-boundary, payment/billing, data-deletion, public-contract, schema, dependency, instruction-file — judged by *effect*, filenames are hints; risk forces Medium minimum), one **GATE MATRIX**, and a single end-of-execution **effective-tier recompute** (`max(planned, actual-diff)`, ratchets up only).
- **Tasks 9–20** convert every pipeline gate (`SKILL.md`, `phases/*.md`) to *reference* that matrix instead of inventing its own fast lane. The legacy `1 task AND ≤3 files` QA-skip (the Small boundary) is replaced everywhere by the ladder's Trivial test so Small changes no longer skip QA.
- Self-application note: coding-team *is* instruction files, so the instruction-file risk class makes every coding-team-on-itself task Medium+ — the fast lane is only for benign source/test/doc changes in target repos.

### Verification
- **Mechanical gate**: ladder table appears only in `task-weight.md` (DRY); no unscoped "skip because simple" bypass; no `1 task AND ≤3 files` surviving as a skip test; deploy clean.
- **Opus prompt-craft audit**: gate-matrix conformance, single recompute positioned before QA, equal-force skip/run framing, no multi-edit contradictions — all pass.
- **Codex `/second-opinion review`**: caught a temporal ordering bug the same-model audit missed — the per-task verification gate referenced an effective tier computed later in the sequence. Fixed in `bf301da` (per-task verification now gates on the planned tier; growth is covered at exit by the unconditional full-suite run + the effective-tier QA reviewer). Doc-drift's tier gate was also separated from its orthogonal no-impact early-exits.

author: cast0rp0lux
body:
## Diagnóstico

Generaciones de 8 min (Jazz-Funk 70s: 500s). El cuello es `_try_year_from_lastfm`: no consultaba `_track_year_cache` ni la capa MongoDB antes de ir a la red — aunque ambas ya existen y `_try_year_from_discogs` sí las usa.

Por cada artista hace hasta 5× llamadas LFM (top-5 tracks en EraPref en secuencial dentro del hilo), y esas mismas consultas se repiten en las 3 fases (pesca → coherencia → replenish). Artistas como Crispy & Co./Isis/Kevin Toney aparecían consultados 2-3 veces en logs.

## Cambio único — cache-aside en `_try_year_from_lastfm`

Mismo patrón que `_get_track_year_from_musicbrainz` (línea ~5185):

```python
cache_key = (normalize(artist), normalize(track))

# 1. In-memory
if cache_key in _track_year_cache:
    return _track_year_cache[cache_key]

# 2. MongoDB L2
cached = _mb_year_cache_get(artist, track)
if cached != "MISS":
    _track_year_cache[cache_key] = cached
    return cached

# 3. Live LFM (lógica intacta)
year = None
# ... extracción track.getInfo → album.getinfo → regex ...

# 4. Write to both layers (including None)
_track_year_cache[cache_key] = year
if year is not None:
    _mb_year_cache_set(artist, track, year, source="lastfm")
else:
    _mb_year_cache_set(artist, track, None, source="lastfm-miss")  # negative cache
```

**Negative caching de `None`**: un artista sin año resoluble no vuelve a la red. Mismo comportamiento que el resto de la función `_resolve_track_year`.

**Thread safety**: escrituras `dict[key] = value` son atómicas en CPython (GIL). Last-write-wins con el mismo valor es inocuo — no se añade lock.

## Lo que no cambia

Lógica de extracción de año, EraPref y su cascada, `_try_year_from_discogs`, `_check_era_coherence`, `_erapref_rescued`, multiplicador de pesca (`target*6`), paralelización, engine, `engine_canonical.py`. Cero cambio de calidad.

author: jdwillmsen
body:
## What

Stores the sensitive `talops` artifacts — `terraform.tfvars`, the Talos secrets bundle, `talosconfig`, and bootstrap state — as **SOPS+age encrypted `*.enc.yaml` files committed to git**. This makes the secrets shared across machines, backed up off-box, and revocable per device, without ever committing plaintext.

Motivation: the secrets previously lived only on whichever laptop ran `talops` (plaintext, gitignored, no backup, no sharing) — a blocker for working across multiple devices.

## How it works

- **Encryption:** SOPS with age recipients; private keys never leave each device, only public keys live in `.sops.yaml`.
- **Hydrate/seal:** plaintext working copies stay in their normal gitignored locations (debuggable). `talops` auto-decrypts them before a command and auto-encrypts changes after a successful mutating command. Change-detected to keep git clean.
- **Vault = source of truth; plaintext = regenerable local cache.**

## Commands

`talops secrets {status,hydrate,seal,lock,edit,add-device}`

Onboarding a device: `talops secrets add-device <pubkey>` → commit + push → `git pull` on the new device.

## Safety / correctness

- **Repo-root anchoring** — the vault always resolves to `<repo>/clusters/<name>/vault` regardless of invocation directory (no split vault).
- **Cluster name resolved from tfvars before hydrate** — hydrate and seal always agree on the cluster dir.
- **Stale-vault guard** — refuses to operate when the local branch is behind upstream (`--allow-stale-vault` / `--fetch` to override/refresh).
- **`reset`** preserves the vault unless `--purge-vault`.
- Toggles: `TALOPS_NO_AUTOSEAL`, `TALOPS_AUTOLOCK`. Falls back to legacy plaintext mode if `sops` is absent.

## Trade-offs (documented in `docs/secrets.md`)

- Encrypted secrets persist in git history (inherent to SOPS-in-git); rotation limits forward blast radius.
- Plaintext sits on disk between runs by design (debuggability); `TALOPS_AUTOLOCK` opts into wiping it.

## Tests

New `internal/secrets` unit tests (seal/hydrate round-trip, idempotent seal, lock, add-device/bootstrap, git-state, repo-root) plus end-to-end binary verification. `gofmt`/`vet` clean.

Requires `sops` and `age` on operator machines (prereq check warns if missing).

## Summary

- **`src/lib/graphql/api.ts`**: Added `GraphQLResponse<T>` type alias; `response.json()` is now cast to `GraphQLResponse<T>` instead of being implicit `any`. The now-redundant `as T` cast on the return value was removed.
- **`src/lib/api/historicalWeather.ts`**: Added `OpenMeteoArchiveResponse` type alias matching the Open-Meteo archive API shape; `response.json()` is cast to it so all subsequent property accesses are fully typed.
- **`src/routes/api/subscribe/+server.ts`**: `res.json()` annotated as `{ message?: string }` to match the upstream service's expected response shape.
- **`src/routes/+layout.svelte`**: `res.json()` annotated as `{ message: string }` — our own `/api/subscribe` endpoint always returns this shape.
- **`src/lib/components/AddComment.svelte`**: `res.json()` annotated as `{ success?: boolean; message?: string }` matching the `/api/comment` response contract.
- **`src/lib/components/ShareButton.svelte`**: All five event handler functions (`copyLink`, `shareOnBluesky`, `shareOnThreads`, `shareOnFacebook`, `shareOnWhatsApp`) given explicit `: void` return type annotations.

## Why

`Response.prototype.json()` returns `Promise<any>` in TypeScript's DOM types regardless of compiler strictness. Without an explicit cast the result variable is silently `any`, suppressing all type checks on every property access that follows. This PR replaces each implicit `any` with the narrowest accurate type, keeping the type-safety guarantees that `strict: true` provides everywhere else in the codebase.

author: robotsix-mill[bot]
body:
## Problem

The data-dir audit flagged `expert_python-backend_memory.md` for unbounded growth (+2.1 KiB, +203.5%).  The root cause is a **trim-on-read, no-trim-on-write** asymmetry in the memory ledger persistence path:

1. `load_memory()` (`pass_runner.py:304`) applies `tail_keep` with a `max_memory_chars` cap (default 8000) when **reading** — the agent sees only the most recent ~8000 chars.
2. `persist_memory()` (`pass_runner.py:331`) writes the agent's **full** `updated_memory` string **without any size cap**.
3. The expert agent is instructed to return "the FULL revised memory ledger" — it typically echoes the loaded content back verbatim plus new observations.  Since the loaded content was trimmed to 8000 chars, the written content hovers around that size but slowly creeps upward as the model adds more than it drops.
4. Over successive consultations, the file on disk grows beyond the cap, even though only the tail is ever loaded.

The asymmetry was documented in `_settings_core.py:276`: *"read-side only — persist_memory is unchanged"*.  This ticket fixes that gap.

## Scope

Two source files + tests:

1. **`src/robotsix_mill/runners/pass_runner.py`** — `persist_memory()` (L331–345)
   - Add `max_chars: int | None = None` parameter (default `None` = backward-compatible, no trimming).
   - When `max_chars` is set and `len(text) > max_chars`, call `tail_keep(text, max_chars, label="memory")` **after** `strip_ephemeral_sections()` and **before** `write_text()`.
   - Log a warning (same pattern as `load_memory`: `"memory file %s truncated: %d → %d chars"`).
   - `tail_keep` is already imported at L28 — no new imports needed.

2. **`src/robotsix_mill/agents/consult_expert.py`** — `run_consult_expert()` (L177)
   - Pass `max_chars=definition.memory.max_memory_chars` to the `persist_memory()` call, mirroring the same value already passed to `load_memory()` at L105.

3. **`src/robotsix_mill/config/_settings_core.py`** — L276 comment
   - Update the stale comment: *"read-side only — persist_memory is unchanged"* → *"oldest entries dropped from the loaded view; persist_memory also applies the cap on write when max_chars is passed"* (or similar concise update).

4. **Tests**
   - `tests/runners/test_pass_runner.py`: new tests for `persist_memory` with `max_chars`:
     - `test_persist_memory_trims_when_over_max_chars` — writes oversized text, verifies output ≤ `max_chars` + note overhead, truncation note present, newest entries preserved.
     - `test_persist_memory_noop_when_under_max_chars` — text under the limit is written unchanged.
     - `test_persist_memory_max_chars_none_backward_compat` — `max_chars=None` (default) writes full text without trimming.
   - `tests/agents/test_consult_expert.py`: update `test_expert_persists_updated_memory` to verify `persist_memory` is called with the `max_chars` kwarg (or add a separate assertion).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **`persist_memory` accepts `max_chars`**: calling `persist_memory(path, text, max_chars=8000)` with text > 8000 chars writes a file ≤ ~8100 chars (8000 + truncation-note overhead), with newest lines preserved and a `[... memory truncated: ...]` note prepended.
2. **Backward compatible**: existing callers that do not pass `max_chars` behave identically to before — full text written, no truncation.
3. **Expert memory is capped on write**: after a `run_consult_expert()` call where the model returns `updated_memory` > `definition.memory.max_memory_chars`, the persisted file is trimmed to that cap.
4. **Warning logged**: truncation on write emits a WARNING log entry (same pattern as `load_memory` truncation).
5. **Existing tests pass**: `pytest tests/runners/test_pass_runner.py tests/agents/test_consult_expert.py` — all existing tests continue to pass without modification (the new `max_chars` parameter defaults to `None`).
6. **Stale comment fixed**: `_settings_core.py:276` no longer claims `persist_memory is unchanged`.

## Out of scope / constraints

- **Other `persist_memory` callers** (`documenting.py`, `ci_fix.py`, `merge.py`, `meta/runner.py`, `cost_analyst_runner.py`, `refine/orchestration.py`, `implement/implementation_logic.py`, `run_health_runner.py`) — these have the same pattern but are deliberately not changed here.  Each can adopt `max_chars` in follow-up work.
- **`web_knowledge.py` `append_general_memory()`** — a different write path (append-only, no ledger replacement); out of scope.
- **Rotation / archiving** — `tail_keep`-based trimming is sufficient; no file rotation or backup mechanism is needed.
- **No change to the expert agent's system prompt** — the prompt still asks for the full revised ledger; the write-side cap handles the overflow mechanically.

## Problem
The feature-029 import-notifications **bell was reported as "not visible."** Root cause is placement, not rendering:

- `base.html` placed `{% include notifications_popover %}` in the **left** navbar cluster — right after the dropzone, before the search form.
- `.nav-logout` carried `margin-left:auto`, so *logout* floated right while the bell stayed crowded next to the dropzone/search.

author: xiangguangyxg
body:
## Why I'm doing:

Tablet pre-split can compute split boundaries cheaply from Parquet/ORC footer min/max stats (the "meta tier") instead of running a data-tier SELECT sample. After #74739, a DECIMAL sort key already pre-splits, but only via the **data tier** — the two footer readers rejected DECIMAL stats, so every decimal bulk load paid the data-tier sub-query. This closes that gap so a DECIMAL sort key pre-splits via the cheap meta tier, mirroring the DATE/DATETIME work in #74710.

## What I'm doing:

Teach the two meta-tier footer readers to decode DECIMAL min/max stats. The pipeline below the readers is type-agnostic and untouched; `DecimalVariant` / `Variant.of(decimalType, …)` already exist (#74739) and are unchanged. BE is unchanged.

- **`ParquetRowGroupStatisticsReader`**: accept `DecimalLogicalTypeAnnotation` only for INT32/INT64-backed decimals (the unscaled integer's signed order equals the decimal order) with an **exact precision/scale match** against the StarRocks column; decode via `BigDecimal.valueOf(unscaled, scale).toPlainString()` → `Variant.of`. FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY/BINARY-backed decimals are rejected → data tier, because parquet-mr footer min/max for byte-array decimals may use unsigned byte ordering (wrong for negatives) unless the writer set a typed sort order this reader does not inspect.
- **`OrcStripeStatisticsReader`**: accept ORC `DECIMAL` with an exact precision/scale match; `convertDecimalStripe` mirrors `convertDateStripe` (`HiveDecimal.bigDecimalValue().toPlainString()` → `Variant.of`, absent stats when `getNumberOfValues() == 0`, decode failures wrapped as `MetaTierUnavailableException` → data-tier fallback). ORC decimal stats are correctly ordered, so no byte-order gate is needed.

Anything outside this window (non-matching precision/scale, byte-array-backed Parquet decimals) falls back to the data tier — never a load failure. BE is unchanged: `datum_from_string` parses all decimal types and `tablet_splitter` requires an exact precision/scale match (else identical-fallback).

Tests: 8 Parquet + 7 ORC decimal cases (positive/negative signed ordering, INT32/INT64/DECIMAL128, scale/precision/non-decimal mismatch rejections, FIXED_LEN/BINARY rejection, all-null absent stats).

author: zackees
body:
## Summary

Closes #115.

Adds a second pitch source to the strip-drag magnetic snap. Where #110 used each neighbor strip's *internal* LED-to-LED spacing (sub-cm pitch, useful for LED-grid alignment), this PR additionally infers the **inter-strip grid pitch** from the spacing between strip centroids themselves, exposing snap targets at every implicit grid column / row — including the ones where no actual strip sits (e.g. the blue-oval gap in the issue screenshot).

## Algorithm

For each axis (X, Y):

1. Gather every other strip's centroid.
2. **Perpendicular band filter** (when ``draggedCenter`` is supplied): drop neighbors whose perpendicular coord sits outside the "near" cluster — defined as the first jump in sorted perpendicular distances. Isolates the row/column the dragged strip belongs to.
3. Sort the kept centers on this axis, take consecutive differences.
4. **Pitch** = true median of the diffs (mean-of-two-middle for even count). Variance guard: skip when ``max(diff) > 3 · median``.
5. For each ORIGINAL neighbor center, emit ``cx ± k · pitch`` (or ``cy ± k · pitch``) for k ∈ {1..5}.

## Tests (TDD Red → Green)

4 new tests in ``tests/unit/strip-snap-targets.test.ts`` under ``describe('inter-strip grid pitch (issue #115)')``. Confirmed RED before implementation, GREEN after:

- **Red 1**: 4-panel row at cx={0,10,20,30} ⇒ target at x=40 and x=-10.
- **Red 2**: 5-panel row at cx={0,10,20,30,40} ⇒ targets at x=50, 60, -10, -20.
- **Red 3**: 3 strips at cx={0,10,25} with diffs [10,15] ⇒ true median 12.5; target at 37.5 or -12.5 (NOT the lower-median 10).
- **Red 4**: A=(0,0), B=(20,0), C=(10,100); dragging near y=0 ⇒ band filter excludes C ⇒ X-pitch = 20, target at x=40 (not the buggy pitch=10 ⇒ x=30 a naive impl would produce).

All 7 existing #110 tests pass unmodified.

## Test plan

- [x] ``npm test`` — 410/410 pass (7 + 4 in ``strip-snap-targets.test.ts``).
- [x] ``npm run typecheck`` — clean.
- [x] ``npm run lint`` — clean.
- [x] ``npm run build`` — succeeds.
- [ ] Visual: load a quad-grid screenmap (the one in #115's screenshot), drag a panel, confirm vertical snap guides appear at EVERY inter-panel column gap, including the blue-oval position two columns away from any existing strip center.
