author: guzmanr1988
body:
## Summary
- Live project-items-card-grid `sectionTotalCents` was reading `selectionQuantities[optId] ?? 1` for every option, silently undercounting linear_ft addons (gutters/fascia/soffit) and area materials (metal/shingle/tile/aluminum/flat_roof) on the vendor project-details dialog (`lead-workflow.tsx:1726` + `lead-inbox.tsx:489`). Donald project (10990 SW 225 Terrace, vendor 3e0821aa) displayed Add-Ons $24 and Materials $1,390 against a $33,082+ correct total.
- Snapshot writer (`buildRoofingBaseLines`, frozen at sendProject) was already correct — `priceLineItems` on Donald show the right $27,800 materials / $3,948 gutters figures. Bug was live-renderer-only; NO re-billing.
- Fix: extract qty-resolution into shared `resolveOptionQty` helper. Both `sectionTotalCents` and the writer's `linear_ft` branch route through it, so live display reconciles in lockstep to billed snapshot.

## Governing rule
kratos 2026-06-15: **live RATES × frozen-MEASURED quantities**. RATE is read from the live vendor catalog (outside the resolver). QUANTITY is a physical property of THIS roof, measured once at sale; the resolver returns the SAME qty the writer used at snapshot time. The resolver IS the writer's qty logic extracted — any fallback the writer doesn't have, the resolver doesn't have either.

Resolver branches by resolved `meta.priceUnit` (catalog-overlay-aware via `getOptionMetadata`):
- `linear_ft` → `roofAddonLinearFt ?? addonLinearFt ?? subGroupLinearFt`; gutters route through `computeGutterTotalLinFt` to add drops × per-floor.
- `square` → `sqftToSquares(round(pitched|flat|areaSqft × waste))`. Configurator's `*Selection.roofSize` is intentionally NOT a source (writer doesn't use it; using it would re-introduce snapshot-vs-live drift).
- `sqft` → `customSizeSqft[optId] ?? areaSqft ?? 0`.
- `default` → `selectionQuantities[optId] ?? 1` (unchanged for flat-priced WD selections).

## Donald post-fix targets (verified in tests)
- **Add-Ons:** $6,696 (gutters $3,948 + fascia_wood $2,748)
- **Materials:** $27,800 (metal $1,390 × 20 squares — `resolver-qty === writer-unitQuantity` lockstep assertion)
- **Patch delta on Donald display:** $33,082 (the hole the qty=1 fallback hid)
- **Frozen sale $33,248 invariant unchanged** (priceLineItems untouched)

## Test plan
`npm run sectiontotal-qty-resolver` (15 legs, 4 assertion clusters):

- [x] **Test 1** — `fascia_wood` lin_ft no drops → qty=229, $2,748
- [x] **Test 2** — `gutters` lin_ft WITH drops → qty=329 (via `computeGutterTotalLinFt`), $3,948. Half-fix detector: $2,748 (qty=229, drops bypassed) FAILS.
- [x] **Test 3** — `metal` area material → qty=20, $27,800. Includes:
  - resolver-qty === writer-unitQuantity lockstep
  - no-roofMeasurement edge → qty=0 (NOT configurator-21)
- [x] **Test 4** — buggy-baseline regression doc: OLD qty=1 fallback produces visible $24 / $1,390; NEW resolver closes both
- [x] **Existing `npm run per-unit-math`** still green (8 legs)
- [x] **`npx tsc -b`** clean

## Review focus
- `src/lib/resolve-option-qty.ts` — the new shared helper. Doc header carves out the governing rule.
- `src/components/shared/project-items-card-grid.tsx:104` — single-line fix at the bug site (qty source now resolver, not `selectionQuantities ?? 1`).
- `src/lib/roofing-base-lines.ts:154-157` — writer's linear_ft branch now uses the same resolver (lockstep enforced at write time too).
- `tests/sectiontotal-qty-resolver/runner.mts` — `$3,948` gutter assertion (Test 2b) specifically — this is the half-fix detector.

## Deploy
HELD for kratos explicit go (nighttime-mode gate). Promote method matches pin-31 precedent: manual wrangler from merged HEAD after kratos's call.

## Blast radius
2 sold+active sent_projects rows affected (both duplicates of the Donald project — 86227178 + d11d1c01 at 10990 SW 225 Terrace; 1 unique quote). Every future sold/active roofing quote rendered via vendor `lead-workflow` / `lead-inbox` `showPricing=true` dialog also fixed.

body:
### What does this complete?
This brings the `capability` module into kwokka-io, the second io leaf after `addr` and the last unit before the io core SCC. `CapabilityMatrix` is the snapshot of backend features detected at startup, one flag per io_uring capability, cached for the process lifetime and read through the future `IoDriver::capabilities()`. `KernelVersion` is the version triple that gates which features turn on, with a `ZERO` constant for the thin-fallback backends. The matrix provides a conservative `thin_fallback` default and a `full` constructor for tests. The crate root re-exports both public types. There is no unsafe and no new dependency, so the cargo-machete ignore list is unchanged.

### How is it proven?
`cargo test` passes 9 capability unit tests covering kernel version ordering, the `at_least` gate, and the thin-fallback and full field defaults, 26 across kwokka-io in total. `clippy` runs clean under `-D warnings`, nightly `fmt` is clean, and `rustdoc` builds under `-D warnings`. The io core SCC is parked for its own large PR.

Closes #50

## What
The week views forced a hard per-column minimum (140px time-grid / 150px compact) + a 200px employee rail, so 7 columns needed ~1220–1250px. On a narrower content area the last day spilled off the right edge — picking the 13th–19th showed 13–18 and only a sliver of the 19th, requiring sideways scroll.

## Fix
Day columns now flex to fill the available width (`minmax(0, 1fr)`) with a ~100px-per-column `minWidth` floor, so a normal 7-day week always fits on screen and columns just widen on bigger displays. Horizontal scroll still kicks in gracefully for very wide custom ranges or small viewports.

author: rileyjmurray
body:
This branch substantially cuts the wall-clock **time-to-green** of a CI run (40+ minutes on the slowest leg today) through a sequence of independent changes to the reusable test workflow and packaging. The net effect is that CI now takes less than 20 minutes. Once merged, this PR will resolve #606.

The error-generator unit tests that dominated the Python-3.12 job (`test_errgenproptools.py::…::{test_errorgen_composition, test_iterative_error_generator_composition}`, ~920 s combined and pinned to one `xdist` worker by `--dist loadscope`) are slow because **coverage.py's legacy C trace function is de-optimized by Python 3.12's specializing adaptive interpreter** (PEP 659). Switching coverage to its `sys.monitoring` core (PEP 669) restores near-native speed: the same two tests drop from ~595 s / ~325 s to a few seconds each.

The only remotely controversial change in this PR is dropping support for Python 3.9. That version reached end-of-life in October 2025 according to the Python Software Foundation. Dropping support for it here shaves almost 10 minutes off build time (one of our dependencies, `stim`, has no Python 3.9 wheels and so has an expensive build-from-source). We could add Python 3.9 back if we pinned the `stim` version in the 3.9 build to something that has a wheel.

## Changes

### 1. Faster installs (foundation)
- Move the install path to **`uv`** with dependency caching (`actions/cache` over the uv cache), and resolve PyTorch — a transitive test dependency — from the **CPU-only** wheel index (`UV_TORCH_BACKEND=cpu`) instead of pip's default CUDA build, which otherwise drags in ~2.5 GB of unused `nvidia-*` wheels per job.
- `setup.py` build speed-ups, and disable parallel extension builds on Windows (a known MSVC parallel `build_ext` failure mode).

### 2. Coverage via `sys.monitoring` — the dominant latency lever
- Set `COVERAGE_CORE: sysmon` at the workflow level so `--cov` runs use coverage.py's PEP 669 core. On Python 3.12 the legacy C tracer made coverage of call-heavy tests dramatically slower (the errgen composition tests ran ~595 s / ~325 s under coverage vs a few seconds without); `sysmon` removes essentially all of that overhead. It falls back gracefully (with a `CoverageWarning`) on Python < 3.12. Coverage *data* is unchanged.

### 3. Test Python 3.10–3.13 (drop 3.9, add 3.13)
- `requires-python` → `>=3.10`; every workflow matrix moves to `3.10–3.13` (feature branches keep an extremal pair, now `3.10`/`3.13`).
- Dropping 3.9 removes the slowest jobs (3.9 lacked stim/numpy-2 wheels and built more from source). Adding 3.13 brings the test set up to the current Python.

### 4. Measure coverage on a single job
- CI computed `--cov` on **every** matrix job but never uploaded or consumed the result, so it was pure overhead. A new `run-coverage` input (default `'false'`) gates `--cov=pygsti`, and each caller enables it for **exactly one** job — `ubuntu-latest` + Python 3.13 — where `sysmon` keeps the tracer cheap. The steps use `shell: bash` so the conditional flag expands on Windows runners too.

### 5. Drop the redundant explicit `build_ext`
- The Cython install step ran `uv pip install -e .[testing]` **and then** `python setup.py build_ext --inplace`, recompiling all extensions a second time (~40 s/job). The PEP 660 editable install already compiles them in-place via build isolation — verified on a clean checkout: the editable install alone yields importable `.so` for all 19 extensions.

### 6. Consistency
- Build cp310–cp313 wheels (drop cp39, add cp313) so the release matrix matches the supported set, and update the README's stated minimum to "python 3.10 or higher".

## Why the Python version changes compose

`sysmon` alone is necessary but not sufficient: time-to-green was gated by the **3.9** jobs, which paid big overhead due to building `stim` from source.

Once 3.9 is gone, the tests for `beta` and `master` would hit bottlenecks with **3.11**. That version has the specializing interpreter (the performance hit) but no `sys.monitoring` (3.12+ only). 

Assuming we proceed with the 3.9 removal it's natural to bump the highest-tested Python version to 3.13. Our develop tests only run the lowest-version and highest-version supported Python, which become 3.10 and 3.13 after this PR. Strictly speaking, we could run efficient coverage tests with Python 3.12.

## Verification

- All six workflow YAML files parse.
- `COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`: the two errgen tests run in ~24 s combined under the exact CI invocation (vs ~920 s on the legacy tracer); full `test/unit/tools` green.
- **Python 3.13, fresh environment:** the full dependency closure (numpy 2.4, scipy, stim, qiskit, torch, cirq, cvxpy, jupyter, …) installs cleanly; the editable install compiles all 19 Cython extensions in-place; **full `test/unit` = 2335 passed, 0 failed** (one MPI-gated test skips only because that local env was built without MPI; CI has it).
- Coverage gating traced by hand and by an independent review: exactly one coverage job per workflow, always `ubuntu` + `3.13` + cython.

## Notes / follow-ups (not in this PR)

- The cp313 wheel build in `autodeploy.yml` only runs on release, so it is **not exercised by this PR** — first validated at the next release.

author: jason-bohan
body:
## Problem

Surfaced by a live autonomous run: a backend agent configured `model: "auto"` was rail-scored as **`weak`** even though it runs on the loop provider (`openai/gpt-oss-120b:free` = `mid`). It got the *full* weak rail set — over-railed — which defeats the adaptive-tier system for the very common `"auto"` agent config.

Two bugs compounded:
1. **`"auto"` was never resolved** to a concrete model. `getAgentModel` returns the literal `"auto"`; `strengthForModel("auto")` misses the map and falls to `_default` → `weak`.
2. **Suffix mismatch.** Even resolved, the loop model is `openai/gpt-oss-120b:free` but the `agentStrength` key is `openai/gpt-oss-120b` (no `:free`) → exact lookup still misses → `weak`.

## Fix (`railFlags.ts`)

- **`resolveModelId(model, configPath)`** — `'auto'`/`'default'`/`''` resolve to `scheduler.loopProvider.model`; a concrete id passes through unchanged.
- **`strengthForModel`** — exact match first, then tolerate a trailing provider variant suffix (`:free`, `:beta`, …) so `…120b:free` matches the `…120b` key.
- **`resolveBaseStrength`** runs both, so strength scoring *and* Phase-3 learning key on the real model, not `"auto"`.
- **`scheduler.ts`** stores the resolved model on the desk, so the "Rails configured" log and `recordRunOutcome()` no longer key on `"auto"`.

Net: an `auto` agent on gpt-oss now correctly scores `mid` → mid rail set (drops `forwardProgressCoerce`) instead of the full weak set.

## Tests

5 new tests in `railFlags.test.ts`: `resolveModelId` variants (auto/default/empty/concrete/no-loopProvider), suffix tolerance, and the end-to-end `resolveBaseStrength('auto') → 'mid'` case. **All 25 railFlags tests pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean.**

> Takes effect on the next server restart. The in-flight UNW-139 run is intentionally left on the old weak resolution so it can reach its PR uninterrupted.

author: demongiggle
body:
This repository already supports binding host paths into a `mirage run` sandbox. The CLI exposes `--ro-bind` and `--rw-bind`, presets support `roBind` and `rwBind`, and the runner applies bind mounts with explicit read-only remounting plus target safety checks. The gap was discoverability: the operator-facing `mirage run --help` text and the main usage guide did not make that existing support obvious enough when someone went looking for a host-folder mount feature.

From a user perspective, that ambiguity makes it look like bind mounts may be missing even though the runtime already implements them. That can lead to unnecessary feature requests or duplicate implementation work, and it also makes the expected `host:guest` syntax less clear than it should be.

This PR fixes the documentation gap instead of changing runtime behavior. It adds an explicit bind-mount note and example to `mirage run --help`, adds a CLI test that locks that help text in place, and extends `docs/usage.md` with a concrete `--ro-bind`/`--rw-bind` example plus notes about absolute-path syntax, read-only versus writable behavior, dedicated-rootfs target creation, and the stricter `--rootfs /` target requirements.

Validation for the change was focused on the touched surfaces. I ran `go test ./internal/cli` and `go test ./internal/runner -run 'Test(ParseBindMount|PrepareBindTarget)'`, both of which passed. I also checked the existing repository coverage for bind mounts and confirmed that the current tree already contains CLI wiring, preset support, runner bind-mount handling, and end-to-end tests for read-only and read-write bind exposure. Full `internal/runner` and e2e suites were not used as the primary validation signal here because this environment does not support one of the `unshare --map-auto` based tests and the bind-related e2e path requires capabilities that are not reliably available in this session.

author: rfs2671
body:
## Problem
PR #56's mount pre-warm (`getCameraPermissionsAsync` on mount) was meant to cut first-open latency but **made it worse**: camera open went **10–15s → 20–30s**.

## Why it hurt
`launchCameraAsync` fires an **external system-camera Intent**, not a warmed in-process module — so pre-initializing expo-image-picker's permission subsystem at mount gives **zero benefit** to the launch. On a slow device it **adds mount-time native contention** and can **serialize the shutter behind its own in-flight init**, consistent with the regression.

## Change — surgical revert
Removes **only** the pre-warm `useEffect` ([was daily_jobsite.jsx:136-150](frontend/app/logbooks/daily_jobsite.jsx)). 18 deletions, nothing else touched.

**Kept (as instructed):**
- ref-guard double-tap protection (`capturingRef`) — more reliable than the old `useState` guard.
- `useMemo`'d `buildStyles`.
- **PR #54 freeze fixes untouched**: `setTimeout(0)` yield before `setActivities`, the permission ref cache, and the per-photo encode yield in `handleSave`.

## Scope
This is the **OTA-able** step — should pull latency back toward (or below) the pre-#56 10–15s. The **durable fix is separate and post-go-live**: native rebuild (fixes the binary↔OTA drift) + likely an `expo-camera` migration to eliminate the system-camera Intent cold-start entirely. Your logcat will confirm whether the residual cost is the Intent launch (→ expo-camera) vs our code (→ tuning).

## Verification
Parses clean (Babel + `babel-preset-expo`); diff reviewed — only the pre-warm block removed.

- **`lib/render/measure-scene.ts`** — loads each scene's real DOM in headless Chromium (Playwright) at canvas size with animations pinned to their settled state; captures every element's `getBoundingClientRect` + computed colors + a screenshot. Reuses the SSR gate's exact bundle→eval→render path.
- **`lib/render/render-truth-gates.ts`** — deterministic checks on the measured layout: **overflow** (blocking; content box crosses the canvas edge; zero false positives), **contrast** + **dead-region** (advisory).
- Wired into the build route as **advisory / log-only** — no behavior change yet (Phase 2 makes overflow blocking + adds the self-repair ladder + $10 ceiling).
- **Playwright** devDependency.

## Proof
Run against the real Fuse build that shipped clipped text + invisible logos: the gate flags exactly the defects 18 static gates missed —
```
scene 1 [overflow] p clipped right (ends 2140 on 1920)
scene 2 [overflow] p / "YOUR INSTITUTION" / "Approved · 2 min" / flow-div clipped
scene 4 [overflow] p clipped right; div clipped left+right
```
and leaves clean scenes 0/3 unflagged. The validation also caught (and I fixed) a contrast false-positive on monochrome corner logos before it could block anything.

author: steverobertsuk
body:
# HealthColors v2.1.4

This PR finalizes HealthColors v2.1.4 with a focus on reliability when HP is changed by other scripts, backwards compatibility for integrations, and cleanup of public exports.

## What is fixed

* Fixed missed updates when external scripts (like AlterBars) change linked character HP attributes instead of token bars.
* Added a dedicated `change:attribute` flow to capture real old/new HP values and correctly re-run token visuals.
* Prevented duplicate FX when both `change:attribute` and `change:graphic` fire for the same HP change.
* Fixed TokenMod observer wiring to use the deduplicating token-change handler.
* Fixed a race condition in delayed attribute-to-token propagation logic that could overwrite newer HP values.
* Fixed `add:graphic` event handling and added a safe null guard for delayed token lookup.

## Compatibility improvements

* Restored legacy public API aliases from v1.7.1 while keeping v2 camelCase methods.

HealthColors now exposes both:

* `gmWhisper` and `GMW`

* `update` and `Update`

* `checkInstall` and `CheckInstall`

* `registerEventHandlers` and `RegisterEventHandlers`

* Hardened external previous-value reads to support both object snapshots and `get(...)` style access.

* If the previous HP is missing or invalid, HealthColors still updates:

  * Tint
  * Aura
  * Name visibility
  * Dead marker

  Only delta-based FX and death transition comparisons are skipped.

## Impact

* No user command syntax changes.
* No settings behaviour changes.
* No required changes for PowerCards, AlterBars, or existing scripts calling legacy HealthColors API names.

author: tsavo
body:
## What

Drains the **value-NOT-in-scope** half of the statement-position assert buckets in the rust 1.96.0 coretests lifter. These asserts flow through a runtime continuation with no nameable literal/version, so they are **sound TERMINAL refusals** naming the qualified continue path — the same class as the existing bin-2 "runtime data, not constructed from source literals" terminals. Soundness is **earned by detecting the continuation structurally**, never assigned by position: a statement carrying a constructed literal digs.

## Mechanism

Two qualified continue paths classified (typed `SideEffect` + whitelisted in `refusal_disposition`):

1. **FUTURE CONTINUATION** (+5, `future.rs::test_join`): an `.await` anywhere, or a free-fn `block_on(async {..})`, flows the asserted value from a runtime executor (`let x = join!(..).await; assert_eq!(x, 0)`). `ControlFlowEffect`. Recursing it would **fake-dig** `x == 0` as a literal (proven empirically by instrumentation) — so the refusal is the sound disposition, not the under-claim it looked like.

2. **OPAQUE REFLECTION** (+21, `mem/type_info.rs`): `match Type::of::<T>().kind { TypeKind::X(b) => assert_eq!(b.field, ..) }` reads compile-time reflection over runtime type identity (`TypeId`), not a source-literal construction. New `ReflectionEffect`; `reflection_scrutinee` strips `const{}`/`.kind` and fires only on a `Type::of`/`TypeId::of`/`.info()` scrutinee. Body asserts accounted at the `Match` arm; the panic-locus variant-pin discharge is unchanged (so discharged held).

## Before → after

Hermetic battleaxe CI-host sweep, rust 1.96.0 coretests, `coretests_sweep --rustc-cfg`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| discharged | 5857 | **5857** (UNCHANGED — no fake-dig) |
| refused | 372 | **398** (+26: 21 reflection + 5 control-flow) |
| unclassified | 272 | **256** (−16) |
| SILENT | 0 | **0** |
| unaccounted | −184 | −194 |
| CID | `ee0c6d92…000a50` | **UNCHANGED** |

`type_info` unenumerated 11 → 0.

**The +26-vs-16 gap explained:** 21 reflection refusals = the 11 previously-`unenumerated` body asserts **+ 10** reflection body asserts that were previously **masked in the unaccounted-negative pool** by the panic-locus synthetic-pin overcount. These are now honestly surfaced as refused (the −184→−194 unaccounted shift). The CID confirms no assert site was added/removed/edited and there is no double-count of a real site.

## Which sub-buckets stay honestly unclassified (sized follow-up)

The **value-IN-scope** half is diggable, not refusable — refusing it would be wrong:

- **let-initializer iterator-cursor folds** (`iter/adapters/{skip,enumerate,skip_while,filter}.rs` `*_fold`, 7) are over **literal domains**. The defolder already digs the in-place case but declines on inner-`let` accumulator shadowing, `ys[i-1]` index exprs, `*x` deref in `skip_while`/`filter` closures, `len()-1` acc-init, and pre-consumed receivers. Closing those is the **versioned-cursor → phantom-function-over-version** lift — deliberately NOT rushed here to avoid fake-digging an untracked cursor. They stay unclassified.
- Remaining unlifted-expr (15: `hint.rs` Cell+drop, `ptr.rs` raw-ptr mutation) and the 1 residual `char.rs` size_hint loop (inside an un-inlined nested fn — a call-site-inlining bucket) stay unclassified.

EFFECT-OR-LEAVE held: only a detected runtime continuation is terminalized; pure/literal positions dig or stay unclassified, never fake-dug, never fake-refused.

## Tests

`tests/assertion_lift.rs` +4 adversarial discrimination tests (both directions):
- (refuse) `await_in_block_on_is_terminal_refusal`, `reflection_match_body_is_terminal_refusal` → classify TERMINAL refused.
- (boundary/guardrail) `literal_scrutinee_match_is_not_reflection_refused`, `literal_block_is_not_control_flow_refused` → NOT terminalized; they dig.

Verification: lib 116/0, assertion_lift 219/0, sweep CID conserved + SILENT 0, `check-coretests-invariants.py` exact-matches the pin (unclassified moved +16 toward 0). **DO NOT MERGE.**

author: the-d66
body:
💡 **What:** Modified the `__leapfrog_step` and `sample_theta` functions in `src/algorithms/HMC.py` to optionally accept and reuse the `grad_theta` value from the previous leapfrog step.
🎯 **Why:** In Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), each leapfrog step performs a half-step update for `r` which requires calculating `grad_loss`. The final `grad_loss` computed at the end of step `n` is exactly the same as the initial `grad_loss` needed for step `n+1`. Re-computing it is redundant and halves the performance of the sampling.
📊 **Impact:** Reduces the number of expensive gradient evaluations (`self.model.grad_loss`) during the inner loop from `2 * HMC_L` to `HMC_L + 1` per sample, nearly doubling the execution speed of the parameter sampling phase.
🔬 **Measurement:** Verified by running the HMC training loop `python src/main.py --config best_models/HMC_reg_cos --epochs 2` and observing successful completion while maintaining correct numerical behavior. Also verified no tests were broken.

author: tikazyq
body:
Fixes GitHub OAuth login on production: the callback set the session cookie and the state-clearing cookie in a plain header array, and axum's array `IntoResponseParts` impl uses `HeaderMap::insert` — so the second `Set-Cookie` overwrote `onsager_session`. Login redirected to `/` but every request was unauthenticated (`/me` 401 → bounce to `/login`).

Use `AppendHeaders` so both `Set-Cookie` headers survive. Extracted the happy-path response into `login_success_response` and added a unit test asserting both cookies are present; mutation-checked (the plain array fails the test with a single `Set-Cookie`).

Closes #639

author: pgsharma
body:
## What

Demotes Arctic Shift from "the corpus the library hinges on" to a documented **sample loader script** users run to build their own local Reddit corpus, plus a guide. Library behavior is unchanged — nothing under `src/metalworks/` was touched.

## Changes

- **`scripts/load_arctic_corpus.py`** — standalone CLI (`argparse`, **stdlib + `duckdb` only**, no metalworks import at module load). Pulls submissions for one or more subreddits across an N-month window from the `open-index/arctic` HF Parquet mirror into `<out>/submissions/<YYYY>/<MM>/<subreddit>.parquet` — the exact layout `ArcticReader(data_root=...)` reads. `--comments` optionally fetches live comment trees via the Arctic Shift API (stdlib `urllib`). Flags: `--subreddit/-s` (repeatable), `--months/-m`, `--out/-o`, `--comments`, `--limit`, `--hf-token`, `--memory-limit-gb`, `--comment-timeout-s`. Progress output + clear errors. Runnable as:
  ```
  python scripts/load_arctic_corpus.py --subreddit Supplements --months 3 --out ./corpus
  ```
- **`scripts/README.md`** — index for the `scripts/` directory.
- **`docs/load-reddit-corpus.md`** + **`docs.json`** nav entry (Extending group) — why / prereqs (`pip install "metalworks[arctic]"`) / command / output layout / how to point metalworks at it (`Metalworks(reader=ArcticReader(data_root="./corpus"))`).
- **`tests/test_load_arctic_corpus_script.py`** — offline smoke test of the CLI surface (loads the script by path, asserts flags + arg parsing + fail-fast on missing `--subreddit`); real pull marked `@pytest.mark.network`.

## Design note

The script **replicates** the reader's minimal DuckDB query + `hf://` glob layout rather than importing `ArcticReader` to *pull*, so it's fully self-contained and works as a copy-paste reference even outside the package. It *optionally* imports `ArcticReader` at the end only to verify the written corpus is readable.

## Gates

- `uv run ruff check .` clean; `uv run ruff format --check .` clean
- `uv run pyright` → 0 errors
- `uv run pytest -q` → 551 passed, 2 deselected (network)
- `docs.json` validates as JSON; new page on disk

author: ahump20
body:
## Summary
This narrows Pitch Atlas block-list reads so signed-in clients can read only the account id they blocked. Visitors should see the same community behavior, while the backend no longer grants client read access to the owning user id or block timestamp.

## What changed
- Added a Supabase migration that revokes broad SELECT on `blocked_users` from public client roles.
- Grants authenticated clients SELECT only on `blocked_id`.
- Added a policy-contract test so future migrations keep `blocker_id` and `created_at` out of client reads.

## Why
`blocked_users` is an account-safety table. RLS already scopes rows to the signed-in blocker, but broad table-level SELECT still exposed columns the app does not need. Keeping the readable surface to `blocked_id` preserves block-list and unblock use cases without exposing ownership/default fields.

## Risk and rollback
- Blast radius: Supabase read grants for signed-in block-list rows.
- Rollback boundary: revert this migration and test update, then restore table-level SELECT if a removed column is required.
- Known unknowns: production grant shape will be checked after merge before calling this live.

## Test plan
- Policy-contract test now checks the exact readable columns for `blocked_users`.
- Full test suite passed locally: 472 passed, 7 skipped.
- Typecheck passed.
- Lint passed with the existing 13 Fast Refresh warnings.
- Production build passed: 105 routes generated and prerender integrity passed.

## Screenshots / evidence
Data-surface proof will be posted after the production migration is applied: migration history, column grants, removed-column checks, and live Pitch Atlas route checks.

## Summary

- Phase 1 of the catch-up loop calls `checkAutoMergeConvergence` on every item carrying `fabrik:auto-merge-enabled`, but it never registers the WorktreeManager for `item.Repo` first.
- If the convergence budget has elapsed, the function dispatches to `pauseForConvergenceFailed` which calls `worktreesFor(item.Repo)`. With no WM registered, `worktreesFor` panics by design — taking down the whole engine.
- Add the same `ensureRepoReady` guard used by every other reinvoke dispatcher (`dispatchCIFixReinvoke`, `dispatchRebaseReinvoke`, `dispatchReviewReinvoke`). Unregistered repos now pause via the standard clone-failure path instead of crashing.

## Repro

A live engine crashed in `~/dev/fantasy/.fabrik` with:

```
panic: engine: no WorktreeManager registered for repo "shadoworg/fantasy" — ensureRepoReady not called
```

The PR (#1213) carried `fabrik:auto-merge-enabled` and the convergence budget had elapsed before the catch-up loop ran. Without this fix, every fresh `fabrik` start with a budget-exhausted yolo PR on the board would panic.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test -race ./...` — all packages green
- [x] `go vet ./...` — clean
- [x] New regression test `TestCheckAutoMergeConvergence_UnregisteredRepo_NoPanic` — exercises the exact panic path; fails before the fix, passes after

author: blokzdev
body:
## Phase 5.1 — pluggable-models foundation

Introduces a provider-neutral `agent/llm` seam and refactors the on-device agent loop onto it, with today's Anthropic path extracted as the first `AgentBackend`. **Pure, behavior-preserving refactor** — Gemini BYOK and the on-device tier land in 5.2+ (`docs/exec-plans/active/20260615-phase5-pluggable-models.md`).

The Anthropic **wire format is unchanged**, so the keyless emulator smoke (`AgentLoopEmulatorTest` + `StubModelServer`) passes untouched — that's the behavior-preservation proof.

### What changed
- **New `agent.llm` package (SDK-free):** `AgentBackend` (blocking `streamTurn(request, sink)` + force-close `cancel()`/`close()`), `BackendRequest`/`BackendSink`/`CompletedTurn`/`AgentStopReason`/`BackendStreamException`, the neutral history model `AgentMessage`/`AgentContent`/`ToolImage`, and `ToolSpec`.
- **`AnthropicBackend` + `AnthropicMessageMapping`:** the existing SDK path moved behind the seam — verbatim `buildParams` (prompt-cache + adaptive thinking + effort high), accumulate-and-stream loop, and tool/message translation. The only files under `agent` (besides `ModelCatalog`, deferred to 5.3) that import `com.anthropic`.
- **`AgentController`:** history is now `AgentMessage`; `runLoop` drives `backend.streamTurn` with a `BackendSink` for live deltas; the stop button calls `backend.cancel()`; the turn switch is over `AgentStopReason`. `buildParams`/`emitDelta` moved into the backend.
- **`AgentTools`:** `specs()` (`ToolSpec`) is the sole tool source; the Anthropic `Tool` builder and `definitions()` are gone.
- **`SessionHistory.rebuild`** returns neutral `AgentMessage`.

### Key design decisions
- **Blocking sink, not `Flow`.** The loop is a single sequential consumer on a dedicated worker thread that cancels by force-closing the stream — Flow's machinery would be unused. Deviates from the design-doc sketch; the deferred Flow alternative + reasoning is in `docs/BACKLOG.md`.
- **Hybrid `replayPayload` for thinking signatures.** Assistant turns carry their original `MessageParam` opaquely for byte-exact replay, so extended-thinking `signature` / `redacted_thinking` data is never lost; the loop reads only neutral text/tool_use blocks.

### Tests
- New JVM unit tests: `AnthropicToolMappingTest` (schema parity/order/required/determinism), `AnthropicMessageMappingTest` (thinking-signature round-trip), `ToolResultMappingTest` (text/image, error flag, pruning marker).
- Migrated `SessionHistoryTest`/`AgentToolsTest` to neutral types.
- Local: `assembleDebug` + `testDebugUnitTest` + `assembleDebugAndroidTest` green; `gofmt` clean. Instrumented smoke runs in CI's `emulator-smoke`.

### Minor intentional normalization
Synthetic error/denied/interrupted tool results now serialize as a single text block (array form) like all successful results, instead of the old string-content form — semantically identical to the model. Noted for transparency.

### Docs
History record; dedicated Phase 5 exec-plan (5.1–5.7, 5.1 done); ARCHITECTURE §8; QUALITY_SCORE; design-doc note; BACKLOG (Flow); VERIFICATION V122 (thinking+tool_use resume round-trip).

exactly — just expressed in Cloudflare's static-config files instead of `vercel.json`.

- `acgi-ai/infra/cloudflare/_headers` — report-only CSP + security headers,
  **byte-identical to vercel.json**. Console's *enforced* CSP is unaffected (served by Caddy on Cloud Run).
- `acgi-ai/infra/cloudflare/_redirects` — `/console`/`/console/*` hard-308 to the
  privileged console origin (privilege boundary), internal `*.md` → 404, SPA fallback last.
- `acgi-ai/wrangler.toml` — Pages project `acgs-marketing`, output `dist/`.
- `.github/workflows/marketing-cloudflare.yml` — `verify` (full `pnpm test:all`) on PR;

  with `::error::` + `exit 1` when `CLOUDFLARE_*` secrets are absent; deploy `needs: verify`).

- `scripts/check-marketing-csp.mjs` — now asserts `_headers` CSP stays byte-identical to

author: itome
body:
## Summary

評価フィードバック #8。`#[component]` 本体は `FnMut` のため、非 Copy な `Signal<T>` prop を `computed(move || …)` 等のネストクロージャに move すると E0507 となり `.clone()` が必要だった。`RwSignal<T>` は Copy 済み。阻害要因は `Signal::Static(T)` がインラインの所有 `T` を保持していたこと。

### 変更
static 値を owner 紐付きの `StoredValue<T>`（Copy・非リアクティブな arena ハンドル）に格納し、両アームを Copy にして enum を Copy 化:

```rust
enum Signal<T> { Stored(StoredValue<T>), Dynamic(ReadSignal<T>) }
```

`Clone`/`Copy` は手書き（`T: 'static` 束縛、`T: Copy` ではない）。derive だと `T: Copy` が付き `Signal<String>` が Copy にならないため。

各 package の不要になった `.clone()`（whisker-icons / -svg / -input / -webview）も除去（Copy な Signal に `clippy::clone_on_copy` が `-D warnings` で発火するため）。`signal_is_copy` テストで `Signal<String>` を2つの `move` クロージャに `.clone()` 無しで move できることを検証。

### トレードオフ（要確認）
- **割り当て**: static `Signal` 構築（`From<T>`/`Default`/`From<&str>`）が、インライン保持ではなく owner 紐付き arena スロット1個を割り当てる（Copy の代償）。1 prop あたり小ヒープ1回で典型用途は無視可能。
- **セマンティクス変化**: static `Signal` が**値セマンティクス→owner スコープのハンドルセマンティクス**に。構築時の owner が dispose した後にコピーを読むと `StoredValue: disposed` で panic（旧来は値が複製され生存）。owner 外構築は detached scope に park（panic せず、微小リーク）。既存コードは「同一 builder 呼び出し内で構築・消費」のため影響なし（全 workspace test / clippy green で確認）。
  - これは memory の Arc→arena handle footgun と同類。docs への注意書き追加を推奨。

## Test plan
- `cargo build --workspace` clean。
- `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` 警告なし。
- `cargo test --workspace` 全 pass（`signal_is_copy` 含む）。
- `cargo fmt --check` clean。

### Motivation
- Reduce expensive full 1..maxlag scanning for conditional Granger checks by testing only a focused set of lags informed by ranked features or selected mode. 
- Expose controls in the web UI to let users choose between full scan, a window around ranked lag, or only the ranked lag, with sane defaults and a fallback for missing long lags.
- Improve efficiency of the conditional Granger implementation by prebuilding baseline lagged columns once per variable.

### Description
- Added new parameters to `run_causal_review_stage`: `conditional_lag_mode`, `conditional_lag_window`, and `conditional_fallback_maxlag`, and wire them through the web form.
- Implemented `_conditional_candidate_lags` in `causal_review_runner.py` to compute candidate lag maps or return `None` for full scans.
- Added `build_candidate_lag_windows`, `_candidate_lags_for_variable`, `_valid_lag_center`, `_valid_positive_lag`, and `_parse_lag` helpers in `conditional_granger.py` to construct per-variable candidate lag lists centered on ranked lags and to validate inputs.
- Extended `run_conditional_granger_tests` signature to accept `candidate_lags` and modified the loop to iterate only over validated candidate lags; also optimized baseline (target and control) lag column construction to avoid rebuilt work per tested lag.
- Updated the web UI (`web.py` and embedded JS/HTML) to include controls for `conditionalLagMode`, `conditionalLagWindow`, and `conditionalFallbackMaxlag`, default values, and to pass those fields with the causal review request; fixed download target ID for the evidence CSV and added a brief help message about the new options.
- Adjusted causal review evidence columns to include `evidence_reason` in the front-end column list.
- Tests updated/added to cover new behavior and APIs in `tests/test_conditional_granger.py` and `tests/test_causal_review_runner.py`.

### Testing
- Ran the unit test suite with `pytest`; all tests passed. 
- Added tests in `tests/test_conditional_granger.py` for `build_candidate_lag_windows` clipping/centering behavior and for honoring `candidate_lags` in `run_conditional_granger_tests`, and they succeeded.
- Added tests in `tests/test_causal_review_runner.py` to verify `run_causal_review_stage` passes the correct `candidate_lags` for `ranked_window`, `best_only`, and `full_scan` modes and to assert error on unknown mode, and they succeeded.

author: grelinfo
body:
Closes #363.

Every grelmicro app that exposes `/readyz` wants to answer "can I reach my backends?" Today the user hand-rolls one check per provider. The demo proved the friction by probing Redis with a borrowed `Lock("healthz").locked()` round trip, which is neither the cheapest nor the most honest readiness signal for a connection pool.

## What this adds

* `Provider.check()`: an async readiness probe on every connection provider. Redis and Valkey run `PING`, Postgres and SQLite run `SELECT 1`. The base method raises `NotImplementedError`, so a provider with no backend opts out.
* `HealthChecks.add_provider(provider, *, name=None, critical=True, timeout=None)`: registers the probe as a `provider:{short_name}` check. Critical by default, so an unreachable backend fails `/readyz`. Pass `critical=False` for a degradable dependency such as a cache, or `name=` to disambiguate two providers of the same vendor.
* `HealthChecks(auto_health=True)`: off by default. On startup it discovers every active provider (including ones a Component borrows without listing) and registers a critical `provider:{short_name}` check for each. An explicit `add_provider` wins, and re-entry is idempotent. A second provider of the same vendor is skipped with a warning.
* `Grelmicro.providers`: lists active providers, deduped by identity.

## Settled decisions

* `auto_health` defaults to **off** (explicit opt-in, no-magic stance).
* Provider checks default to **critical** (matches the demo they replace and the `/readyz` framing).

## Demo

The FastAPI demo drops its hand-rolled `check_redis` for `HealthChecks(auto_health=True)`, which now probes both Redis and Postgres with no boilerplate.

## Tests and docs

Per-provider `check()` tests, full `add_provider` and `auto_health` coverage, a `Grelmicro.providers` test, a new "Provider Readiness Checks" docs section with runnable snippets, a `providers.md` note, and a changelog entry. The public-API snapshot is updated for the new `auto_health` parameter.

author: antonvdberg-bit
body:
## Summary

Docs-only governance packet. Ships two design docs to `main` with a binding stream-boundary preamble and a four-noun vocabulary that becomes canonical across all future multi-tenant platform work, **before IM-2 starts**.

Zero code, zero schema, zero DB write, zero auth/session change, zero Vercel/DNS change, zero tenant delivery artifact change, zero visual-separation code, zero IM-2 implementation.

## Files (exactly 3)

| File | Kind | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/operations/MULTI_TENANT_CONTAINMENT_AND_VISUAL_SEPARATION_AUDIT.md` | new (~611 lines) | Read-only MT-1 audit. Canonical home of the four-noun vocabulary in §5. Owns cross-tenant contamination model, visual-separation requirements, isolation tests, audit-trail requirements, and the MT-1..MT-8 plan. |
| `docs/operations/OPERATOR_MULTI_TENANT_CREDENTIAL_V1.md` | new (~1113 lines, r2) | Membership-matrix design. Owns the `user_tenant_memberships` schema, `auth_users.factory_master` capability, 9 required user flows, IM-1..IM-8 plan, and the 12 tampering tests §9.5b. Filename retains `OPERATOR_*` for link stability; doc scope explicitly covers both operators and multi-tenant clients (§1.4, §2.3.A, §4.8). |
| `artifacts/chat_history.md` | edit | New dated bullet `MULTI_TENANT_STREAM_BOUNDARY_VOCAB_2026_06_15_HIST` carrying the DRA for this PR. |

## The four approved nouns (binding across both docs)

1. **Core Capability** — reusable, CorpFlow-owned functional unit; code shared by all tenants.
2. **Tenant Deployment** — the tenant-specific *activation* of a Core Capability.
3. **Tenant Override** — a tenant-specific *difference* on top of a Tenant Deployment.
4. **Promotion to Core** — an anonymised improvement that started life as a Tenant Override and is rolled up into the Core Capability via an explicit packet.

## Two binding rules that follow

- A Tenant Override never silently affects another tenant. Cross-tenant inheritance only happens through an explicit Promotion to Core followed by a forward-promotion packet.
- A Core Capability is owned by the platform stream; a Tenant Deployment + its Overrides are owned by that tenant's delivery stream. The platform stream changes Core Capabilities and the membership matrix; it does not change any tenant's Deployment content (chatbot prompt, brand, CRM data, sandbox content).

## What this stream does NOT touch (codified in both docs)

- **No chatbot work.** Living Word chatbot, Lux concierge, future tenant chatbots stay with their respective delivery streams. This stream only documents that the chatbot prompt is a Tenant Override that today is hardcoded in `api/factory_router.js → handleChat` and should move to `tenant_personas.personaJson.chatbot.system_prompt` in MT-8.
- **No tenant sandbox creation or seeding.**
- **No tenant delivery artifact mutation.** Files under `artifacts/quality-audits/<tenant>/` are read for context only.
- **No DB write.**
- **No auth/session code change.** Every gate in `lib/server/auth.js`, `lib/server/session.js`, `lib/cmp/router.js` is governed by credential doc IM-5/IM-6 packets, each independently approved.
- **No blurring with tenant delivery work.** A change cannot land via this stream if its main effect is to deliver value for one tenant.

## Implementation gate (codified in the credential doc §33)

The 8-packet plans IM-1..IM-8 (credential doc) and MT-1..MT-8 (audit doc) exist for design completeness only — to prove the design is decomposable into reviewable units. They are **not** authorisation to begin implementing. Each packet starts only after Anton's explicit, per-packet approval.

- **IM-1** — schema (additive, behaviour-free). **APPROVED and SHIPPED 2026-06-15** (PR [#359](https://github.com/antonvdberg-bit/cor​pflow-ai-command-center/pull/359) squash `1c46dfbc150877ea8b39ec336cc18869e1ed906e`, Vercel deployment `5059820786`, follow-up docs PR [#361](https://github.com/antonvdberg-bit/corpflow-ai-command-center/pull/361) squash `843ef8f0`).
- **IM-2..IM-8** — explicitly **not started**; require their own approvals.
- **MT-2..MT-8** — explicitly **not started**; require their own approvals.

## Boundary discipline preserved by this PR

This PR contains only the two design docs and the chat-history bullet. It does **not** touch:

- any tenant's delivery artifacts under `artifacts/quality-audits/<tenant>/`;
- the visual-separation v1 code (`components/TenantChromeHeader.js` + `lib/client/tenant-chrome-view-model.js` + `node-tests/tenant-chrome-view-model.test.mjs` remain untracked locally for their own future PR);
- the Living Word chatbot code (`lib/server/chat-widget/*` remains in its delivery stream, untouched here);
- any schema / API / auth / session / Vercel / DNS surface.

The branch `docs/platform-stream-boundary-vocabulary` was created fresh off `origin/main` (head `843ef8f0`) with zero leftover staged content from other branches. The 7 untracked files in the working tree (visual-separation v1 + Living Word delivery scripts) were explicitly **not** staged.

## Why this matters

Without this governance lock, three failure modes are open:

- **Core/tenant mixing** — a "factory" change quietly leaks tenant-specific content (e.g. today's `api/factory_router.js → handleChat` hardcoding one tenant's persona prompt; called out for MT-8 in the audit doc §5.4).
- **Tenant brand or prompt content accidentally promoted into Core** — IM-1..IM-8 / MT-8 specifically guard against this with the anonymisation review step.
- **Design documentation mistaken for implementation authorization** — the "Implementation gate" preamble in each doc makes per-packet approval explicit.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this PR (no code change, so the existing test suite proves no cross-effect).
- [ ] Merge.
- [ ] Post-merge sanity: GET `https://core.corpflowai.com/api/factory/health` returns `ok:true` (docs-only PR; no runtime change expected).
- [ ] After merge, return the **IM-2 scope proposal only** (no IM-2 code yet) for Anton's explicit approval.

## Rollback

Revert this PR; both docs disappear from `main`; zero DB/Vercel/runtime impact. The four-noun vocabulary discussed in committed chat-history bullets remains as oral history; without the docs on `main`, future Cursor sessions would lose the binding canonical home and would need the docs reinstated before any IM-2..IM-8 / MT-2..MT-8 packet starts.

## Local gates

- `ReadLints` on all three touched files: zero diagnostics.
- No code touched, so no `npm test` re-run is required for this PR.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v11.6.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#1160)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.5.3...v11.6.0)

##### Minor Changes

- `pnpm install` completes without re-resolving when `pnpm-lock.yaml` was deleted but `node_modules` is intact: the up-to-date check now treats the current lockfile (`node_modules/.pnpm/lock.yaml`) — the record of what the previous install materialized — as the wanted lockfile, verifies the manifests still match it, restores `pnpm-lock.yaml` from it, and reports "Already up to date". Previously this scenario triggered a full resolution and a re-verification of every locked package against the registry.

- [`615c669`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/615c669): Added support for configuring URL-scoped registry settings through `npm_config_//…` and `pnpm_config_//…` environment variables, for example:

  ```text
  npm_config_//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=<token>
  pnpm_config_//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=<token>
  ```

  This provides a file-free way to supply registry authentication. Because the registry a value applies to is encoded in the (trusted) environment variable name, it is host-scoped by construction and cannot be redirected to another registry by repository-controlled config. The environment value is treated as trusted config: it takes precedence over a project/workspace `.npmrc` but is still overridden by command-line options. When the same key is provided through both prefixes, `pnpm_config_` wins.

- Raised the default network concurrency from `min(64, max(cpuCores * 3, 16))` to `min(96, max(cpuCores * 3, 64))`. Package downloads are I/O-bound, not CPU-bound, so deriving the floor from the core count left machines with few cores (for example 4-vCPU CI runners) downloading only 16 tarballs at a time and unable to saturate a low-latency registry. The `networkConcurrency` setting still overrides the default.

##### Patch Changes

- Improved the warning printed when a project `.npmrc` uses an environment variable in a registry/proxy URL or in registry credentials. The message now explains why the setting was ignored and how to migrate it to a trusted source — for example by moving the line to the user-level `~/.npmrc` or running `pnpm config set "<key>" <value>` — with a link to <https://pnpm.io/npmrc>. The `pnpm config set` example is only suggested when the key has no `${...}` placeholder, so the snippet is always safe to copy-paste.
- Print a "Lockfile passes supply-chain policies (verified 2h ago)" message when lockfile verification is skipped because a cached verdict for the same lockfile content and policy is reused. Previously the cached short-circuit was completely silent, which made it look like the policy gate never ran [#​12324](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/12324).
- Platform-specific optional dependencies are now skipped even when their `os`/`cpu`/`libc` fields are missing from the registry metadata or the lockfile. Some registries strip these fields from the package metadata, which made pnpm download and install the binaries of every platform regardless of `supportedArchitectures`. The missing platform fields of an optional dependency are now inferred from its name (e.g. `@nx/nx-win32-arm64-msvc` → `os: win32`, `cpu: arm64`), so foreign-platform binaries are skipped without even downloading them [#​11702](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11702).

</details>

author: romeo-folie
body:
## Problem
The reconciler's `importClobOrphan()` restores on-chain CLOB positions missing from the local ledger. The orphan scan matches CLOB↔ledger rows **by tokenId** — so a position already tracked under `(marketId, direction)` whose tokenId/asset didn't line up in that scan (e.g. a `rebate-farming` leg) gets flagged as an orphan and re-imported as a phantom `reconciled:clob` **duplicate** row.

This double-counts the position in P&L and inflates open exposure — the wipe-to-dust incident's open follow-up. **Confirmed live (2026-06-14):**
- Market `1897067` NO held **both** a `rebate-farming` and a `reconciled` open row.
- 5 sports markets (Scotland, LoL, Türkiye, UFC, Ecuador) were booked as `won` outcomes **and** simultaneously held as open `reconciled` orphans → daily P&L was untrustworthy (apparent "+$23" yesterday was partly this artifact).

## Fix
Add a `hasOpenPosition(market.id, direction)` guard in `importClobOrphan` (after direction is derived, after the resolved-market / recently-closed guards): **skip the import when a ledger row already exists for that market+direction.**

- **Direction-specific** — a legitimate opposite leg (the real second side of a pair) still imports.
- A genuine orphan (no ledger row) still imports.
- `market.id` is the Gamma numeric id that `recordPosition` writes and `hasOpenPosition` checks via the same `positionKey` — consistent.
- Fail-safe: a Redis error propagates to the outer try/catch → returns false (no import), which is the conservative outcome.

## Tests
New case: an orphan flagged by the tokenId scan (`getOpenPositions` empty) but already tracked under `(market, direction)` (`hasOpenPosition=true`) → `recordPosition` **not** called. Also added `hasOpenPosition` to the positionLedger mock + a `beforeEach` reset so the `true` override can't leak across tests (the suite uses `clearAllMocks`, which doesn't reset implementations).

Full suite **2844 pass**, `tsc --noEmit` clean, no eslint errors in touched files (cleared 2 pre-existing redundant assertions).

## Deploy
`src/monitor/*` (not futures) → rebuild **pga-monitor** after merge.

author: modifamorphic
body:
## Summary

Polish pass on the FFI surface and a small hash refactor. Closes the small-polish gap identified in the project review: no C header shipped with the FFI crate, no end-to-end FFI test, and the MurmurHash64A tail handling was more branchy than it needed to be.

## Changes

- Add hand-written `crates/darktide-ffi/darktide.h` mirroring the full C ABI surface in `crates/darktide-ffi/src/lib.rs` (15 functions, 2 `#[repr(C)]` structs, 4 opaque handle types). Uses `#pragma once` and an `extern "C"` guard for C++ consumers.
- Add `crates/darktide-ffi/tests/ffi_lifecycle.rs` with four integration tests:
  - null-pointer safety for every pointer-taking FFI function
  - Oodle load/free round-trip with the vendored library
  - synthetic-bundle lifecycle end-to-end (open → read_index → index_entry → extract_all → file_entry → file_data), including the `file_data` truncation contract (asserts both the full-copy return value and the truncated return value)
  - `darktide_murmur_hash64` and `darktide_lookup_extension` through FFI
- Add `"lib"` to `darktide-ffi` `crate-type` so integration tests can link the crate (`cdylib` + `staticlib` alone produce no rlib).
- Refactor `murmur_hash64a` tail handling in `crates/darktide-bundle/src/hash.rs` from explicit per-length (1-7) byte assignment to a zero-padded `copy_from_slice` + `from_le_bytes` read. Byte-equivalent; existing `mmh64a` test vectors cover input lengths 0..=8 (every interesting tail length).
- Reference the new header from the README FFI section.

## Notes

- The synthetic-bundle test deliberately uses a std-only temp file (`std::env::temp_dir()` + `std::process::id()`) instead of the `tempfile` crate. `tempfile` 3.27 pulls in `getrandom` 0.4 which transitively brings a WASI component toolchain (`wit-bindgen`, `wasm-encoder`, `wasip2`, `wasip3`, etc.) — 33 crates for one tempfile was disproportionate.
- The C header was verified against `lib.rs` function-by-function, and the `DarktideFileEntry` layout was confirmed byte-for-byte (the 4-byte alignment padding between `num_variants` and `data_len` matches on both sides because both use `#[repr(C)]` / standard C struct layout).

## Verification

author: kevin-hs-sohn
body:
## Summary
Phase 2 of the OSS local vault (after #571). A **credential-injecting TLS-MITM forward proxy** so a bot actually *uses* a registered credential without ever seeing it.

- **Pure decision core** `local_proxy_decision.py` (no mitmproxy, no secret): `resolve_host` (explicit host > `SERVICE_HOST_MAP` > none, exact match) + `decide_injection` → PassThrough / BlockPendingApproval / Inject (header plan only).
- **mitmproxy addon** `local_proxy.py` (lazy import, optional extra `magi-agent[vault]`): on Inject fetches the secret via `LocalVault.get_secret` and sets the auth header (stripping any pre-existing), scrubbed at frame end; on `requires_approval` with no approval → **403 + enqueues an approval** (this makes sub-project D real enforcement).
- **Lifecycle (local serve only)**: `MAGI_LOCAL_VAULT_PROXY_ENABLED` default-ON under the local sentinel; starts the proxy on 127.0.0.1, points the A egress seam (`MAGI_EGRESS_PROXY_*`) at it. Hosted never starts it (sentinel + `MAGI_VAULT_ADMIN_URL` short-circuit); missing extra fails soft (serve continues, proxy off).
- Additive non-secret `host` field on credential metadata + API.

### Independent security review: APPROVED (no Critical/Important)
Exhaustive trace: secret never logged / in the decision object / in exceptions / in the 403 body / in the approval record; mitmproxy flow logging off (`with_dumper/with_termlog=False`); CA key 0600 in 0700 vault dir; 127.0.0.1-only bind; approval fail-closed; exact host match (no substring/suffix/port bypass); core import graph mitmproxy-free.

## How to use
`pip install 'magi-agent[vault]'` then `magi-agent serve`: register a cred for e.g. notion in the dashboard → a bot `curl https://api.notion.com/...` is auto-authenticated by the proxy; the bot never sees the token. `requires_approval` creds return a pending-approval 403 until approved in the dashboard.

## Test Plan
- [x] `pytest tests/test_local_proxy_decision.py tests/test_local_proxy_addon.py tests/test_credentials_admin.py` → 47 passed, 1 skipped (mitmproxy importorskip); test_local_dashboard/egress_proxy green; ruff clean; module map regenerated; `uv lock --check` consistent
- [x] Proof tests: `test_secret_never_in_decision_object`, `test_addon_never_logs_secret`, `test_addon_block_enqueue_payload_carries_no_secret_with_fake_http`
- [ ] Follow-up: dashboard host-field UI (API already accepts `host`); consider blocking (vs pass-through) when an active cred's secret can't be decrypted

author: proggeramlug
body:
## What

`class NextNodeServer extends _baseserver.default` (interop-ESM dynamic parent) read base-server's relative-`require` captures (`_iserror`/`_utils`/`_log` → `this.__perry_cap_*`) as `undefined` from inherited methods → `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getProperError')` on every request (HTTP 500).

## Root cause

Pinned via JS read-back probes at three points on the **same instance** and **same method path**:
- parent-ctor end: captures = real objects ✓
- **post-construct (after `new NextNodeServer()` returns): `undefined`** ✗
- request: `undefined` ✗

So captures were written correctly by `super()` but **clobbered during the derived class's own construction, after `super()` returned** — the derived field-initializer phase. Synthesized capture fields (`__perry_cap_*`) are declared `init: None`, and `apply_field_initializers_recursive` emits `this.<field> = undefined` for every `init: None` field. When the field-init chain included the inherited dynamic parent's fields, that undefined-write re-initialized the captures `super()` had just populated. (ES runs derived field initializers *after* `super()`, so the clobber wins.)

## Fix

Skip `__perry_cap_*` fields in the field-initializer loop (`crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call/new.rs`). These synthesized fields are populated **exclusively** by the constructor's capture-param assignments, so a field-init undefined-write to them is always wrong.

## Verification

Real Next.js standalone server: all captures resolve (`_iserror`/`_utils`/`_log` = object), `getProperError` TypeError gone. The request now reaches a deeper render error (separate wall). Continues the Next.js bring-up (#793; after #5152).

author: geiserx
body:
## What

An adversarial control-client audit flagged two panics reachable (today only in theory) from control-server-supplied wire data. A hostile or MITM control server could otherwise drop the node off its control connection (DoS).

- **`ts_control/src/control_dialer.rs`** — the `DialMode::Ace` arm of the dial-plan `TcpDialer::dial` was `unimplemented!()`. `next_dialer` skips every `Ace` candidate before `dial` is called, so it's unreachable **today** — but `candidate.mode` comes from the control-supplied `MapResponse.control_dial_plan`, so a future change that wires Ace dialing without re-checking the skip would turn it into a remotely-triggerable panic in the reconnect path. Return a typed `io::ErrorKind::Unsupported` error instead; the dial loop falls through to the next candidate / system DNS exactly as for any failed candidate.
- **`ts_packetfilter_serde/src/ip_range.rs`** — `IpRange::iter_prefixes` had `_ => unreachable!()` for a mixed-family (one v4, one v6) `Range`. The deserialize path (`parse_range`) rejects mismatched families so it's unreachable from the wire, but `IpRange::Range` is a public constructor — make the function total (empty iterator for the impossible case) so packet-filter compile can never panic the netmap-apply path even if a future internal caller builds one by hand.

## Why no behavior change

- The `Ip` dial arm is byte-identical (`.await?` preserved). The `Ace` arm is now a bare typed `Err(...)`; both arms unify to `io::Result<TcpStream>` (the `.timeout().await?` folds `Elapsed` into `io::Error`), so no `return` is needed (clippy-clean).
- The parser still rejects mismatched-family ranges — the `mismatched_ip_kinds` `#[should_panic]` test (which asserts `IpRange::try_from("127.0.0.1-ffef::")` errors) still passes. `iter_prefixes` is only ever called on parser-produced (same-family) ranges.

The rest of the control client audited **clean**: Noise IK pinned-server-key handshake (no downgrade/MITM), bounded 16 MiB netmap frame + 120s read watchdog, `Result`-based parsing with no production unwrap/index on wire data, fail-closed filter compile, n²-backoff map-poll reset only on substantive frames.

## Verification

`cargo build -p geiserx_ts_control` (0 errors), `cargo test -p geiserx_ts_control` (233) + `geiserx_ts_packetfilter_serde` (15, incl. `mismatched_ip_kinds`), `clippy -D warnings` (0), `fmt`, `cargo run -p checks` (anti-leak guard) all green.

body:
## Problem
On `membership/reciprocal-clubs` (and any venue-detail page), a CTA/card/panel/download link pointing at a static asset (`/uploads/<file>.pdf`) did nothing on a direct click. Only "open in new tab" worked.

## Cause
Links were gated on `isExternal` / `startsWith('http')`. A relative `/uploads/...` href is not external → rendered as a React Router `<Link to>`. The SPA router intercepts the click, finds no matching route, and silently does nothing. New-tab works because that's a real browser navigation hitting nginx.

## Fix
Added an `isHardLink()` helper (absolute URL, `mailto:`/`tel:`, `/uploads/`, or any file-extension path → real `<a>`) and applied it at every link decision point in `VenueDetailPage`, including two card CTAs that were unconditionally `<Link>`.

Verified: `npm run typecheck && lint && build` all green.

author: jpwesselink
body:
## The bug

Reported on a real project (Pathé Thuis, 2026-06-15). \`dotsec validate\` reports 221 errors of the form

\`\`\`
AWS_ACCOUNT_ID: inline @encrypt directive not allowed when schema exists, run \`dotsec remove-directives\`
\`\`\`

…on every key in a freshly \`extract-schema\`'d \`.sec.prod\`, even though the file has no inline directives — only file-level config:

\`\`\`
# @provider=aws @key-id=alias/dotsec @default-encrypt

AWS_ACCOUNT_ID=ENC[…]
AWS_REGION=ENC[…]
\`\`\`

\`dotsec remove-directives\` would also be a no-op on this file — the directives the validator is complaining about don't exist in the source.

## Root cause

\`lines_to_entries\` (\`dotenv/src/lib.rs:147-151\`) synthesizes \`(\"encrypt\", None)\` onto every entry whose file declares file-level \`@default-encrypt\` and which has no explicit per-key \`@encrypt\`/\`@plaintext\`. The encrypt/decrypt path consumes that synthetic directive — design is correct.

But \`validate_entries_against_schema\` walks \`entry.directives\` looking for any \`SCHEMA_DIRECTIVES\` and errors when found. It can't tell synthetic apart from user-written, so every entry under \`@default-encrypt\` looks like a violation.

## Fix

Pass \`&FileConfig\` to the validator. In the inline-directive check, recognize and skip the synthetic-default case:

\`\`\`rust
let is_synthetic_default = (name == \"encrypt\"   && file_config.default_encrypt == Some(true))
                        || (name == \"plaintext\" && file_config.default_encrypt == Some(false));
if is_synthetic_default { continue; }
\`\`\`

This stays correct in the inverse — a user who writes inline \`@plaintext\` under file-level \`@default-encrypt\` (a real override) keeps producing the error. \`has_explicit\` was true at parse time, synthesis never happened, the directive in \`entry.directives\` is genuinely user-written.

## Coverage

Two new regression tests:

- \`schema_validation_ignores_synthetic_default_encrypt\` — file-level \`@default-encrypt\`, schema exists, no inline directives → zero \"inline @encrypt\" errors (the Pathé Thuis case)
- \`schema_validation_user_inline_plaintext_still_errors_with_default_encrypt\` — user-written inline \`@plaintext\` under file-level \`@default-encrypt\` → still flagged (the inverse must keep working)

## Call sites updated

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| \`dotsec-napi/src/lib.rs\` | \`validateAgainstSchema\` now also passes \`extract_file_config(&lines)\` |
| \`dotsec/src/cli/commands/{format,push,validate}.rs\` | same |
| \`dotenv/src/lib.rs\` tests (12 sites) | pass \`&FileConfig::default()\` — none of the existing tests used file-level defaults |

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo test --workspace --all-targets\` — 431 pass, 0 fail (includes both new regressions)
- [x] \`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings\` — clean
- [x] End-to-end smoke against the reported file shape: \`init -y\` → \`set -y\` × 2 with \`--encrypt\` → \`extract-schema\` → \`validate\` → exits clean. Before this fix the validate step errored.

author: etendue
body:
## Summary

Implements v4_plan E2.6: wires **DiffusionHarmonizer's temporal mode** into `viser_gui_4d` so continuous Play sequences get de-flickered by the model (curr + last K corrected outputs as temporal reference), as opposed to the existing per-frame DiFix/Fixer path.

This is the only place Harmonizer's temporal advantage (video-level consistency) can be leveraged — E2.1 is offline single-frame, E2.2 training distillation is nontemporal by construction (random novel views, no frame order).

## What's new

**Temporal IPC layer (HMN1, independent from DFX1 — protects E1 anchor):**
- `utils/harmonizer_protocol.py` — HMN1 wire codec: 20-byte header (magic|H|W|C|K) + (1+K_in) uint8 frames; client-side deque design (history on client, server stateless, seek = clear deque = natural reset). DFX1 reply reused for single-frame return.
- `utils/harmonizer_client.py` — `HarmonizerTemporalClient`: K-frame self-reference history deque; `fix(img, reset=)` clears history on discontinuous timeline changes; failure does not poison history (no append); graceful raw fallback (never crashes viewer).
- `harmonizer_temporal_server.py` — temporal Harmonizer inference TCP server (runs in harmonizer-cosmos-env container); `make_harmonizer_temporal_transform` does V-stacking → 5D (1,C,1+K,H,W) forward → V=0 output selection; pure-torch (no einops) so Mac can import for shape-contract tests.

**viser_gui_4d wiring (6 minimal touchpoints):**
- `--harmonizer_temporal_server` / `--harmonizer_temporal_K` CLI (mutually exclusive with `--difix_server`).
- `_postproc_reset_flag`: any non-play timeline change (seek/scrub/loop-wrap/init) sets it → next frame sent cold (V=1).
- `_postproc_last_wh`: forces reset on resolution change (history frames must match curr HxW).
- `_maybe_difix` now dispatches: temporal client first (1+K with reset), else original DifixClient path unchanged + None-guard against AttributeError.

**Demo + tests:**
- `scripts/e26_temporal_demo.py` — raw / nontemporal_fixed / temporal_fixed three-column comparison on a continuous frame sequence.
- `tests/test_harmonizer_temporal_ipc.py` — 20 Mac tests, all green.

## Key fix during integration: Conv3d warmup (cce14ba)

First inceptio runtime test crashed server-side: `RuntimeError: Kernel size (3,1,1) can't be greater than actual input size (2 x 144 x 256)`. Root cause: Harmonizer's temporal CausalConv3d (kernel=3 on V axis) only accepts **V=1 or V≥3**; my cold-start growth (V=1→2→3→4→5) walked into the V=2..K-1 forbidden zone.

Fix mirrors the official `inference_pix2pix_turbo_harmonizer.py` L133 `have_history = len >= min_history`: send V=1 while `len(history) < K`, send the full 1+K stack only once the deque is full. Lesson: the model class docstring "V can be 1" refers to the nontemporal path, not arbitrary V.

## Verification

- **36/36 Mac tests green** (temporal 20 + DiFix 11 + E2.1 5; zero regression — HMN1 magic isolated from DFX1, DiFix single-frame path byte-identical).
- **inceptio end-to-end 目测通过** (2026-06-15): temporal mode V=5 works, seek auto-resets history, frame buffer holds corrected data (self-reference history confirmed correct). V=5 latency ~1000ms; K=2 (V=3) drops to ~600ms as a tuning option.

## Commits
- `9de9101` feat(E2.6): temporal Harmonizer IPC layer (protocol + client + server)
- `5cf26e7` feat(E2.6): wire temporal Harmonizer into viser_gui_4d

author: orolol
body:
## Contexte

Batterie demandée `{ctx~0, 16k} × {base, MTP-4, Eagle3, DFlash}` (`scripts/spec_decode_battery.sh`), GPU vérifié calme :

| mode | ctx ~0 | ctx 16k |
|---|---:|---:|
| base (sans rien) | 60.5 | **52.7** |
| MTP-4 | 92.0 (acc .83) | **4.0** (acc .44) ⚠️ |
| Eagle3 | 91.2 (AL 2.33) | 27.8 (AL 1.54) |
| DFlash | 111.2 (AL 3.66) | 27.5 (AL 3.31) |

À 16K le décode de base est sain, mais MTP-4 s'effondre à 4.0 tok/s — avec une acceptance **saine** (0.44). Donc pas l'acceptance.

## Diagnostic

- `mtp_rebuilds=0` → **pas** de recapture de graphe.
- `mtp_verify_seconds` ~constant **85 ms/cycle** à 4K/8K/16K → le verify n'est **pas** la falaise.
- `main_decode_steps=8=fallback_window` : l'auto-fallback s'enclenche (acc<0.55), puis le décode plein tourne à ~4-5 tok/s.

Seule différence base ↔ fallback : l'**interpréteur decode est AUTO-ON à `mtp>0`**. Contrôle décisif (mtp=0, interpréteur forcé), totalement découplé de MTP :

| mtp=0, ctx | interp ON | interp OFF |
|---|---:|---:|
| 4K | 65.3 | 65.4 |
| 8K | **6.6** | 59.6 |
| 16K | 3.5 | 53.9 |

Cause (lecture code) : `interpreter/opcodes/attn_decode_full.cuh` exige `decode_n_splits<=1` et scanne tout le KV **en série par q-head** — aucun split-KV, contrairement à `attention_decode_tiled` (plat à 24K). C'est **O(contexte)**, il s'effondre dès 8K.

## Fix

Rust pur, zéro machinerie de graphe : l'auto-policy de l'interpréteur prend un **cap de contexte** — auto-ON ssi `max_context <= QWEN36_INTERPRETER_DECODE_MAX_CONTEXT` (défaut **4096**, où l'interpréteur gagne @128 / fait jeu égal @4K). `QWEN36_INTERPRETER_DECODE=1` bypasse le cap. `pure-MTP interp OFF @16K = 35.9` (vs 35.8 ON) → couper l'interpréteur **ne régresse pas** le verify.

## Validation (défaut, fix actif)

| cellule | avant | après |
|---|---:|---:|
| MTP-4 @16K | 4.0 | **39.3** (×10) |
| MTP-4 @ctx16 | — | 132.5 (interpréteur conservé) |
| MTP-4 @4K | — | 52.2 (conservé) |
| base @16K | 52.7 | inchangé |

## Suite (lane interpréteur/long-ctx)

Donner à `attn_decode_full` un chemin split-KV pour rouvrir l'interpréteur au-delà de 4K. Note : à 16K **tous** les modes spec restent sous base (52.7) — le routage « base seul ≥16K » tient pour l'instant.

author: sairam0424
body:
## Summary

Promotes the Content-Security-Policy from **Report-Only → enforced**. The policy
string is **byte-identical** — only the header key changes (`Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`
→ `Content-Security-Policy`) — so the exact policy that logged **zero violations** in the
live v1.4.0 production sweep (all four views incl. the WebGL Play view) is now what
actually blocks. 1 file, +11/−3.

This completes the production-hardening story: CSP shipped Report-Only in v1.4.0 to
observe safely; this flip makes it defend.

## Why it's safe (26-agent per-directive audit)

A dynamic workflow mapped **every CSP directive against the real resource loads** —
including paths the click-through sweep didn't exercise (Polly-audio `blob:` media, the
AWS `/api/*` fetches, the optional 5th voice view + wake word). Adversarially verified.

- ✅ Every browser-loadable resource class is covered; **nothing loads outside the policy**.
- ✅ `next/font` **self-hosts** (26 woff2 under `/_next/static/media`) → `font-src 'self' data:` is correct. A verifier's "fonts come from `fonts.gstatic.com`, CSP will block them" claim was **disproven against the build output** (the only `gstatic` string is a build-time loader directive in a dev sourcemap, not a runtime `@font-face`).
- ✅ All AWS calls (Bedrock/Polly/Transcribe) are **server-side**; the browser only hits same-origin `/api/*` + Vercel beacons → `connect-src 'self' …vercel-insights` is sufficient.
- ⛔ Every proposed *tightening* (drop `blob:` from img/worker-src, drop `shields.io` / `vercel.live`) was **rejected** — breaking prod on an auth-less portfolio is far worse than a slightly loose CSP; the enforced policy must stay ≥ the zero-violation baseline.
- ℹ️ `'unsafe-inline'` on script/style is **intentional + unavoidable** (Next inline bootstrap + `inlineCss` + Motion runtime style *attributes*, which nonces can't cover). Accepted on an auth-less site with `rehype-sanitize` on chat markdown.
- ℹ️ `upgrade-insecure-requests` retained (it becomes meaningful once enforced; resolves the only Report-Only console notice).

## Test plan

- ✅ `pnpm build` green — 35 test files, 199 tests.
- ✅ Local prod server: `Content-Security-Policy` header present, Report-Only **gone**,
  the other 4 security headers intact, `/` → 200.
- ✅ Real-browser sweep (Classic + Play/WebGL) under the **enforced** policy: **zero CSP
  refusals** (the only console errors are the known local-only Vercel-analytics 404s,
  which don't exist on the real Vercel deploy and aren't CSP blocks).

## After merge

Post-deploy I'll re-confirm on prod that `Content-Security-Policy` (not Report-Only) is
live and re-sweep for refusals — but the policy is unchanged from the one already proven
clean in production, so this is verification, not risk.

author: khusmann
body:
## Problem

`PlotlyOutput` is blank under shinylive — the JS console shows 404s for every
file-backed dependency it ships at runtime:

```
GET .../app_xxx/typedarray-0.1/typedarray.min.js          404
GET .../app_xxx/crosstalk-1.2.2/js/crosstalk.min.js       404
GET .../app_xxx/plotly-main-2.25.2/plotly-latest.min.js   404
GET .../app_xxx/irid-plotly-0.2.0.9000/plotly-irid.js     404   ← irid's own factory
```

## Root cause (not packaging — verified)

The files are present in the webR VFS (confirmed in the shinylive `app.json`
bundle, and `plotly-irid.js` ships in the built tarball exactly like `irid.js`).
The problem is *serving*: widget deps don't ride the static page — they're sent
at mount time in the `irid-widget-init` message and loaded client-side by
`Shiny.renderDependencies`. The old path registered a resource path
*mid-session* (`createWebDependency` → `addResourcePath`). **shinylive doesn't
serve mid-session resource paths**: its request bridge only invokes the Shiny
app handler and has no httpuv `staticPaths` layer, so every such file 404s.
UI-attached deps (e.g. `irid.js`) and CDN/href deps (e.g. CodeMirror) are
unaffected, which is why only widget file-deps broke.

This was settled with a throwaway shinylive spike (not committed; lives under
`dev/spikes/shinylive-runtime-dep`) driven by headless Chrome — a UI-attached
control dep loads while the resource-path form 404s.

## Fix

`register_widget_dep()` now **inlines** each file-backed script/stylesheet
directly into the dependency's `head` HTML (`<script>…</script>` /
`<style>…</style>`), clearing `src`/`script`/`stylesheet`. No resource path is
registered, so there's nothing for shinylive to fail to serve. href-only and
head-only deps pass through unchanged.

Inlining is byte-for-byte a wash in shinylive (webR has no real HTTP layer — a
would-be file `GET` crosses the same in-browser bridge as the message). The only
real cost is in *server* Shiny, where a resource path would be browser-cached
across reloads — so `widget_deps_to_send()` tracks each `name@version` on
`session$userData` and ships the (multi-MB) content only once per session.
`Shiny.renderDependencies` also dedupes *rendering* by name, so a remount's
re-fired init is a no-op for the deps step.

## Verification

Re-ran the spike with a **before/after** in one shinylive export (headless
Chrome over the real webR runtime):

```
control: true  |  runtime OLD (resource path): false  |  runtime FIXED (inline head): true
HTTP 404 .../app_xxx/spike-runtime-old-1.0/runtime.js
```

The old resource-path form still 404s; the new inline-head form loads.

Unit tests in `test-widget-deps.R` updated to the inline contract (passthrough
for href/head-only, inlining for file-backed, `</script>` escaping, per-session
dedupe, mount integration). `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the plotly factory comment
updated.

## Summary

This PR introduces a comprehensive AI agent system for interior architecture and construction professionals. It includes a modular multi-agent architecture with specialized agents for different workflows, plus an extensive knowledge base of templates, checklists, databases, and reference materials.

## Key Changes

### Agent System (`agents/`)
- **Main orchestrator** (`main_agent.py`): Routes user requests to appropriate specialized agents based on intent
- **Seven specialized agents**:
  - `consulting_agent.py`: Customer consultation and requirements gathering
  - `estimate_agent.py`: Estimate creation and review using cost databases
  - `specbook_agent.py`: Material specification book generation
  - `schedule_agent.py`: Construction schedule and daily log creation
  - `contract_agent.py`: Contract review and change order documentation
  - `inspection_agent.py`: Completion inspection and defect management
  - `architect_agent.py`: Architectural design support (regulations, drawings, permits)
- **Configuration** (`config.py`): Centralized model ID and knowledge base loading utilities
- **Documentation** (`README.md`): Usage guide for all agents

### Knowledge Base (`interior_architect_agent_knowledge/`)

**Common Consultation Materials** (`01_공통_상담자료/`)
- Customer consultation questionnaire (412 items covering project scope, budget, timeline, lifestyle, design preferences)
- Site investigation checklist (building conditions, electrical, plumbing, windows, space details)
- Requirements summary template

**Interior Contractor Resources** (`02_인테리어_업자/`)
- Cost database by construction type (demolition, carpentry, electrical, plumbing, etc. with 2024 market rates)
- Completion inspection checklist (punch list format)
- Standard construction schedule with 30-unit apartment baseline
- Daily construction log template
- Change order confirmation form
- A/S response documentation template

**Architect Resources** (`03_건축가/`)
- Design brief template
- Design stage deliverables guide (planning through construction administration)
- Drawing review checklist (layout, elevation, section, structural, MEP coordination)
