author: yosuke-wolfssl
body:
## Description

Fixes a TOCTOU-induced uninitialized-pointer dereference in `HandleInclude`
(`apps/wolfsshd/configuration.c`) that can crash `wolfsshd` with a SIGSEGV.

`HandleInclude` walks an `Include` directory using **two separate `readdir`
passes** split by `WREWINDDIR`:

1. **Pass 1** counts non-directory entries into `fileCount`.
2. `fileNames` is allocated with `WMALLOC(fileCount * sizeof(char*))` — **without
   zero-initialization**.
3. **Pass 2** fills the array but is bounded by
   `i < fileCount && (dir = WREADDIR(...)) != NULL`, so it stops early if
   `readdir` returns `NULL`.
4. The processing loop then iterated the **full** `fileCount`, calling
   `WSTRLEN(fileNames[i])` / `WSNPRINTF(...)` on every slot.

If the directory shrinks between the two passes (a local user removing files
from a writable `Include` directory, e.g. a group-writable
`/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/`), the second pass fills fewer slots than `fileCount`.
The tail slots `[fileFilled .. fileCount-1]` remain uninitialized, and the
processing loop dereferences those garbage pointers, crashing the daemon at
start/restart. No SSH authentication is required to trigger it.

## Fix

- **Bound the processing loop to the actual fill count.** Capture the number of
  slots populated by the second pass (`fileFilled = i;`) and iterate
  `for (i = 0; i < fileFilled; i++)` instead of `i < fileCount`. This is the
  fix that closes the uninitialized read.
- **Zero-initialize the array after allocation** (`WMEMSET(fileNames, 0, ...)`)
  as defense-in-depth, so any slot not reached by the second pass is `NULL`
  rather than garbage and the code fails safe against future changes.

The opposite direction (more files appearing in pass 2) was already safe — the
`i < fileCount` guard stops the second pass at the allocated size.

## Testing

- `./configure --enable-sshd && make` — clean build.
- `apps/wolfsshd/test/test_configuration` — all `Include` / wildcard cases pass,
  including `Include sshd_config.d/*.conf`, which exercises this exact two-pass
  path and confirms no regression in the normal (`fileFilled == fileCount`)
  case.

author: mlauf-labs
body:
Closes #31. Part of #27.

## What
A saidex-native completion hook so observability backends can record the extraction-level verdict that LangChain `callbacks` never see.

- New `on_complete: Callable[[ExtractionEvent], Awaitable[None]] | None` parameter on every entry point (`extract_data`, `extract_data_from_text`, `extract_data_list`, `extract_data_list_from_text`, `extract_data_with_tools`, `run_extractor_agent`) **and** all six sync wrappers.
- New exported `ExtractionEvent` (schema_name, result, stats, messages, source_text) and the `OnComplete` type alias.
- New opt-in `capture_source_text: bool = False` — when set, the input text is stored on `stats.source_text` and the event.

## Behaviour
- Fires **exactly once per top-level call**, on success and failure, after all retries and fallback.
- Hook exceptions are logged and suppressed — an observer can never break the extraction.
- Batch path fires its own hook with the **list result** and **item schema name**; the inner `extract_data` call is silenced so it fires only once.
- `source_text` defaults off (PII/memory); the event always carries `messages` so a hook can derive its own context regardless.

## Why
LangChain callbacks fire per LLM call and have no `on_extraction_end`. The hook closes that gap; running it inside the same Langfuse span attaches `success` / `failure_reason` / `field_issues` to the same trace as the LLM generations.

## Tests / docs
- `tests/test_completion_hook.py`: fires once on success/failure, source_text on/off, hook exception isolated, no-hook noop, batch reports list + item schema, agent path.
- Langfuse docs gain an "Attaching the extraction verdict (`on_complete`)" recipe with a shared-trace example.
- `ruff`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy src/` (strict), `pytest` — all green (217 passed).

author: kaylakassis
body:
Turns THRYVE's soft paywall into a **hard** one: unskippable, fail-closed, enforced on every owner endpoint (reads included), with the owner's billing + data-export escape hatches preserved — plus a win-back discount drip for owners who hit the wall and don't convert.

> **Stacked on #16.** Base is `claude/booking-tz-fix` so this diff is *only* the paywall work. Merge #16 first (or retarget this to `main` once #16 lands).

Built to the approved plan; informed by the high-converting mobile-paywall references Kayla shared (hero → headline → proof → benefit list → highlighted plan → reassurance → CTA → trust line).

---

## Before → after

| | Before (soft) | After (hard) |
|---|---|---|
| Enforcement | writes only, ~73 endpoints | reads **and** writes, every owner endpoint |
| On DB error | **fail open** (log + allow) | **fail closed** (deny, distinct `gate-unavailable`) |
| Escape | "Use the free client view" → `/me` | unskippable; only Billing / Export / Log out |
| `active` rows | `isActive` true even with null/expired period | requires a live period (closes a latent bypass) |
| Win-back | none | dwell-cron email + **abandoned-cart inline offer** |

---

## A. Central fail-closed enforcement
`api/_lib/workspaceGate.js` → `ensureActiveWorkspace(user, req, res)` replaces the soft `requireActiveSubscription` (now deleted).
- Single `isWorkspaceActive(row)` shared by the gate and `/api/me` so they can't disagree.
- Hard-allowed: live `trialing`, live `active`, `past_due` (dunning owns the suspend flip). Blocked: expired-trial, `suspended`, `cancelled`, `incomplete`, `inactive`.
- **Fails closed** on DB error; ~60s per-lambda positive cache so a transient blip can't bounce a paying owner; sponsored bypass; `evictWorkspaceGateCache` on `/billing/sync`.

## B. Migration (132 files)
Mechanical `ensureWorkspace` → `ensureActiveWorkspace` across all owner endpoints. Exempt set stays ungated by construction: `billing/*`, `account/{export,delete}`, `auth/*`, `me/*` (client portal), `onboarding/*`, public booking/site/sign/view pages, `webhooks/*`, `cron/*`, health.

## C. Unskippable wall — `Paywall.jsx` + `AppShell.jsx`
- Removed the `/me` escape; `body.app-walled` scroll-locks and hides the view-toggle.
- Affordances: **Subscribe**, **Manage billing** (only when a Stripe customer exists), **Export my data** (the always-ungated `GET /api/account/export`), **Log out**.
- **isClient carve-out**: an owner who's also a client elsewhere keeps one labeled link to that business's portal; solo owners get none.
- **Redesigned** in the reference format using THRYVE tokens (renders natively in Calm + Bold). No fabricated Monthly/Annual toggle (one real $49 plan) and no fake ratings/user-counts — the truthful "replace $122/mo of tools, save $73/mo" claim fills the social-proof slot.

## D. Win-back drip
- `api/_lib/winback.js` → `ensureWinbackOffer` (idempotent, one offer per workspace ever, race-safe). Shared by both triggers.
- **Abandoned-cart (primary):** on `?subscribed=cancelled`, `POST /api/billing/winback-offer` mints/reads the coupon and the wall shows "Wait — 30% off your first 3 months" inline; Subscribe is auto-discounted server-side (`checkout.js` applies the stamped coupon — no code entry).
- **Dwell cron (catch-all):** `api/cron/winback.js` (daily, 11:00 UTC) emails + pushes owners who left and didn't convert after 3 days.
- Stripe: `createWinbackCoupon` (repeating %-off coupon + single-use promo code); checkout drops `allow_promotion_codes` when a coupon is pre-applied (Stripe rejects both).

## E. Funnel measurement (no new tables)
`workspaces.paywall_first_seen_at` (stamped in the gate's deny path, COALESCE-preserving) + `converted_at` (stamped in `sync.js` + `webhooks/billing.js`). With the existing `onboarding_state`, the full signup → onboarding → paywall → customer funnel is queryable, and these feed the win-back dwell trigger.

---

## Schema (idempotent ALTERs on `workspaces`)
`paywall_first_seen_at`, `converted_at`, `winback_offer_sent_at`, `winback_coupon_id`, `winback_promo_code`, `winback_expires_at`, + partial index `idx_workspaces_winback_candidates`.

## Tests / verification
- **`tests/paywall-coverage.test.mjs` (new)** — 3 grep invariants, no DB: every non-exempt endpoint gated; exempt set never gated; zero residual `requireActiveSubscription`. **3/3 pass.**
- **`tests/audit-fixes.test.mjs`** rewritten: `isWorkspaceActive` truth table (incl. active-with-null-period) + fail-closed assertions.
- `npm run lint` clean (0 errors), `npm run build` clean.
- DB-backed e2e (suspended owner → 402) is in the suite but Postgres isn't reachable from the CI sandbox here.

## Deliberate non-goals (per locked decisions)
- No card-required trial (kept the no-card 28-day trial).
- No A/B paywall variant engine (one strong wall; variant infra is a separate build).
- Win-back is single-use and triggered by the **rejection** (cancelled checkout), not shown proactively.

## Highest-risk areas to review
1. Fail-closed could lock out a paying owner on a DB blip — mitigated by the PK lookup + positive cache + distinct `gate-unavailable` status (retry UI, not the wall).
2. The 132-file migration accidentally gating the client portal / billing / export — guarded by the coverage test's exempt-set invariant.
3. Stripe `discounts` + `allow_promotion_codes` mutual exclusion + no double-coupon on cron rerun (the `winback_offer_sent_at IS NULL` guard).

author: hannesrauhe
body:
## Summary

**Trigger-period correctness**
- Feed cutoff and post-count fetch were anchored to calendar midnight and a rolling 24 h window, respectively. Both now use `getLastTriggerTime()`, so the full trigger period is always visible even when it spans two calendar days.
- New helpers: `getLastTriggerTime()`, `getNextTriggerTime()`. Trigger period (last → next) is shown in the feed footer for debugging.

**PRNG bug fix**
- All days within the same month were landing at the same trigger time (~16:50 in June 2026). Root cause: consecutive date strings share only their last character, giving djb2 hashes too close for a single xorshift32 round to spread across the 720-minute window. Fixed by running 3 rounds.

**Multi-device sync**
- Removed the localStorage post-count cache entirely. On every page load, `fetchTodayPostCount` makes a server call anchored to `getLastTriggerTime()`, so any device always starts with the authoritative count. In-session, `periodPostCount` is held in memory and the tick loop resets it to 0 when it detects a new trigger period has started (no page reload required).

**State machine redesign**
- Removed the trigger-time gate for users with 0 posts. Any user who hasn't posted in the current period can take a photo immediately — no countdown wait.
- Removed the `before_trigger` state entirely. The feed is now always the resting state: 0 posts → capture, 1 post → feed + "+ Post", 2 posts → feed + live "next post in Xh Ym" header countdown.

**Dead code cleanup**
- `src/screens/countdown.ts` deleted.
- `timer.ts`: `getTriggerForDate` and `getTodayTrigger` made internal (no longer exported); `formatWallTime` removed.
- `package-lock.json` added to `.gitignore`.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open app with 0 posts before today's trigger time → should go straight to capture (no countdown)
- [ ] Post once → feed appears with "+ Post" button and "1/2 posted"
- [ ] Post twice → feed stays visible, header shows "next post in Xh Ym" live countdown
- [ ] Open app on a second device after posting on the first → correct count loaded from server
- [ ] Verify trigger times vary across days (no clustering at the same time)
- [ ] Feed shows posts from the full trigger period, not just the last 24 h

author: kompiro
body:
Refs #1568

## Purpose

Design doc deciding whether/how to give lifecycle annotations machine-readable migration intent (`@deprecated(until: …)`, `@migration_target(from: …)`) — gap **B** of the syntax-v1.0 stocktaking (#1567).

## Decisions (resolved in review)

- **Q1 (scope) → (b)**: store + display + light filter/style in core. **export (dated dependency graph) and PERT/critical-path are out of scope** — PERT is a non-goal (#23); if export demand appears it's a separate follow-up (same escape-hatch thinking as `job.schedule` / draw.io).
- **Q2 (value) → graceful degradation (date-or-string)**: parseable date/quarter → machine-usable (filter/style); otherwise an opaque display-only string. Same "recognized → semantic; unrecognized → opaque" pattern as `operations` verb-decoration / open annotations / `job.schedule`.
- **Q5 (drift) → pure note**: a passed `until` emits no diagnostic (no "current time" in the evaluation; consistent with warn-don't-error / not following runtime).
- **Q3/Q4 (recorded, finalize at implementation)**: `@name(key: "value")` param form; builtin-only keys (`until`, `from`); custom annotations stay bare to keep the two-tier surface minimal.

## Changes

- Add `docs/design/migration-intent-fields.md` (inventory, options, comparison, decisions, implementation guidance).

## Manual Verification Checklist

N/A — design doc only.

## Related Docs

- `docs/design/migration-intent-fields.md` → promoted to an ADR in the implementation PR (design file deleted there).
- #1568 (parent gap B in #1567), #23 (time-axis non-goal), ADR-20260511-02 (prose-convention precedent), TPL-20260610-01.

author: chazut
body:
1.1.0 **introduces the full gear-upgrade (swap) layer** (weapon, armor, helmet, rig, backpack, headset, mag/ammo awareness, mod-stripping), shipped **always-on**, and lands a large wave of **behaviour and reliability fixes** (doors, multi-floor looting, exfil, SAIN personality, faction-mod coexistence) plus some **attempted (as-yet unconfirmed) fixes for FIKA / headless setups** — FIKA is not an officially supported configuration.

---

## Headline: the in-raid gear-upgrade (swap) layer (new)

Bots now upgrade everything they wear and carry mid-raid, not just their primary. Each kind scores the candidate against what the bot already has and only swaps on a real improvement (margin 1.10). Corpse gear can **displace** the equipped piece; containers and ground loot only fill empty slots. Scavs never swap (empty-slot equip only).

- **Weapon** (Phase 1) — scored on ergonomics, recoil, effective range and ammo quality with per-map weights, not price. A no-downgrade guard stops trading a good AP rifle for an expensive shotgun.
- **Armor + helmet** (Phase 2) — armor-class driven.
- **Rig** (Phase 3) — capacity + armor class; same-type only (simple↔simple, armored↔armored); the bot's carry is transferred into the new rig before the atomic swap, and the swap aborts if anything wouldn't fit.
- **Headset** (Earpiece) — handbook-price scored.
- **Backpack** — pure capacity; carry transferred first, capacity guard on the candidate's *free* cells (corpse leftovers ride along), aborts if it wouldn't fit.
- **Mag / ammo awareness** (Phase 4) — pickups during a loot session are evaluated against the loadout the bot will *end* the session with (post-swap), with a cartridge-compatibility walk so mags/ammo for the new gun are kept and the rest isn't hoarded.
- **Strip-before-discard** (Phase 5) — a weapon about to be dropped to the corpse is stripped of its valuable mods first (scope, suppressor, grip, etc., above a per-slot price threshold); kill the bot later and you find the old gun picked clean.
- **Multi-swap chains** — one corpse can yield weapon + armor + rig + backpack + headset in sequence, each with its own pre-swap settle + re-evaluation.

### Swap config
The gear-swap layer is a core behaviour, **always on**, with the margin hardcoded (`LootConfig.SwapMargin = 1.10`) — no F12 toggle. The whole layer is new in 1.1.0, so there's nothing for users to migrate; the per-kind enable toggles + margins that came and went during this dev cycle never shipped in a release. `WeaponScorer` emits a companion mods line for the dashboard.

---

## Looting reliability

- **Hung loot session watchdog** — a loot session with no progress (no pickup / drain / tx) for 30s is cancelled so the bot can't get pinned crouched forever.
- **Dead-teammate recovery** — when a member dies, the squad re-evaluates the extract decision; if surviving loot drops below the recomputed threshold the extract is cancelled, and the squad bee-lines to the corpse to recover the gear once it registers.
- **Guard-on-loot-POI unstick** — a bot that lands in GuardAction on a loot POI without ever entering Looting (arrival check failed on radius / LoS) is blacklisted + re-dispatched after 5s instead of idling.
- **Own-kill bee-line gated** — only PMC / PlayerScav / bot-scav squads bee-line to their own kills; Goons / bosses / cultists / raiders no longer get pinned on a corpse they can't loot.
- **Corpse interaction distance tightened** — corpse arrival caps at 2.5m (containers / loose loot keep 4m) so bots don't kneel-loot a body across the room.

## Doors

- **Door opening rework** — bots actually open doors instead of phasing through them. Movement holds for the animation window after firing the interaction (the open animation is cancelled by movement input otherwise), the bot is prepped into the right state, a validated `Door.Interact` result is used, and a per-door cooldown stops the re-fire-every-frame no-op.
- **Forward-ray + collider approach detection** — replaces the old path-segment test that missed ~80% of doors (and off-axis approaches).
- **DoorWatch diagnostic** — tracks every interaction; logs success / phantom-walk / timeout and settles a stuck `Interacting` door back to `Shut` so it isn't left dead for the rest of the raid.
- **Accepted door-state desync** — bot interactions never finalize BSG's door state; the watch settles it. The close-doors-behind stuck-remediation was repaired to work under that desync.
- **World-side unlock at grant** — when the unlock roll wins, the door is unlocked immediately so the navmesh link opens *before* the dispatch path is computed (previously the bot routed around the building to a window and never reached locked-room loot).

## Movement, dispatch & multi-floor

- **Multi-floor looting** — cells are cleaned one floor at a time (committed floor per squad), Quest waypoints are exempt from the floor filter, and a ping-pong livelock in `PickFromCell` was fixed.
- **Same-floor roam splinters** + a configurable **cross-floor chance** (default 20%) so bots loot a floor without vacuuming it, then drift up/down naturally instead of yo-yoing the staircases.
- **Synthetic patrol legs** — patrol-point arrival radius tightened to 5m (decoupled from the cover-scan radius) and a minimum-hop requirement, so bots actually walk *to* patrol points instead of "arriving" the instant one is picked.
- **Leader roam continuation** — a leader who finished the squad anchor during roam chains onto a splinter instead of guarding beside it, without disturbing teammates' targets.
- **Arrival-failure grace window** — a Guard→Goto transition no longer fails arrival in the first few frames before the bot has started moving (which used to 3-fail-blacklist POIs instantly).
- **Dispatch-loop fixes** on unreachable / value-skipped POIs.
- **Squad-teardown cache clear** — corpse-kill credits + reachability cache are cleared when an empty squad is removed, so a recycled squad id can't inherit stale state and bee-line across walls.
- **Orient toward loot target** on session start.

## Exfil

- **Extract reliability** — arrival now requires being physically inside the exfil trigger collider (not just within the loose radius); a 15s force-extract timer despawns a bot stuck within radius but outside the trigger (underground hatches); the navmesh sample is biased into the trigger volume; Goto keeps priority at the exfil so Guard can't steal the bot and freeze the timer.

## SAIN personality

- **Brain-lookup fix** + per-agent extract-threshold fallback when SAIN hasn't resolved an archetype.
- **Resolve deadline counted from first member activation** (30s) instead of squad registration — fixes every PMC squad locking to Average during long map loads.
- **2nd-raid-of-session fix** — the cached `BotManagerComponent` is now invalidated when the GameWorld changes, so brain resolution works on every raid of a session (the cache used to hand back the previous raid's dead manager).
- **PlayerScav** extract-trigger + splinter-dispatch oscillation fixed.

## Player convergence (restored)

The advection **player-convergence pull** is back, ported from the original **Phobos** mod by **Janky** (full credit to them for the design): each grid cell gets a vector toward the living human player(s), refreshed every 30s, folded into dispatch. Per-map ranges live in the Maps/Zones JSON (optional key, falls back to compiled defaults). New F12 **master toggle, default OFF**, plus radius / force scales (negative force pushes bots away).

## Faction-mod coexistence

- **"Vanilla X" toggles renamed** to "Disable ORBIT on X" (clearer; same polarity).
- **Vanilla Raiders** opt-out toggle added (pmcBot + exUsec).
- **ISB faction** taken over by default (toggle to opt out); detected via its `samc137.ISBinfo` plugin, matched as a substring so a prefixed variant still registers, and the single "ISB" role substring covers all its WildSpawnTypes.

author: hramaros
body:
## Summary
This PR adds category-based filtering to the image gallery, allowing users to filter images by category through an auto-generated filter chip UI. Categories are extracted from the data and displayed as interactive buttons, with counts for each category.

## Key Changes

- **Category data extraction**: Added `category` field to the data normalization pipeline in `app.js`
- **Filter UI generation**: Implemented `buildFilters()` function that:
  - Extracts unique categories from items and counts occurrences
  - Generates interactive filter chips with category counts
  - Sorts categories alphabetically (with "Autre" always last)
  - Hides the filter bar entirely if no category data exists
- **Filter logic**: Updated `applyFilter()` to respect both search query and active category selection
- **Visual display**: 
  - Added category badges on gallery cards (`.card-cat`)
  - Added category display in lightbox modal (`.lb-cat`)
  - Styled filter chips with active state and hover effects
- **Configuration**: Added `allCategoriesLabel` config option and `category` field mapping in `config.js`
- **HTML structure**: Added filter navigation container and category elements to card and lightbox templates
- **Documentation**: Updated README with category filtering explanation and n8n workflow notes

## Implementation Details

- Categories are displayed as styled chips with counts; clicking a chip filters the gallery and regenerates the UI to reflect the new active state
- The filter bar is dynamically hidden if no categories are present in the data
- Category matching is case-sensitive and trims whitespace
- The "All categories" chip always appears first and shows the total item count
- Active category state is validated when data is reloaded; if the active category no longer exists, it resets to "All"

author: iainchesworth
body:
Saves the multi-agent CI/CD redesign analysis and lands its two safest, highest-value steps.

**Docs**
- `docs/cicd-redesign.md` — the full build-once redesign plan AND an adversarial critique that corrects its over-claims (the "13->3 builds" headline is really ~13->7; assembly-only Docker rests on an undocumented runner-OS==base ABI coupling; scanners can't reuse prebuilt build trees). Read the critique before implementing later phases.

**Phase 0 — CTest labels** (`test/CMakeLists.txt`)
- Label the three suites unit/integration/perf so `ctest -L unit` (fast, PR/local) and `-L integration` are gateable. Directly targets the regression that first-failed at *release* instead of in CI. Pure CMake, no behaviour change until a `-L` filter is wired into the ctest step (deferred).

**Phase 1 — OS-keyed vcpkg cache** (`.github/actions/setup-vcpkg-cache/action.yml`)
- Key the vcpkg **binary** cache by runner OS instead of the per-job prefix, collapsing the four disjoint same-triplet caches (Linux GCC / CodeQL / SonarCloud / MSVCAnalysis) into one. The critique calls this the highest-true-value change. `cache-key-prefix` kept as an accepted-but-ignored input for back-compat (no caller changes needed).

Later phases (reusable `_build.yml`, assembly-only Docker, scanner consolidation, versioning automation) are intentionally **not** in this PR — they need the critique's fixes first.

author: tank-operator-host[bot]
body:
## Summary

Non-restricted sessions (`TANK_RESTRICTED_GIT` false/unset) are trusted workspaces and should have **full, automatic git access** — `clone`/`fetch`/`pull`/`push` to any repo the session's installation can reach, with no manual token handling. Restricting git is the opt-in (`TANK_RESTRICTED_GIT=true`) governed mode, not the default.

They had no working git auth at all: `repo-cloner` always wrote an empty `credential.helper` into the cloned repo's `.git/config` (an empty value *clears* the helper list), and no credential helper was ever wired up, so `git push` fell through to a TTY prompt and failed. Pre-storm "free access" was simply the `mint_clone_token` MCP tool being ungated — there was never a baked credential path.

## Changes
- **New `k8s/session-config/git-credential-tank.sh`** — a git credential helper. On each git op it mints a short-lived, repo-scoped GitHub App token via the in-pod `mcp-github` MCP (`127.0.0.1:9992`), authenticated with the pod's projected `auth.romaine.life` SA token, requesting the App's full permission set. Fails closed off-github / on error. Grants nothing the session can't already mint through MCP; it removes the manual step.
- **`install-agent-git-template.sh`** is now mode-aware (already called by both runner-launch scripts, already branches on `TANK_RESTRICTED_GIT`): restricted → governed hook templates (post-commit auto-publish + pre-push block), unchanged; **non-restricted → install the helper to an executable path and set `credential.helper` + `credential.useHttpPath=true` globally.**
- **`repo-cloner.sh`** — the `credential.helper ""` scrub is now gated to restricted mode only, so non-restricted clones inherit the global helper instead of having it clobbered.
- **`k8s/templates/session-configmap.yaml`** — ship the helper in the `tank-session-config` ConfigMap (mounted whole-dir at `/opt/tank/session-config/`, so no `sessionConfigMounts` change needed).
- **`docs/features/session-lifecycle/capabilities.md`** — new "Non-Restricted Session Full Git Access" capability entry.

## Testing
- `go test ./cmd/tank-operator -run 'TestInstallAgentGitTemplate|TestGitCredentialTankHelper|TestInstallAgentPostCommit|TestSessionPodBootstrapScript'` — all PASS, including the new `TestInstallAgentGitTemplateScriptInstallsCredentialHelperOutsideRestrictedGit` and `TestGitCredentialTankHelperMintsToken` (mint request shape + SSE parsing + non-github bail), and the existing restricted-mode hook test still green.
- `helm template tank-operator ./k8s` renders with the new ConfigMap key.
- `bash -n` on all changed/new scripts.
- **Live in a non-restricted session pod**: ran the new `install-agent-git-template.sh` for both modes against isolated HOMEs (non-restricted wires the helper + it mints; restricted installs hooks only), then exercised the helper end-to-end — `git fetch`, `git push` (this PR's branch was pushed through the helper), across `tank-operator`, `glimmung`, `auth`, `mcp-github`, `infra-bootstrap`, `mcp-azure-personal`.

## Feature Contracts

Affected contracts:
- [x] **Session Lifecycle** — non-restricted git access capability; the governed restricted-git publish path is unchanged. New durable behavior documented in `session-lifecycle/capabilities.md`.
- [x] **Agent Runners** — session-side git setup: the runner-launch git-template step now installs the credential helper for non-restricted sessions; restricted sessions keep the governed hooks.

Evidence:
- `TestInstallAgentGitTemplateScriptInstallsCredentialHelperOutsideRestrictedGit`: non-restricted ⇒ `credential.helper` + `useHttpPath=true` set, helper installed executable, no governed hooks.
- `TestInstallAgentGitTemplateScriptRunsUnderSh`: restricted ⇒ governed post-commit + pre-push hooks installed, `init.templateDir` set (unchanged behavior).
- `TestGitCredentialTankHelperMintsToken`: helper requests `mint_clone_token` with `full:true` scoped to the requested repo, parses the SSE-framed MCP reply, returns `x-access-token`, and emits nothing for non-github hosts.
- Live push of this branch through the helper from a non-restricted session.

## Notes
- Scope choice: the helper mints the App's **full** permission set (the "full admin token" intent). One-line change to right-size to `write+workflows` if preferred.
- Existing pods are not retrofitted (session lifecycle: no pod resurrection); this applies to sessions created after the chart bump.
- Full test-slot validation is currently blocked by a separate glimmung-runner RBAC bug (cannot create the `*-session-readonly` ClusterRoleBinding after #1209) — tracked separately, not a dependency of this change.

author: cbebot
body:
## What

Rebuilds the customer wallet (`/wallet`) and its inner pages from a generic
dashboard-card layout into a **private-bank money console** — now that payments
are live. The company flagged the old wallet as "extremely poor"; it had been
left thin because payments weren't real yet.

## Main wallet (`/wallet`)

- **WalletVault** — engraved-onyx statement header. Available balance in NGN
  (the settlement truth) with an honest *"≈ in your currency"* approximate line;
  a **green breathing "Synced"** indicator when live, **calm amber "On hold"**
  when frozen; strong minted-gold + frosted-metal action buttons.
- **BalanceTrend** — running balance over time from `balance_after_kobo` (inline
  SVG, no charting dependency) — data that was previously unused.
- **CashflowPanel** — money **in *and* out** over 30 days (the old strip only
  counted debits).
- **StatementLedger** — date-grouped (Today / Yesterday / dated), filterable
  (All / In / Out), with the running balance per row.
- **FrozenBanner** — honest wallet-on-hold state (`frozen_at` / `frozen_reason`).

## Inner pages (`/wallet/funding`, `/wallet/withdrawals`, `/wallet/funding/[id]`)

- New **WalletPageHeader** (refined editorial header) replaces the generic hero.
- Fixed the banned **"instantly"** copy and an **invisible-on-light "View proof"
  button** (the onyx-only ghost class rendered white-on-white on a light surface).

## Multi-currency (display only)

NGN-kobo stays the settlement truth. New server-only `lib/wallet-currency.ts` is
decimal-correct (incl. 0-decimal currencies) and returns `null` → NGN-only when
no live rate is available — it never fabricates a rate. The FX converter is now
re-exported from `@henryco/pricing`.

> ⚠️ The foreign line is **dormant until `OPENRATE_APP_ID`** (alias
> `OPEN_EXCHANGE_RATES_APP_ID`) is set on the account Vercel project. Until then
> the wallet shows NGN only with "Wallet settlement is in NGN." — no fake rates.

## Safety

- **Read-only over money**: renders server-confirmed kobo only; no client-side
  balance math; the idempotent top-up reconciler stays the only write (once per
  load). Kept the per-read `allSettled` resilience barriers.

## Verification

- `typecheck`, `lint`, `pnpm tone:check`, `pnpm i18n:check:strict` — all green.
- Verified visually in **light, dark, and mobile** (engraved vault, green/amber
  states, strong buttons, statement, inner-page headers).

## Notes / follow-ups

- Wallet copy locale overrides (fr/es/pt/ar/de/it) for the new strings still to
  add — they fall back to EN at runtime today and the i18n gate passes.
- Payment / serious-action **email engine** is a separate piece (not in this PR).

- `value_for(kind,base,sym,addend)`: the 8-byte store value (Relative=B+A, Sym=S+A).
- `apply(ctx, rela, count, resolve)` [freestanding]: write each RELA in place at `base+r_offset` — RELATIVE/GLOB_DAT/JUMP_SLOT/ABS64/64 via `value_for`, IRELATIVE by calling the `(base+addend)` resolver, COPY by memcpy of `st_size` bytes. Symbols resolve through the global link-map scope (interposition) → local def → 0 for weak-undef → `Err(reloc idx)`. TLS deferred to G12f.

Also fixes a clippy `contains` lint in `linkmap.rs` that slipped through #1870 — my `ldso/src` warning grep was structurally broken (the message line precedes the `-->` path line); verification corrected.

Pure classify/value math is hosted-tested; the in-place apply is verified by the dynamic-run harness (PR 3/3: entry asm + xtask harness).

Gate: `cargo test -p ldso` (26 pass), clippy clean default+freestanding both -gnu arches, spec-lint clean.

body:
## What

Resolves the Dependabot **moderate** alert [GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93) — *PostCSS XSS via unescaped `</style>` in CSS stringify output* (affects `<8.5.10`). Adds `postcss: ^8.5.10` to `overrides`.

## Why an override

The top-level `postcss` was already `8.5.15`; the flagged copy was an older `8.4.31` bundled under the Next/Tailwind toolchain. The override lifts every copy to `8.5.x` — a within-major bump, low risk.

## Risk

Build-time dependency processing **our own** CSS (Tailwind), never attacker-controlled — not exploitable in this app. The fix is cheap and clears the alert.

## Verification

- `npm audit`: postcss **clean**, all copies `8.5.15`. Moderate count 4 → 2.
- `next build`: succeeds (Tailwind/postcss pipeline intact).
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean. `vitest run`: 13/13.

## Not fixed (intentional)

`uuid <11.1.1` (moderate, [GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq)) via `exceljs` is left as-is: exceljs only calls `uuid` **v4 without a `buf`**, so the vulnerable v3/v5/v6 code path is unreachable, and the only available fix is a risky major override of exceljs's transitive `uuid@8` → `11`. Not worth the regression risk on `.xlsx` generation for a non-exploitable issue.

## What

Implements the optimisation-model + control-design decisions from the design thread,
the UI slice that surfaces them, and the doc that records them
(`docs/optimization-and-ux.md`). **53 Python tests pass; the wireframe harness
(`project/test-merged.mjs`) passes.**

## Engine (`smartplate/`)

- **Nutrition is a band, not a point** — calories free inside ±tol, overshoot < undershoot,
  protein a one-sided floor; `nutrition.shortfall` for the gap. (`domain/nutrition.py`)
- **Mode = objective vs constraint** — `config.MODE_META` (objective / what-gives /
  kcal tolerance / plain-language outcome, surfaced via `/api/meta`).
- **Magic numbers killed** — cook cap + effort overridable per user; carbon truly off
  at `carbon_pref == 0`.
- **Rating footgun** — optional soft ★ above a hard safety floor (flag, default hard);
  substitution never drops below the user's chosen ★.
- **Budget recommender** — `kernel/recommender.py`: Floor / Usual / Variety bands,
  expected surge priced in, suggested ★ floor, one-off support; `/api/plan/<id>/recommend-budget`.
- **Novelty/variety model** — `domain/fatigue.py` (familiar/novel pools + levels) and a
  **gated** novelty nudge in the solve (`SMARTPLATE_VARIETY=on`, off by default).
- **Feasibility/shortfall diagnostic** on every solve.
- **"I made X" lookup** — `domain/intake.py` parses free text → nutrition estimate
  (matched/unmatched + confidence); `POST /api/intake`.

## UI / wireframe

- Canonical Mifflin activity factors (5 levels).
- **Slider cull**: 5 priority sliders → one mode dial (money ⇄ everything-else) + 2 leans;
  Taste slider dropped (learned). Setup grouped as **Locks / Dials / Rules**.
- **Variety**: level control + novel **✦** marking (not V/U — see below) + a
  "⭐ usual · ✦ new" week chip; **budget-recommender card** + a mode-outcome line.

## On V/U badges (the open question)

Rejected. Badging the "usual" majority is noise, and a literal "V" collides with
veg/vegan. We mark **only the new picks** with a subtle **✦**, plus one week-level
"⭐ usual · ✦ new" chip tied to the variety level and the rate-to-train loop.

## Still open (small)

Persisting `intake` results into the rolling nutrition ledger — lands with the
ledger build (SPEC §1). A *hard* variety composition-constraint (vs the current soft
gated nudge) remains an option.

## Why

The `dev → main` promotion (#634) is conflicted (`mergeable_state: dirty`) — `dev` and `main` diverged at the **v4.1.0 back-merge (#558)**, leaving a `package.json` version conflict (`main` `4.1.0` vs `dev` `4.6.6-dev.0`).

This merges `main` into `dev` to reconcile the histories, which makes #634 a clean merge.

## Safety — history-only, zero content change

A full merge of `main` into `dev` produces **zero net file changes** (`git diff origin/dev` is empty): `dev` is already a complete content-superset of `main`. `main`'s 571 SHA-distinct commits are old merge/squash history, not unique code. So:

- ✅ Nothing from `main` is lost (there was no unique content to lose)
- ✅ Nothing stale enters `dev` (tree is byte-identical to current `dev`)
- ✅ `package.json` stays at `dev`'s `4.6.6-dev.0` (the only conflict, resolved in `dev`'s favor)

## Effect

Once merged, `main` becomes an ancestor of `dev`, so **#634 (`dev → main`) drops its conflict** and can be merged (after `pnpm github:sync` enables the admin-bypass).

## Summary
This PR replaces the Memory game station (S18) with a new Arkanoid game station, while keeping Memory available only as a bonus game. The Arkanoid game is refactored to support both bonus mode (single 45-second round) and station mode (progressive multi-round gameplay).

## Key Changes

- **Removed S18 Memory station**: Replaced with Arkanoid station (`sarkanoid`) featuring ball & paddle gameplay
- **Refactored `arkanoidGame()` function**: Now accepts an `opts` parameter to support two modes:
  - **Bonus mode** (no opts): Single 45-second timed round, awards +2 XP per brick destroyed
  - **Station mode** (opts.station): Three progressive rounds with increasing brick counts and ball speed; completion of all rounds completes the station
- **Progressive difficulty**: Station mode increases ball speed by 18% per round and adds more bricks in later rounds
- **Updated station registry**: Changed station ID from `s18` to `sarkanoid` with new icon (🧱) and description

author: barnabasj
body:
## Problem

`AddDefaultPolicies` adds the read/write/destroy policies with `type: :append`,
but the generic-action (`action_type(:action)`) policy is added **without** it —
so Spark's `add_entity` default (`:prepend`) places the generated grant policy
**before** the resource's own `policies`. For a generic action a failing grant
then forbids it **before a user `bypass` is ever evaluated**.

This bites any `default_policies: true` resource with a user bypass on a generic
action — e.g. an `AshOban`/system bypass:

```elixir
oban do
  scheduled_actions do
    schedule :prune, "0 3 * * *" do action :prune end
  end
end

policies do
  bypass AshOban.Checks.AshObanInteraction do
    authorize_if always()
  end
end
```

The nightly `:prune` worker runs with no actor + the AshOban interaction context,
but is discarded with `Ash.Error.Forbidden`: the prepended `action_type(:action)`
grant policy fails (no grant for a nil actor) before the bypass runs. The policy
breakdown shows the bypass as `?` (never reached).

## Fix

Add the generic-action policy with `type: :append`, exactly like the
read/write/destroy policies above it, so user `bypass` policies take precedence
(which is what the module docstring already promises).

```diff
-    {:ok, Transformer.add_entity(dsl_state, [:policies], generic_policy)}
+    {:ok, Transformer.add_entity(dsl_state, [:policies], generic_policy, type: :append)}
```

## Test

Adds regression coverage to `AshGrant.DefaultPoliciesTest`: a user
`bypass action(:privileged)` on the `Article` test resource (which grants no
permission for `:privileged`) now authorizes a no-grant / nil actor — it was
forbidden before the fix.

Targeting `claude/fervent-bhabha-f3e38f` (PR #6) since that's the branch we build
on downstream; the same bug is on `main`, so this can retarget to `main` if you
prefer.

author: chris17453
body:
The rtld now supports runtime loading; **G12 (the full dynamic linker) is done.**

**ldso (link.rs):**
- `_dl_open(path,mode)`: search (saved LD_LIBRARY_PATH) / open / map / build the objview, BFS its DT_NEEDED, relocate the new range against the full scope, run init; returns a handle (object index + 1).
- `_dl_sym(handle,name)`: resolve in the handle's object, or whole-scope for RTLD_DEFAULT(0). `_dl_close` (refcount unmap is a follow-up). `_dl_addr` (find the object containing an address).
- CRITICAL: the rtld adds **itself** to the resolution scope (`rtld_objview` from AT_BASE + its `_DYNAMIC`) so `libc.so.6`'s `_dl_*` references bind to the rtld's exports.

**glibc (dlfcn/mod.rs):** dlopen/dlsym/dlclose/dlerror/dladdr thin-wrap the rtld's `_dl_*` + RTLD_* constants + Dl_info. Static links that never call dlopen drop these via `--gc-sections` so the externs don't break a static link.

**HARNESS:** `foo.c`→`libfoo.so` + `dlopen_pie.c` (`dlopen("libfoo.so")`+`dlsym("foo")`) through our ld → **exit 99**. `xtask ldso --check` now runs 4 end-to-end smokes: raw_pie 42, libc.so.6-linked 13, tls 7, dlopen 99.

Gate: `cargo test` -p ldso (39) + -p glibc (60), clippy clean default+freestanding both -gnu arches (ldso + glibc + xtask), spec-lint clean, `xtask ldso --check` 4 smokes PASS, `xtask glibc --check` static smoke exit 0.

**G12 sub-ladder a–h all complete.** Next: G13 (net).

author: bhanunuthakki
body:
## What

S4 of the **capture-every-number** program: de-allowlist the IR-spreadsheet path so the issuer's own audited supplemental spreadsheet — the highest-fidelity numeric source — lands **every** data row in `kpi_facts` at the `IR_DOC` tier, and remove the historically **NU-only** ceiling by auto-building `ir_config` for any ticker with a discoverable IR spreadsheet.

## How

A `SheetKpi` now carries `origin` (`"analyst"` | `"capture"`) and `exact_label`:

- **analyst** rows — the curated holdings tier KPIs, LLM-mapped to canonical names (unchanged), substring-matched.
- **capture** rows — the long tail: enumerated deterministically from the sheet (no LLM gate decides which rows survive), unit/scale from a conservative heuristic classifier, footnotes / FMP line items filtered, matched `exact_label` (a bare `NII` can't grab `Risk-adjusted NII`), and routed through **S1's `canonical_metric_name`** at **ingest** time so each joins an existing series or mints a clean `origin='capture'` definition.

Key pieces:
- `config_builder.widen_config` adds the capture layer to an existing (hand-built) config while preserving its analyst rows **verbatim** — the NU regression guard. `build_ir_config` emits both layers (capture-only, no LLM call, when a ticker has no holdings).
- `ingest.py` canonicalizes capture labels, threads a per-name `origins` map through `persist_manifest` → `find_or_create_kpi_definition`, and keeps the existing `_supersede_llm_incumbents` so an audited `IR_DOC` value **supersedes** S3's broad LLM value for the same metric (tier precedence).
- `refresh_ir_kpis.py` widens before ingest; `refresh_ir_kpis_all.py` refreshes the **union** of configured tickers (`--discover`) and tickers with an on-disk IR spreadsheet (bootstrapped via `--file`).

## Verification (real data — prod-DB copy upgraded to head)

- **NU regression**: the four curated analyst series are **byte-for-byte unchanged** after the widened ingest.
- **NU capture**: **210** capture definitions / **2515** facts land at `IR_DOC` tier (`origin='capture'`, `extracted_by='ir_spreadsheet'`).
- **New ticker**: a brand-new ticker with no holdings/config auto-configures **214** capture-only metrics — the NU-only ceiling is gone.

## Tests

- `tests/test_ir_capture.py` — config round-trip (origin/exact_label + legacy default), row enumeration, exact-label disambiguation, unit/scale classifier, footnote/FMP filtering, `widen_config` preserves-analyst + idempotence, capture-only build with no LLM call.
- `tests/test_ir_spreadsheet_ingest.py` — end-to-end ingest: capture at IR_DOC/`origin='capture'`, curated series not disturbed, capture reuses an existing series via canonicalization, IR_DOC value supersedes the LLM incumbent.
- `tests/test_refresh_ir_kpis_all.py` — spreadsheet-only ticker bootstrapped via `--file`, configured ticker still `--discover`, union/sort, skip rules, disk scan.

Lint (ruff) and type-check (pyright) clean on touched files; no new baseline errors.

- Removes false interactive `cursor: pointer` affordance from static `.card` elements.

Static layout elements (like the dashboard "System Health" cards) were showing misleading pointer cursors and interactive hover states, confusing users about what was clickable. ## Build 102 / v2.2.0 — 房间消息持久化 + 我在的房间订阅 + 通知系统

Adapts the SQL-shaped spec to the actual stack (MongoDB/Mongoose, no Redis; reuses the existing notify()/NotificationPreference infra).

### A. Message persistence (per-room retention)
- Dropped the fixed 7-day `WorldChatMessage` TTL → cron-driven retention.
- `ChatRoom.retentionDays` 7 / **30 (default)** / 0 = 无限 (Premium).
- `roomMessageSweep` (every 6h): official/virtual lobby rooms keep ~24h (live-focused); custom rooms keep their `retentionDays`.
- `emptyRoomSweep` cold window 3d→**30d**, skips 无限 rooms, cascades memberships.
- `dropLegacyTTL` at boot drops the old `createdAt_1` TTL index (idempotent).

### B. Leave-room confirmation (`RoomExitConfirmSheet`)
- Backing out of a non-owner custom room → **保留(继续接收通知) / 离开 / 取消** via `beforeRemove`. Owner & official rooms skip.

### C. ✨ 我在的房间 + unread
- `JoinedRoomsSection` on the Plaza 热门 tab: per-row 静音 toggle, 离开 button, unread badge. Unlimited subscriptions.
- Auto-subscribe owner on create, members on join/enter.

### D. Global room-notification toggle
- 房间消息 toggle in NotificationSettings (default ON) → `world_chat_message` opt-out. Two-layer gate: per-room mute × global pref × quiet hours.

### E. Backend
- `RoomMembership` model; endpoints: `GET /rooms/joined`, `POST /rooms/:id/enter`, `POST /rooms/:id/mark-read`, `PATCH/DELETE /rooms/:id/membership`, `retentionDays` in `PATCH /rooms/:id`.
- Room-message push fan-out in `/send` (un-muted subscribers, skips sender + reply/@mention).

### F. Client
- `api/worldChat`: getJoinedRooms / enterRoom / markRoomRead / setRoomNotifications / leaveRoomMembership; `JoinedRoom` type.
- i18n en/zh/ja/ko.

### Validation
- Backend: `node -c` + require-load of app/routes/jobs ✅ (29 worldChat routes).
- Client: `tsc --noEmit` clean for all touched files ✅ (2 remaining errors are pre-existing in `localChat.ts`, identical on origin/main).

author: michaelcrosato
body:
## What this does
This is **"model switching"** — using a stronger model for the riskiest work and a cost-efficient one for routine work. It builds on the previous PR, which made the model policy actually control each agent's model.

How model choice works here (important): you can't change a sub-agent's model on a per-call basis in the CLI / GitHub Actions lanes — the model is fixed by the agent's definition file. So "switching" means **picking which builder to use**:

- **High-risk work (Tier C)** — security/auth/crypto, irreversible actions (database migrations, deploys, IAM), novel architecture, concurrency — now builds with a new **`builder-strong`** agent on the most capable model (opus). It also carries a stricter contract: stop-and-ask on ambiguous security details, and add abuse-case/negative tests.
- **Routine work (Tier A/B)** continues on the standard **`builder`** (sonnet), which was also cleaned of leftover jargon.
- The loop (`/work`) now reads the feature's tier and spawns the matching builder. The triage rubric and the ops plan were updated so all the docs agree; the "model selection (later)" promise in the rubric is now actually wired.

Because the previous PR's gate enforces "each agent's model must match policy," `builder-strong` is locked to its policy model automatically — the shipped config has 6 agent bindings and zero drift.

## How to see it
- New file `.claude/agents/builder-strong.md`; `.claude/model-policy.json` now lists `builder-strong` under the reasoning tier.
- `.claude/skills/work/SKILL.md` step 3 (BUILD) shows the Tier C → builder-strong / A·B → builder routing; `TASK_AUTONOMY_TRIAGE.md` §2/§7 match.

## What could be risky
No enforcement code changes — this is agent/skill/config behavior plus docs. The change only sends **harder, higher-stakes** features to a **stronger** model (a safety improvement); routine features are unchanged. A new contract test guards the actual intent (the Tier-C builder must resolve to a *different* model than the default), and it's written model-agnostically so a future model rename won't break it.

## Machine checks
- `bash scripts/verify.sh` → **VERIFY: PASS (exit 0)**; model-policy drift gate green (6 bindings); **308** contract tests (+2 F-MP2).
- Reviewed by a fresh-context **evaluator** (behavior/config + docs, no enforcement surface — same review class as the earlier skill de-fluffs).

author: odanree
body:
## Summary

GitHub silently rejected every issue creation from `GitHubIssueSink` when the check name was long. Caught by trying to file the v0.2.0 audit findings from oc-realestate-intel — every POST returned 422, the sink caught and logged the exception (by design), and the operator saw a clean CLI exit with no issue actually filed.

## Root cause

The label scheme was `governance:<check_name>:<fingerprint>`. For an `audit.prompt_lacks_refusal_language` finding with a 12-char fingerprint, that's 59 chars — over GitHub's hard 50-char limit on label names. Returns 422 Unprocessable Entity.

Same problem would hit any custom check whose name is long. The runtime checks shipped in v0.1 happened to have short names (`disclaimer`, `url_allowlist`, `prompt_injection`), so it never surfaced — until the audit CLI started emitting `audit.<rule_id_lowercase>` check names.

## Fix

- Dedup label is now `gov:<fingerprint>` (always 16 chars). Still uniquely identifies a finding because the fingerprint already hashes from `check_name + inputs`.
- Per-check categorization label `governance:<check_name>` is preserved, with a defensive truncation to 50 chars on overflow.
- Two new tests assert both labels stay under the cap regardless of check-name length.
- One existing test updated to match the new label shape inside the POST body.

## Test plan

- [x] **78/78 green** (76 pre-existing + 2 new label-cap tests)
- [x] Manually retried filing the oc-realestate-intel audit finding (will land after merge + tag).

author: paudley
body:
## Summary
Implements a reusable notation-projection layer so that the Music extension can declare how each notation system maps into and out of GMEOW with explicit, honest accounting for loss and parameter semantics.

Closes #318.

## What changed

- **New core slice** `slices/core/notation/`:
  - `manifest.ttl` — declares the slice, tier `core`, dependency on `core`, consumer `music`, and module abstract.
  - `module.ttl` — adds `gmeow:NotationProjectionProfile`, `gmeow:ProjectionLoss`, `gmeow:notationSystem`, `gmeow:sourceParameter`, `gmeow:targetParameter`, `gmeow:projectionLoss`, `gmeow:lossKind`, `gmeow:symbolicLossRate`, `gmeow:timeSemantics`, `gmeow:parameterCompleteness`, and individuals for common music notation systems (Common Western Notation, Mensural notation, Graphic notation, Lead sheet, Tablature) plus loss kinds (`Lossless`, `Partial`, `NearTotal`, `Ambiguous`).
  - `shapes.ttl` — SHACL shapes enforcing profile completeness, valid loss rates, and honest declaration of time semantics and parameter completeness.
  - `docs.md` — module documentation and design rationale.

- **Music extension updated** `slices/extensions/music/`:
  - `manifest.ttl` — added dependency on `core/notation`.
  - `module.ttl` — added projection profiles for each notation system used by `music:Piece` instances, linking them via `gmeow:notationSystem` and declaring `gmeow:projectionLoss`.
  - `tests/test_music_notation_projection.py` — 6 competency tests covering profile completeness, loss accounting, no arbitrary subclasses, and honesty assertions for mensural and graphic notation.

- **Mapping DSL** `dsl/mappings/music-notation-projection.ttl`:
  - `gmeow:ProjectionMapping` cells from CWN, Mensural, Graphic, Lead-sheet, and Tablature to their GMEOW profiles.
  - `gmeow:TermEquivalence` rows for each notation system and loss kind.
  - FnO function declarations in `dsl/mappings/transforms.fno.ttl` for symbolic-loss-rate normalization, pitch-class preservation, duration-preservation, and tablature-fret-to-pitch projection.

- **Generated artifacts refreshed** via `make regenerate`:
  - `generated/mappings/` SSSOM/EDOAL/projection-query updates
  - `generated/statements/` RDF 1.2 + OWL statement artifacts
  - `generated/module-status.md` now lists the notation slice

## Verification

- `make check-generated` — no drift, no orphans (18/18 generators match).
- `pytest slices/extensions/music/tests/test_music_notation_projection.py` — 6/6 passed.
- Full `make check` passes lint, validate, compile, ELK reason, HermiT reason, verify, and fast tests.

## Known pre-existing failures on main

Two targets are failing on `origin/main` independently of this branch and are not introduced here:

- `make audit` fails because `tests/fixtures/coverage/hallucination-kg.ttl` triggers a SHACL violation from an external ontology term.
- `make test-fast` fails on `test_external_ontology_catalog_has_specific_descriptions` because generated ontology-docs catalog descriptions are generic placeholders.

create and approve pull requests" so future Version PRs open automatically.

`black .` met 26.5.1 → **61 files** puur geformatteerd (jaarstijl 25→26, o.a. compactere gewrapte string-args). **Geen functionele wijzigingen.** Gescheiden van commit 1 per git-workflow-regel.

author: jakechampion
body:
The keystone the trait-spine epic (#2691) needs. A trait may now take type parameters, referenced in its method signatures; each impl binds them positionally:

```fern
trait From[T] { function from(v: T): Self; }
struct Celsius { deg: i32 }
impl From[i32] for Celsius { function from(v: i32): Self { return Celsius { deg: v }; } }
var c: Celsius = Celsius.from(20);

trait Container[T] { function get(self: Self): T; }
impl Container[i32] for IntBox { function get(self: Self): i32 { return self.v; } }
```

This is the foundation for `From`/`Into`, `TryFrom`, `Collect`, and `?`-error conversion for arbitrary (non-`dyn`) error types.

## Changes
- **ast**: `TraitDecl.TypeParams`, `ImplDecl.TraitArgs`.
- **parser**: `[T,…]` after a trait name (decl) and after the trait name in an `impl` (args).
- **checker**: the conformance check binds the trait's type params to the impl's `TraitArgs` (`From[i32]` → `T=i32`) and substitutes them into the trait's method signatures (`substByName`, applied before the `Self`→impl-type substitution) before the structural compare. Wrong arity / mismatched bindings are rejected (`E021`). **Dispatch is unchanged** — calls resolve to the impl's concrete monomorphic method, so there are no IR/interp/codegen changes.
- **modload**: mangles struct/enum names in `TraitArgs` so cross-module `impl From[mod.Foo] for …` lines up.

## Tests
- **parser**: `TypeParams` / `TraitArgs` populated.
- **checker**: receiver-method + associated-function + two-param accepted; wrong-arity and mismatched-binding rejected.
- **e2e** (interp / x86-64 / arm64 / wasm): `Container[i32]` dispatch + `From[i32]` constructor → 90.
- Full trait / derive / supertrait / default-method / dyn / associated-types e2e suites remain green.
- `docs/TRAITS.md` gains a "Generic traits" section.

## Scope
Concrete trait arguments (`From[i32]`, `From[mod.Foo]`). **Follow-ups:** bounded generics over a generic trait (`f[T: From[i32]]`) and `dyn`-generic-traits — both need the `T: Trait` bound grammar extended to parse `Trait[args]`. Part of #2691.

author: chrisgleissner
body:
## Why

This repo holds **~708 GB of live GitHub Actions artifacts** (≈98% of the account's storage, against a 0.5 GB allowance). 91% is Playwright/E2E test evidence + nyc coverage uploaded on **every** CI run with the **default 90-day retention** and **no cleanup**. This PR stops the bleeding by capping `retention-days` per artifact class — **without changing any upload condition, test, the coverage scope/percentage, release deliverables, or failure-debuggability.**

> **The diff is purely additive: 93 insertions, 0 deletions — only `retention-days` lines plus one new cleanup workflow. No upload `if:` condition is changed anywhere.** This is deliberate (see "Why retention-only" below) and is why the repo's `tests/unit/ci/*WorkflowContracts.test.ts` suite still passes unchanged.

The one-time deletion of the existing ~708 GB backlog is handled separately (guarded dry-run → human review → throttled delete); the dry-run summary is below.

## Approach: classify every upload, then apply the minimal safe change

Each `actions/upload-artifact` step was classified by tracing the workflow graph for a matching `download-artifact` (by name or glob `pattern:`):

- **A — Hand-off** (consumed in-run by a later job) → **`retention-days: 1`**, condition untouched. In-run downloads happen immediately, so 1 day is always safe. The two dominant families are class A.
- **B — Terminal evidence** (not consumed) → **`retention-days: 7`**, condition untouched.
- **C — Release/publish** (APK/AAB/IPA/notices/Pages) → **`retention-days: 7`**, condition untouched (the GitHub Release is the source of truth).

### Why retention-only (two deliberate deviations from the generic remediation)

1. **Playwright capture modes left ON.** The generic advice (`screenshot: only-on-failure`, `video: retain-on-failure`) is **unsafe here**: `scripts/validate-playwright-evidence.mjs` (run in the `web-coverage-merge` job) **asserts** every evidence folder has a PNG + exactly one `video.webm`. Reducing capture would fail the merge job on green runs. (There are **no** `toHaveScreenshot`/`toMatchSnapshot` assertions, so nothing else depends on capture mode.)
2. **No `if: failure()` gating.** The repo has a `tests/unit/ci/*WorkflowContracts.test.ts` suite that **locks upload conditions** (e.g. `perfNightlyWorkflowContracts` asserts perf-nightly `if: always()` — "always uploads perf artifacts"). Gating uploads on failure would break those tests (constraints #1/#2) and remove evidence the maintainer deliberately keeps. **`retention-days` alone already yields ~97% reduction**, so conditions are left exactly as-is — which also means failure-debuggability is preserved *identically* to today (every red-run evidence path is byte-for-byte unchanged, only the retention window shrinks).

## Step 1 — Classification table (artifact → class → consumed-by → change)

| Workflow | Artifact name | Class | Consumed by (same run) | Condition (unchanged) | retention |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| android | `coverage-unit` | A | `web-coverage-merge` (name) | `always()` | 90→**1** |
| android | `web-dist-coverage` | A | `web-e2e`, `web-screenshots` (name) | unconditional | 90→**1** |
| android | `e2e-nyc-output-${shard}` | A | `web-coverage-merge` (`e2e-nyc-output-*`) | `always()` | 90→**1** |
| android | `playwright-evidence-e2e-${shard}` | A | `web-coverage-merge` (`playwright-evidence-*`) | `always()` | 90→**1** |
| android | `playwright-evidence-screenshots` | A | `web-coverage-merge` (`playwright-evidence-*`) | `always()` | 90→**1** |
| android | `playwright-evidence` (merged) | B | — | `always()` | 90→**7** |
| android | `hvsc-perf-quick` | B | — | `always()` | 90→**7** |
| android | `maestro-evidence` | B | — | `always()` | 90→**7** |
| android | `third-party-notices` | C | — | `always()` | 90→**7** |
| android | `*-release-apk` | C | `release-artifacts` + GitHub Release | tag&&keystore | 90→**7** |
| android | `*-release-aab` | C | `release-artifacts` + GitHub Release | tag&&keystore | 90→**7** |
| ios | `ios-prepared-workspace` | A | maestro + package jobs (name) | unconditional | 90→**1** |
| ios | `ios-maestro-evidence` | B | — | `always()` | 90→**7** |
| ios | `ios-maestro-evidence-tgz` | B | — | `always()&&tag` | 90→**7** |
| ios | `ios-maestro-failure` | B | — | `failure()` (already) | 90→**7** |
| ios | `ios-package-failure` | B | — | `failure()` (already) | 90→**7** |
| ios | `*-ios-ipa` | C | GitHub Release (`gh release upload`) | tag-job | 90→**7** |
| fuzz | `fuzz-test-artifacts` (28 GB) | B | — | `always()` | 90→**7** |
| fuzz | `fuzz-deterministic-artifacts` | B | — | `always()` | 90→**7** |
| web | `web-docker-telemetry-${platform}` | B | — | `always()` | 90→**7** |
| perf-nightly | `hvsc-perf-${profile}` | B | — | `always()` | 90→**7** |
| pages | `github-pages` (`upload-pages-artifact`) | C | `deploy-pages` (in-run) | — | **unchanged** (action defaults to 1-day; Pages deploy is source of truth) |

New file: **`.github/workflows/cleanup-artifacts.yaml`** — daily sweep of stale (>7d) **non-release** artifacts, `actions: write`, with a `dry_run` input. Insurance; touches no test.

## Step 3 — Proof nothing broke

**1. Workflow YAML valid (actionlint):** identical **4** pre-existing errors on `origin/main` and this branch — all the unrelated `use_pypi` input on `codecov/codecov-action@v5`. **Zero** new lint issues; `cleanup-artifacts.yaml` clean.

**2. Artifact graph still satisfied:** every `download-artifact` consumer resolves to a producer upload running unconditionally — and since **no condition changed**, this is trivially preserved. Mechanical check: 0 consumed artifacts gated on `failure()`.

**3. Workflow-contract tests pass:** the full `tests/unit/ci/*` suite + script tests run green against the modified workflows — **16 files / 71 tests passed**, including `perfNightlyWorkflowContracts`, `telemetryGateWorkflow`, `androidMaestroWorkflowContracts`, `validate-playwright-evidence`. (A purely-additive `retention-days` change touches no assertion.)

**4. Green CI run:** `android.yaml`/`web.yaml`/`ios.yaml` run on this PR (GitHub-hosted). **Proven on a real failing job:** when E2E shard 9 flaked, it **still uploaded** `playwright-evidence-e2e-9` (15 MB) and `e2e-nyc-output-9` (31 MB) with the new retention applied exactly (`created 2026-06-15` → `expires 2026-06-16` = 1 day) — confirming both the durable fix and that failure evidence is still captured.

**5. Test inventory & coverage unchanged:** the entire diff is `.github/workflows/**`. No test, matrix, shard count (12), threshold (`COVERAGE_MIN: 91`), or capture mode changed → identical test set & coverage %.

## Step 4 — Backlog cleanup dry-run (read-only; reviewed)

```

CUTOFF (5 days):           2026-06-10T08:05:22Z   (keep created_at >= cutoff)

DELETE set (class A/B, >5d old, non-release): 27,295 artifacts   670.2 GB
KEEP (release / class-C by name):              1,872 artifacts     5.24 GB
KEEP (newer than 5 days):                      1,177 artifacts    33.15 GB
(accounting: 27,295 + 1,872 + 1,177 = 30,344 == live ✓)

SAFETY ASSERTIONS:
[PASS] every DELETE row older than 5 days (max created 2026-06-10T07:06:30Z < cutoff)
[PASS] zero release/class-C artifacts in DELETE set (0 found)
[PASS] zero DELETE names resembling a release asset (apk/aab/ipa/release/notice/pages = 0)
KEPT release/class-C deliverables: third-party-notices(948), ios-ipa(461),
       c64commander-ios-ipa(347), c64commander-release-aab(58), c64commander-release-apk(58)
```

The delete touches `actions/artifacts` only — **never** GitHub Releases, tags, or release assets (each id is a 10-digit artifact id passed to `DELETE /actions/artifacts/{id}`; commit SHAs are 40-hex and structurally cannot be passed to that endpoint). All 83 releases verified present; re-verified after deletion.

body:
## Summary

Adds Article 13-oriented group ranking helpers while preserving the existing provisional ranking API and tests.

## Official rule scope

- Keeps `rank_group_table` and `build_group_table` as provisional helpers for existing smoke-test behavior.
- Adds `rank_group_table_article_13` and `build_group_table_article_13` for FIFA Article 13-oriented group ranking checks.
- Implements same-points resolution with head-to-head points, head-to-head goal difference, head-to-head goals scored, overall goal difference, overall goals scored, conduct score, and FIFA ranking fallback.

## Software fallback boundary

When FIFA ranking data is missing or teams remain tied after all available official criteria, team-name ordering is used only as a deterministic software fallback. It is explicitly not presented as a FIFA competition rule.

## Tests

Adds `tests/test_group_ranking_fifa_rules.py` to verify:

- Head-to-head points can outrank superior overall goal difference.
- Three-way ties can be resolved by head-to-head goal difference.
- Overall goal difference applies after equal head-to-head results.
- Conduct score applies after goal criteria.
- FIFA ranking applies after conduct score.
- Missing FIFA ranking falls back deterministically without claiming official-rule completeness.

## Follow-up PRs

1. Store official FIFA ranking snapshot metadata for reproducible fallback behavior.
2. Add more Article 13 edge-case tests if team review identifies additional tied-team scenarios.
3. Convert Annexe C 495 third-place qualifier combinations to machine-readable data.
4. Define knockout draw-resolution policy before final simulation outputs.

## Presentation-safe wording

The project now separates provisional group ranking from an Article 13-oriented ranking utility. This supports official-rule-aligned checks, but final tournament simulation and champion-probability claims still require ranking snapshot metadata, Annexe C conversion, and reproducible simulation outputs.

- Cashier captures the drop-off photo during checkout; `Create Order` is disabled until one is attached, with a hint linked via `aria-describedby`.
- No Order exists pre-checkout, so the photo is captured client-side as a `File` and uploaded immediately *after* checkout commits. A failed attach toasts and lets the cashier retry from the order detail card — it never fails the Order.
- Reuses the shared `PhotoUploadDialog` via a new capture-only mode (`SinglePhotoCaptureDialog`) that hands the `File` back instead of uploading.
- Photo lives in the transactions Zustand store (not the page context) so a pick re-renders only the checkout field, not the catalog.

**Feature 7 — payment precedes pickup ([ADR-0009](docs/adr/0009-payment-precedes-pickup.md))**
- An Order must be fully paid before *any* pickup event (partial or not). Enforced server-side in `createOrderPickupEvent`, with a fail-fast in `createOrderPickupEventPresign` so no pickup photo is uploaded for an unpaid Order.
- Web mirror in `order-action-gates` folds `isPaid` into `canOpenPickup` and exposes `pickupDisabledReason` (distinct copy for cashier vs pickup-only worker). Payment stays a separate step via the existing `OrderPaymentCard`.

**Docs**
- `CONTEXT.md`: drop-off photo → "Required at intake"; OrderPickupEvent → "Payment precedes pickup".
- ADR-0009 records the strict-vs-completion-gated trade-off.

body:
All frontend event date/time display was using timezone-unaware methods (`date-fns format()`, `toLocaleString()`, `toISOString()`), which apply the JS engine's local timezone (UTC on production). A Berlin event at `11:00 AM` stored as `2026-06-22T09:00:00Z` rendered as `09:00 AM` everywhere.

Additionally, lightweight event types (`EventListItem`, `EventDetailRow`, `HostEventRow`, `SavedEventRow`) only selected `{ name, slug }` from `city`, omitting the `timezone` field required for correct display.

## New display utilities (`lib/datetime/event-timezone.ts`)

Five `Intl.DateTimeFormat`-based helpers with an explicit `timeZone` parameter:

```ts
formatEventTime(date, tz)            // "11:00 AM"
formatEventDateLong(date, tz)        // "Monday, 22 Jun 2026"
formatEventDateShort(date, tz)       // "22 Jun 2026"
formatEventDateTimeMedium(date, tz)  // "22 Jun · 11:00 AM"
formatEventCardDate(date, tz, now?)  // "Today · 11:00 AM" | "Tomorrow · …" | "Monday · …" | "Mon, Jun 22 · …"
```

`formatEventCardDate` uses UTC calendar arithmetic for today/tomorrow/this-week detection to avoid DST edge cases.

## Schema propagation

Added `timezone: true` to every city Prisma select that feeds a display component — `eventListSelect`, `getEventDetail`, `getSavedEvents`, discovery, search, host-workspace, and `me/page.tsx`.

## Display call-sites replaced

Removed all `format()`/`toLocaleString()`/`toISOString()` event-date calls across:
`EventDetailServer`, `EventCard`, organizer community+host event list/detail pages, host dashboard, admin event pages, `me/page.tsx`, ambassador check-in page, and city event slug metadata.

## Tests

21 unit tests added, including the exact regression case and multi-timezone offset scenarios.

author: jescard-tamer-cecg
body:
## Problem

Clicking **View Summary** on a ticket in Slack just spun forever and never opened the modal. Production logs showed a `NullPointerException` thrown on every click:

```
ERROR c.c.supportbot.config.SlackAppInit : Error while handling blockAction(ids: [ticket-summary-view] …)
java.lang.NullPointerException
  at com.google.common.base.Preconditions.checkNotNull(Preconditions.java:904)
  at …TicketSummaryService.lambda$getEscalationViews$0(TicketSummaryService.java:103)
  at …TicketSummaryService.summaryView(TicketSummaryService.java:64)
  at …TicketActionsHandler.openSummaryView(TicketActionsHandler.java:72)
```

`getEscalationViews` wrapped both `Escalation.team()` and `escalationTeamsRegistry.findEscalationTeamByCode(...)` (both `@Nullable`) in Guava `checkNotNull`. When a ticket has an escalation whose team code no longer resolves in the registry (e.g. a team removed/renamed after the PT-351 GroupRef refactor), the whole summary build throws. Because the exception happens **before** `slackClient.viewsOpen(...)`, Slack never gets the modal and the button spins indefinitely.

Observed on one ticket, failing on every click for over a week.

## Fix

Resolve the escalation team null-safely instead of asserting non-null:

- If the team code is `null` or absent from the registry, log a `warn` (with `ticketId` / `escalationId` / `teamCode`) and render the escalation **without** a Slack mention.
- `EscalationView.teamSlackGroupId` is now `@Nullable`; the view carries the raw `teamCode` so the mapper can show a fallback label (`Team: <code> (not configured)`) rather than a broken `<!subteam^…>` mention.

A single unresolvable escalation can no longer take down the entire summary view. The new `warn` log surfaces the exact orphaned team code, so the underlying config can be fixed as a follow-up.

## Testing

- New regression test `TicketSummaryServiceTest.escalationWithUnresolvableTeam_doesNotCrashSummary` — one resolvable + one orphaned escalation; asserts the summary builds and the mapper renders without throwing.
- `./gradlew :service:build` green (spotless, checkstyle, full test suite).

## Summary

Fixes #175. `time.add`/`time.sub` (and any time function that takes a timestamp:
`time.fmt`, `time.diff`, `time.parse`, zone-aware paths) now accept a date-only
string `"YYYY-MM-DD"` and treat it as midnight (`00:00:00`).

Before, only a full `"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"` timestamp parsed, so date-range /
slot-generation code had to hand-append `" 00:00:00"` to every calendar date — a
sharp edge agents repeatedly tripped over.

```fluxon
# now works (previously errored):
log "${time.add "2026-06-25" 30 :min}"   # -> 2026-06-25 00:30:00
```

## Changes

- `parse_ts` accepts either a full base (`>= 19` chars) or a date-only string
  (exactly 10 chars → midnight). A **partial** time (truncated clock like
  `"2026-06-25 09:00"`) is still rejected — silently dropping minutes a caller
  wrote would be surprising data loss. Calendar validation (no Feb 31, no leap
  overflow) still applies to date-only input.
- `parse_iso` slices the fractional-second / zone remainder safely for the
  date-only case (no more assuming a 19-char base).
- Doc note in `docs/fluxon-agent.md`.
- Tests: `parse_ts_accepts_date_only_as_midnight`, `time_add_accepts_date_only`,
  and the old `parse_rejects_garbage` updated to reflect the new contract.

- `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked` (all green), `cargo fmt --check`,

  examples/demo.fx` smoke test.

author: xrey167
body:
## Problem

`try_resolve_by_identifier` trimmed only the **query** value and compared the stored `record.value` / `record.scheme` **as-is** (`lib.rs:101-106`). But `identifier_to_graph` canonicalizes both with `.trim().to_ascii_lowercase()` when building the graph node key (`lib.rs:131-136`).

Since `is_identifier_value` / `is_identifier_scheme` validate the **trimmed** form, a crosswalk row whose stored scheme/value carries surrounding whitespace (e.g. `"BBG000B9XRY4 "` from a sloppy feed) is **valid input** — yet it gets resolved by the graph path while being **silently dropped** by the in-memory path. That is exactly the two-resolve-path divergence the `identifier_to_graph` comment warns about, on trimming instead of case.

## Fix

Trim both the query and stored sides of **both** fields in the in-memory filter so it mirrors the graph-key canonicalization:

```rust
let scheme = scheme.trim();
let value = value.trim();
// ...
record.scheme.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case(scheme)
    && record.value.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case(value)
```

author: yoojinko
body:
# release/2.0.0 — Backend (AIN Teams) migration

> **Major release.** Auth, DM/conversation, and agent management move from the legacy orchestration server to the new AIN Teams (NestJS) backend, with a JWT-based BFF. Adds the exhibition kiosk guest flow. Breaking enough in architecture to warrant a major version bump (1.2.8 → 2.0.0).

## Summary
- feat: backend JWT auth foundation — challenge/verify/refresh via same-origin BFF (EPIC13)
- feat: route DM chat through the backend BFF; server-owned conversation ids (EPIC14/15)
- feat: sync agent list from the backend roster; agent import via backend invite (EPIC16/17)
- feat: exhibition kiosk guest flow — wallet-less shared service account, server-side EOA signing, Ctrl+K fresh session (EPIC18)
- fix: SSE streaming (emit `connected` immediately, disable undici read timeout, raise proxy maxDuration)
- docs: ainspace ↔ backend integration guide
- chore: bump version to 2.0.0

## Includes

### Backend auth foundation (EPIC13)
- Browser holds JWT (architecture C); all backend calls proxy through the ainspace BFF (`/api/backend-auth/*`), wallet signature is the only browser-native step
- challenge → verify → refresh with token rotation; tokens in localStorage token-store
- `workspaceId`/`clientId` injected server-side by the BFF (not read from the JWT claim)

### DM / conversation via backend (EPIC14/15)
- `GET/POST /api/threads` and `/api/thread-message` proxy to backend `/dm`
- Server-owned conversation id; member-set dedup; agent a2aUrl → backend user UUID resolution (cached on StoredAgent)
- SSE consumed via fetch-streaming; emit synthetic `connected` immediately to avoid deadlock; undici read-timeout disabled; proxy `maxDuration` raised for Vercel Pro streaming

### Agent sync & import (EPIC16/17)
- Agent list synced from the backend roster; cadence driven by Redis key TTL
- Agent import routed through the backend invite flow (`workspaceId` in body)
- Use backend `agentCardJson` as the agent card

### Exhibition kiosk guest flow (EPIC18)
- Wallet-less guest experience restored as a **shared service account**, scoped to a dedicated kiosk deployment (single env: `BACKEND_KIOSK_PRIVATE_KEY`)
- Kiosk mode is **server-decided** by the BFF (`/api/backend-auth/kiosk-login` returns 200/404); client bootstraps unconditionally and is kiosk-agnostic
- **EOA local signing**: the private key signs the auth challenge inside the BFF and is never transmitted — only the signature reaches the backend
- Kiosk shows as a normal logged-in user (login display falls back to `backendUser.ainAddress`)
- **Ctrl+K = fresh visitor session**: kiosk thread list is local-only (no repopulation from the shared account), `forceNew` creates a new conversation, on-screen messages cleared; backend session kept alive
- Wallet-login flow unchanged throughout (verified by multi-agent adversarial review)

## ⚠️ Deploy notes / dependencies
- Requires the AIN Teams backend reachable at `BACKEND_BASE_URL`, with `clientId`/`workspaceId`/origin allowlisted (see integration guide)
- Kiosk deployment is a **separate Vercel project** with `BACKEND_KIOSK_PRIVATE_KEY` set (public web leaves it empty)
- Backend must support EOA (`provider:'eth'`) verify for kiosk login
- Temporary `[kiosk]` debug logs are still present (to be removed after kiosk deploy verification)

## Verification
- `nvm use 22 && yarn build` passes
- 36 commits from `dev` (EPIC13–18 + fixes)

body:
## Summary

- Replaces the empty README with comprehensive documentation for someone with no prior ML or LLM experience
- Covers quick start (train + chat), full project structure, and a step-by-step plain-language explanation of every concept in the model

## Architecture walkthrough included

Each concept is explained from first principles and linked to the source file where it is implemented:

1. **Tokenization** — why text must become integers, how the character lookup table works
2. **Tensors** — multi-dimensional arrays, row-major storage, gradient buffers
3. **Embeddings** — token vectors, positional embeddings, why they're added together
4. **Attention** — Q/K/V intuition, causal mask, softmax, multi-head, full forward + backward
5. **MLP + GELU + residuals + layer norm** — per-token processing and training stability
6. **Training** — cross-entropy loss, backpropagation via chain rule, AdamW optimizer
7. **Generation** — autoregressive sampling, temperature scaling

## Suggested reading order

The README includes a "What to Read Next" section ordering the source files from simplest (`Tensor.cs`) to most complex (`Trainer.cs`) for progressive learning.
