author: jkitchin
body:
## Summary

Two spatial-relaxation coverage fixes that turn three MINLPLib instances from
`feasible` (no dual bound) into **certified optimal**, continuing the
certification-gap work from #128. Both fixes are rigorous outer
approximations — they only ever produce valid lower bounds.

| Instance | Before | After | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `st_e11` | feasible, bound=None | **optimal**, bound=189.31 | pinned-variable fold |
| `st_e38` | feasible, bound=None | **optimal**, bound=7197.44 | monomial×var lift |
| `ex1226` | feasible, bound=−20.99 | **optimal**, bound=−17.0 | monomial×var lift (bonus) |

## Fix 1 — fold pinned variables (commit 1)

The fractional-power / monomial aux-column builders intentionally skip a
variable whose domain is degenerate (`ub − lb` within tolerance). Spatial
branching routinely drives a domain to a point, so at those nodes a term like
`x**0.6` or `x**2` had no aux column and the linearizer raised
*"Fractional power (i, p) has no aux column"*. That collapsed the node's
objective to a feasibility-only relaxation and silently dropped its dual bound.
`st_e11` finished `feasible`/`bound=None` even though the root LP produced a
valid bound and the per-node LP bounds climbed 161 → 187 toward the optimum.

A pinned variable has an *exact* value, so `x**p` is the constant `v**p` and a
partially-pinned product collapses to a lower-order term. Folding pinned
factors into constants/coefficients is rigorous (no relaxation slack) and
restores the node bound. `_linearize_expr` now takes the node `flat_lb/flat_ub`
and folds pinned monomial/fractional-power bases and product factors.

## Fix 2 — lift monomial×variable products `x**2 * y` (commit 2)

A product mixing a repeated factor with a distinct one (`x*x*y`) was classified
into `general_nl` and the linearizer raised *"Mixed repeated-factor products
are not supported"* → feasibility fallback, no bound. `_decompose_product` now
collapses the repeated original-variable group into its monomial aux column,
reducing `x*x*y` to the lifted bilinear pair `[col(x**2), y]`. The existing
McCormick pipeline relaxes that with one monomial envelope plus one bilinear
envelope. `_collect_lifted_bilinear_products` is threaded the monomial map so
the `(monomial_col, var)` bilinear aux is actually built.

This also tightened `ex1226` enough to close its gap (bonus certification).

## Soundness & regressions

- Every reported bound ≤ incumbent objective; both mechanisms are rigorous
  polyhedral outer approximations (exact for the pinned case).
- 17-instance affected-set census (from #128): all prior wins intact, prob10
  bound preserved, only `ex1226` *improves* (feasible→optimal). **0 regressions.**
- `nvs16` soundness regression test (#120) still passes.
- ~390 relaxation / McCormick / alphaBB / NLP-BB / MILP-BB / convexity-soundness
  tests pass, plus the two new regression tests
  (`test_pinned_var_lift.py`, `test_monomial_var_product.py`).

## Honest scope: the two remaining gaps are deeper than their labels

- **`st_e04`** — labelled "`(affine)**1.2` objective", but the binding
  constraint is the *omitted* equality `x3 = exp(11.86 − 3950/(460+x2))`
  (exp-of-rational). Linearizing the affine-base power alone drives x3→14.7
  (term→0) and the bound stays ≈1000 vs optimum 5339 — it would not certify.
  The real blocker is the exp-of-rational constraint relaxation.
- **`nvs01`** — labelled "sqrt·var", but the objective is
  `sqrt(x0**2 + 900) · x1` (a product of `sqrt(quadratic)` and a variable) and
  a constraint carries a non-constant division `(18505.5·x1²+…)/(x0²+7200)`.
  This needs sqrt-of-convex envelopes plus bilinear-division relaxation.

Both are tracked as follow-up work; neither is a one-line linearizer gap.

## What

Only require `GT_CLOUD_API_KEY` at workflow validation when the Agent node will actually fall back to the default `GriptapeCloudPromptDriver`.

`Agent.validate_before_workflow_run()` previously required the cloud key unconditionally, so a workflow using a non-cloud prompt driver (e.g. an Anthropic Prompt Model Config) failed validation with `GT_CLOUD_API_KEY is not defined` even though no cloud driver was used.

Original report came from [here](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-library-nuke/issues/71).

## Changes

- `validate_before_workflow_run()` returns early (no key required) unless the node would build the default cloud driver.
- New helper `_uses_griptape_cloud_driver()` mirrors the driver-selection precedence already in `process()`:
  - a connected `agent` carries its own driver → no cloud key needed;
  - a `model` resolved to a `BasePromptDriver` (Prompt Model Config) supplies its own credentials → no cloud key needed;
  - only a plain model string / fallthrough to default → cloud key required.
- Added `tests/unit/agents/test_agent_validation.py` covering all four cases, including the regression: no key + connected prompt driver → validation passes.

body:
## Issue relacionada

Closes #87

## Resumo

Implementa a normalizacao de uma linha parseada do razao em conta de debito, conta de credito, direcao e valor.
Quando a linha tem debito, a conta de origem fica no debito e a contrapartida no credito.
Quando a linha tem credito, a contrapartida fica no debito e a conta de origem no credito.
Linhas sem debito ou credito valido passam a gerar erro de normalizacao.

## Tipo de mudanca

- [x] `feat` (nova capacidade)
- [ ] `fix` (correcao de comportamento)
- [ ] `refactor` (melhoria sem mudar comportamento esperado)
- [ ] `chore` (estrutura, scripts, migracoes, CI)
- [ ] `docs` (documentacao)
- [ ] `spec` (PRD, spec ou decisao de arquitetura)

## Escopo impactado

- Dominios: `razao`
- Arquivos/modulos principais alterados:
  - `core/razao_parser.py`
  - `tests/test_razao_parser.py`
- Dependencias externas afetadas: nenhuma

## Checklist de validacao

- [x] Testes automatizados relevantes foram executados
- [x] Casos de erro criticos foram testados
- [x] Regras de acesso por usuario/empresa foram verificadas quando aplicavel
- [x] Migracoes Alembic foram revisadas quando aplicavel
- [x] Contratos de API e schemas foram atualizados quando aplicavel
- [x] Documentacao/PRD/specs foram atualizados quando aplicavel
- [x] Nao ha segredos, credenciais ou dados sensiveis versionados
- [x] Diff foi revisado e esta legivel (mudanca focada)

## Evidencias

- `./venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_razao_parser.py`
  - Resultado: `5 passed`
- `./venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests`
  - Resultado: `184 passed, 2 deselected`

Comportamentos cobertos:
- Linha com debito normaliza origem como `conta_debito` e contrapartida como `conta_credito`.
- Linha com credito normaliza contrapartida como `conta_debito` e origem como `conta_credito`.
- `conta_origem` e `conta_contrapartida` sao preservadas.
- Linha sem debito ou credito valido gera `RazaoParseError`.

## Riscos e rollback

- Risco principal: alguma planilha real pode trazer valores de debito/credito em formato diferente do retorno atual do parser.
- Impacto esperado se falhar: a normalizacao pode rejeitar linhas que precisem de tratamento adicional em issue futura.
- Plano de rollback: reverter as alteracoes em `core/razao_parser.py` e `tests/test_razao_parser.py`.

## Observacoes para review

Validar especialmente a regra contabil central: debito/credito sao interpretados em relacao a conta do bloco, nunca por uma regra global como “debito significa banco”.

author: kevinrapley
body:
## What

Two fixes to the **Assign a role to a team member** page (`/pages/team/role-assignments/`), both reported from live testing.

### 1. Broken "Check and confirm" layout
The summary-list keys wrapped character-by-character (e.g. `Team / mem / ber / email`, `Acces / s / durati / on`).

**Cause:** a `display` conflict between the two stylesheets the page loads. `govuk-frontend.css` sets `.govuk-summary-list{display:table; table-layout:fixed}` and `.govuk-summary-list__row{display:table-row}`, but `auth-role-assignments.css` overrode only the **row** to `display:grid` while leaving the `<dl>` as `display:table`. A `display:table` parent with `display:grid` children generates broken anonymous table boxes, collapsing the key column to minimum width.

**Fix:** set `.govuk-summary-list{display:block; width:100%}` so grid rows are direct flow children; widen the key column min from `140px` to `160px`; add `overflow-wrap:break-word; word-break:normal` to the key so it wraps at spaces. Change is page-scoped (this CSS only loads on the role-assignments page).

### 2. Internal codes leaked into the success message
The "Role assigned" panel exposed developer-facing identifiers:

```
Assignment ID: asn_031bc56b
Scope: team_daas
```

**Fix:** removed both lines (and the now-unused `assignment` variable). The confirmation still names the role, person and team in plain language, consistent with the page's principle of not exposing implementation terms to users.

## Testing
- `node --test` on the three relevant suites — all pass:
  - `tests/auth-role-assignment-ui-route-state.test.js`
  - `tests/auth-role-assignment-api-route-state.test.js`
  - `tests/govuk-tables-summary-lists-application-route-state.test.js`

author: itzzavdheshh
body:
## 🚀 Program
GSSoC

## 📝 Description

### Problem
* The frontend chat uploader dispatched POST requests to `/api/upload` without attaching the authenticated user's JWT token, causing all upload attempts to fail with `401 Unauthorized`.
* The backend lacked custom file-type validation rules on the `/api/upload` endpoint, exposing the application to unrestricted file upload vulnerabilities (XSS/RCE vectors).
* The backend server had syntax and merge conflict errors from previous upstream updates which prevented compilation.

### Solution
1. **Frontend**: Prop-drilled the active `token` state into `<MessageInput />` and attached the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header to the POST request.
2. **Backend Authentication**: Created and integrated the `requireAuth` Express middleware to cleanly validate JWTs.
3. **File Filter Validation**: Implemented a custom whitelisting `fileFilter` in `multer` to verify both the file extension and the MIME type sequentially (securing against malicious extension-renaming bypasses).
4. **Error Handling**: Wrapped multer execution inside `/api/upload` to return graceful `400 Bad Request` messages instead of raw crash traces.
5. **Upstream Sync & Cleanup**: Synced the repository with the latest upstream commits and resolved the compilation/syntax issues in `server.js`.

## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes #103 

## 🔄 Type of Change
- [x] 🐛 Bug fix
- [x] 🧹 Refactor / cleanup
- [x] 📝 Documentation

## 🧪 How to Test
1. **Automated Integration Tests**:
   Navigate to the backend directory, install packages, and execute the test runner:
   ```bash
   cd PingUp-Backend
   npm install
   node --test tests/auth.test.js tests/roles.test.js tests/upload.test.js
   ```
   Verify that all 25 tests pass successfully.

2. **Manual Chat Upload Test**:
   - Start the backend and frontend dev servers.
   - Log into a chat room, select an image via the paperclip icon (`📎`), and send it.
   - Verify that the image uploads successfully, returns a valid static URL, and renders in the message list feed.

## 📸 Screenshots (if applicable)
N/A

- [x] I am contributing under GSSoC
- [x] My code follows the project's existing style
- [x] My PR title follows Conventional
- [x] I have linked the related issue above

author: chapman-jon
body:
Ports rsgl's `cast_columns` (the next step in the data pipeline, after `result_dfs` and `types`).

## What

When a single aesthetic maps to a **date** in one layer and a **timestamp** in another, the dates are promoted to datetimes so the layers share a comparable axis. pandas has no first-class pure-date dtype — DB drivers return `DATE` as object-dtype `datetime.date` and `TIMESTAMP` as `datetime64` — so this reconciliation matters before rendering.

Mirrors the rsgl functions one-to-one:
- `aes_has_dt_and_ts` — aesthetic maps to a date in some layer and a timestamp in another
- `aes_with_dt_and_ts` — all such aesthetics across the pgs
- `cast_for_aes` — cast the aesthetic's column to datetime per layer (no-op where already a timestamp; layers lacking the aesthetic returned unchanged)
- `cast_columns` — top-level entry

## Tests

Ports the `test-cast_columns.R` cases. Kept **synth-only** for the temporal cases: the test DuckDB returns `economics.date` as a `TIMESTAMP` (not a date), so rsgl's economics-based date case is reproduced with `synth.day` (date) / `synth.day_and_time` (timestamp), which are unambiguous and controlled by `conftest.py`.

Full suite: **422 passed** (was 409).

author: sunnyd27
body:
## What
Surface the SAME week's Weekly Hold candidates on **Sunday's weekly-wrap** in addition to Monday's week-ahead, giving a relaxed Sunday→Monday-pre-open pick window. The blind-pick **lock stays at the week's first trading-day open** (unchanged).

## Key mechanism
`weeklyHoldBasis()` (calendar.js) shifts a Sunday date forward to the upcoming Monday, so Sunday and Monday key off the **same ISO week** → identical candidates, identical `target_date`, one-pick-per-week dedup via the existing `UNIQUE(user_id,kind,target_date)`. The basis lives **inside `createWeeklyHoldPick`**, so a Sunday-then-Monday pick **cannot double-pick**.

## Changes
- `calendar.js`: `weeklyHoldBasis()`; `isWeeklyHoldOpen(now, basisDate=now)` (default keeps existing callers).
- `generate.js`: candidates on week-ahead AND weekly-wrap, via the basis.
- `ai.js`: `buildWeeklyWrapPrompt` injects `weeklyHoldBlock` + schema.
- `picks.js`: create/state compute `target_date` + open gate off the basis; pick card now renders on weekly-wrap.
- `template.js`: Sunday co-locates the card under "Your Week in Juice"; other editions keep it by Tomorrow's Call.
- Sunday verdict dropped (shows Saturday) — Sunday = reflect + pick ahead.

## Tests / docs
- `test-weekly.js` → **65 assertions** incl. new Section 10: basis shift, Sun≡Mon candidates + `target_date`, lock open Sun & Mon-pre-open / closed post-open, pick phase on weekly-wrap, **the explicit Sun-then-Mon dedup (one row)**, holiday-Monday week. Full suite green (`test-evening-email`'s Monday failure is a pre-existing, unrelated test-only bug — real email path safe-navs).
- ROADMAP §20a + CONTEXT entries reconciled from "Monday-only" to the Sunday+Monday window.

No migration.

author: aditya-ingale
body:
### Booking Entity & Database
- BookingRequest entity — tenant, property, moveInDate, message, status
- BookingStatus enum — PENDING, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, COMPLETED
- booking_requests table auto-created by Hibernate
- Unique constraint prevents duplicate PENDING requests for same property

### Booking APIs
- POST /api/bookings — tenant submits booking request with optional counter-offer
- GET /api/bookings/tenant — tenant views own bookings (optional ?status= filter)
- GET /api/bookings/landlord — landlord views incoming requests (optional ?status= filter)
- PUT /api/bookings/{id}/status — landlord accepts, rejects, or counter-offers
- DELETE /api/bookings/{id} — tenant cancels own PENDING request
- PUT /api/bookings/{id}/respond-counter — tenant responds to landlord's counter-offer
- GET /api/bookings/stream — SSE stream for realtime booking status updates (per user)

### Rent Negotiation Feature
- Tenant can propose counter-offer rent on booking submission
- Landlord can accept, reject, or propose their own counter-offer
- Tenant can accept or reject landlord's counter
- counterOfferBy field tracks who made the last offer (TENANT / LANDLORD)
- Status stays PENDING during negotiation, resolves to ACCEPTED/REJECTED

### SSE Realtime Booking Updates
- BookingSseService — per-user emitter map (ConcurrentHashMap)
- Landlord receives instant notification when tenant submits booking
- Tenant receives instant notification when landlord accepts/rejects
- Supports multiple tabs/devices per user (CopyOnWriteArrayList per userId)
- Dead emitter cleanup on connection close/timeout/error

### Email Notifications
- sendBookingNotification() added to EmailService
- Landlord emailed when new booking request arrives
- Tenant emailed when landlord accepts or rejects
- Email failure does not fail the booking (non-blocking)

### Business Rules Enforced
- Landlord cannot book their own property
- Duplicate PENDING requests for same property blocked
- Only PENDING requests can be cancelled or processed
- Only the property owner can accept/reject bookings

## Tested
- POST /api/bookings → PENDING booking created ✅
- Booking notification email received by landlord ✅
- GET /api/bookings/tenant → tenant sees own bookings ✅
- GET /api/bookings/landlord → landlord sees incoming requests ✅
- PUT /api/bookings/{id}/status → ACCEPTED with response message ✅
- Landlord counter-offer → status stays PENDING, counterOfferBy = LANDLORD ✅
- Tenant responds to counter → ACCEPTED ✅
- DELETE /api/bookings/{id} → cancelled successfully ✅
- Duplicate booking prevention → error returned ✅
- SSE stream → booking update received instantly in Postman ✅

author: realmeylisdev
body:
## Description

After reinstalling and signing back in, only a few DM conversations were restored even though the relay still held the full history. Root cause is **client-side**: the one-time DM history **drain** marked itself **permanently complete** on the first empty relay page without verifying recovery had actually happened. Two paths trip this:

1. **Cold-start relay race** — the drain fires on inbox open gated only on signer readiness, not relay connectivity. `queryEvents` (unlike `publish`/`subscribe`) did not retry-connect, and the relay pool completes a query immediately with an empty result when no relay has accepted it. A drain that fired before the WebSocket pool connected fetched nothing, then permanently marked itself complete.
2. **Remote-signer decryption failure** — for Keycast / `divineOAuth` accounts every gift-wrap decrypt is an RPC call. A wrap that failed to decrypt was silently dropped (no row, no dedup marker) while the drain still completed, so those conversations were lost.

The conversation list is a pure local-DB projection, so unrecovered history was invisible with no UI path back. Verified directly against `relay.divine.video`: the affected account has **122 gift wraps on the relay** (readable without auth) while the app showed **3**.

### What changed
- **Connectivity-gated completion** — the drain marks complete on an empty page only when at least one relay was connected to answer it; with 0 connected relays it defers and resumes on the next inbox open.
- **`queryEvents` retry-connect** — matches `publish`/`subscribe`, so a cold query reconnects instead of returning empty instantly.
- **One-time re-drain** — a `DmSyncState.drainVersion` bump clears the stale "complete" flag once, so installs already stranded by the old drain recover **without another reinstall**.
- **Durable failed-decrypt queue** — wraps that fail NIP-44 decryption are persisted to a new `pending_gift_wraps` table and replayed by `retryPendingDecryptions()` on inbox open (capped per wrap), so flaky remote-signer decryption never permanently loses a conversation.

**Related Issue:** Closes #5202

## Reproducing steps

**Before this PR**
1. Use an account with many DM conversations (ideally a Keycast / Divine-OAuth account).
2. Uninstall and reinstall the app.
3. Sign back into the same account and open **Messages** on the first cold start.
4. Only a few chats are restored. Logs show a `DM history drain ... complete` once, then `DM history drain skipped ... already complete` on every later open — permanently — while the relay still holds the full history.

**After this PR**
- On the first post-reinstall open, the drain no longer completes against an unconnected pool, and wraps that fail to decrypt are queued and retried, so the full conversation list is restored. Installs already stranded recover on their next inbox open via the drain-version re-run.

## Out of Scope
- Pinning which of the two paths (cold-start race vs remote-signer decrypt failure) was the proximate trigger for a given report — the fix covers both. A device log line (`DM history drain complete ... eventsFetched=N`) would distinguish them but is not required for the fix.

## Verification
- `dart format` + `flutter analyze` clean across `dm_repository`, `nostr_client`, `db_client`, and the changed `mobile/lib` files.
- Package suites green: `db_client` (664), `dm_repository` (309), `nostr_client` (271).
- Mobile DM suites green: `test/blocs/dm/` and `test/screens/inbox/`.
- Drift schema-parity + migration tests pass with the new `pending_gift_wraps` table (added via the existing runtime `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` pattern — no schema-version bump).
- New tests: drain connectivity-gated completion (defer on 0 relays / complete on ≥1 relay), drain-version re-run, failed-decrypt → pending queue, `retryPendingDecryptions` recovery, `PendingGiftWrapsDao` CRUD + retry cap, `DmSyncState.drainVersion`, and `queryEvents` retry-connect.
- Not yet exercised on a physical device.

## Type of Change
- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

body:
## What
Adds `RawFile.profile(scan_number) -> (mz: float64[:], intensity: float64[:])` to the Python bindings. The frequency-domain profile bins are converted to m/z via the scan event's calibration coefficients; centroid-only scans return empty arrays.

## Why
The Rust core already decodes profile data (`ScanDataPacket.profile`, `Profile::to_mz_intensity`), but the Python `RawFile` exposed centroids only (`peaks()` / `scan()`). This surfaces the raw profile to Python without dropping to Rust or round-tripping through mzML.

## How
Thin wrapper mirroring `peaks()`: locks the shared source, calls `reader.read_scan(...)`, and `Profile::to_mz_intensity` with the scan event's coefficients.

## Testing
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test` pass. Spot-checked on a Q Exactive file: the non-zero profile (point count and intensities) matches an independent reference reader.

Happy to file a tracking issue first if you prefer issue-before-PR for new API; it's a small additive wrapper.

author: fuleinist
body:
## What

`loadSnapshot` in `cmd/diff.go` accepted a `dir` argument but read
the snapshot file with a bare relative path
(`snapshotDir + "/" + env + ".json"`). The companion writer in
`cmd/snapshot.go` correctly uses
`filepath.Join(dir, cfg.Settings.SnapshotDir, ...)`, so the reader
must join the same way.

In the default workflow (run everything from the project root) the two
paths happen to resolve to the same place, so the bug is latent. It
surfaces as soon as the caller's CWD is not equal to `dir` — for
example when `snapshot_dir` is set to an absolute path in
`config.yaml`, or when the binary is invoked from another directory.

## Why

Two things are wrong with the current code:

1. The function signature is a lie: `dir` is a required parameter but
   it does nothing. Future callers will reasonably assume it does.
2. `snapshot` and `diff`/`migrate` resolve the snapshot directory
   differently, even though they live in the same package. The fix
   makes the reader match the writer.

## Testing

Two tests in `cmd/diff_test.go`:

- `TestLoadSnapshot_JoinsDirWithSnapshotDir` writes a real JSON
  snapshot under `t.TempDir()/<snapshotDir>/<env>.json` and asserts
  `loadSnapshot` finds it. The test fails on the old relative-path
  code with `open .schema-sync/snapshots/dev.json: no such file or
  directory`.
- `TestLoadSnapshot_MissingFileReturnsError` covers the negative case
  so the error path stays exercised.

`go test ./...` passes; `go vet ./...` is clean.

author: xumaple
body: Adds `@temporalio/google-adk-agents`, a contrib plugin that runs Google Agent Development Kit (`@google/adk`) agents as durable Temporal Workflows. The agent graph runs inside the Workflow and replays deterministically; the non-deterministic boundaries — every model call and every MCP tool call — are routed out to Activities, so the whole run gets Temporal's retries, timeouts, heartbeating, and crash-safe replay. For users it's a one-line change: wrap the agent's model in `TemporalLlm` and register the plugin.

author: prusnak
body:
Prevent `/v1/mint/quote/{method}/check` from returning quote status for quotes that belong to a different payment method than the method in the URL.

The batch custom mint quote check path authenticated the requested route, but then passed all supplied quote IDs directly to `check_mint_quotes`. For custom methods, the response mapping only checked that each returned quote was custom, not that it matched the URL method. This allowed a caller authorized for one custom method route to query known quote IDs from another custom method.

Reuse the existing mint quote method validation before loading quote statuses, matching the method-scoped behavior already used by mint requests.

Add a regression test that creates a `venmo` custom mint quote and verifies it cannot be checked through the `paypal` batch quote check route.

Réimplémentation fraîche de la **console à onglets UrT** (feature `855ae13b`), longtemps différée car « intestable à l'aveugle ». Faite en 5 itérations avec **test en jeu entre chaque** (workflow implémente → teste → itère).

## Feature
La console unique devient un tableau de tabs **All / General / Frag / Chat** :
- **Tout** message → onglet *All* (identique à la console classique).
- Les lignes **frag** (kills) et **chat** sont routées vers leur onglet, via les **octets marqueurs** du mod q3ut4 (`0x11`/`0x12` = frag, `0x13` = chat) — fiable, pas une heuristique. Le reste → *General*.
- **Barre d'onglets visuelle** : onglets opaques sous le panneau, actif surligné (jaune), liseré **rouge** enveloppant l'ensemble console+onglets.
- **Bascule** : clic gauche/droit (= précédent/suivant) ou shift+←/→. Cvar `con_tabs` (défaut on) + commandes `con_nexttab`/`con_prevtab` bindables.

## Implémentation
- `console_t consoles[NUM_CON]` + pointeur actif `con` ; helpers de print paramétrés par console.
- `CL_ConsolePrint` classe + fan-out (All + onglet catégorie) via `Con_WriteText`.
- Resize/clear/clearnotify bouclent sur toutes les consoles.
- Switch hooké dans `Console_Key` (cl_keys.c) ; `Con_NextTab`/`Con_PrevTab` exposés.

## Validé
Compile proprement (client + renderers) ; **testé en jeu** (routage, rendu, clics, resize). Contenu à `cl_console.c` + petit hook `cl_keys.c`/`client.h`.

author: johnnywyles
body:
Fixes to the LCD, RPC, and IBC OpenAPI specs **and the `/api` reference page itself**, verified against the deployed stack: **CometBFT 0.38.19 / ibc-go v8 / osmosis v31**. Every path in all three specs was live-probed against the deployed gateway to confirm it is actually reachable.

## /api page: dropdown + hydration (makes the specs actually reachable)
- **Version dropdown didn't switch the rendered spec.** It pushed `/api/?v=X` (trailing slash) while the site is `trailingSlash:false`, so the nav 301-redirected and the Stoplight `<elements-api>` web component (reads `apiDescriptionUrl` once on mount) never re-fetched. Fix: push `/api?v=X` and add `key={currentVersion}` to remount on change. **Pre-existing since the Docusaurus-3 web-component migration** (the prior React `<API>` reacted to the prop; the web component does not) — not introduced by the spec content work.
- **SSR-stable version state.** `currentVersion` is no longer read from the URL query during render (which would diverge from the query-less prerender); it starts at the SSR-stable default and syncs to `?v=` in an effect after mount, so the page's own version state never differs between server and first client render.
- `SectionsMenu` now supports a controlled `value` so the dropdown label stays in sync on deep links.

Verified by driving the built `/api` page headless: the dropdown swaps the rendered spec for all four sets, deep links render the correct spec and label, and switching versions introduces no new console errors.

Note: `/api` still emits the recoverable React #418/#423 hydration warnings that Docusaurus 3 logs on standard-layout pages site-wide (the same warnings appear on plain content pages such as `/integrate/rpc` and `/build/chain/modules/gov`, whose component stacks sit entirely in the theme bundle; the homepage has none). This change neither adds nor removes those; eliminating them is a framework-level issue out of scope here.

## LCD.yaml — regenerated from the deployed node swagger
Replaced the stale, hand-aged spec with the node's own swagger (`lcd.osmosis.zone/swagger`): **176 current paths**, server pinned to `lcd.osmosis.zone`. Live sweep: all 176 routes are registered on the deployed node.

The raw node swagger tags every operation `Query`/`Service`, which renders as one giant flat sidebar. Re-tagged by module into **23 groups** (osmosis modules first: Epochs, GAMM, Incentives, Lockup, Mint, Pool Incentives, Superfluid, Tokenfactory, Txfees; then cosmos: Auth, Bank, Gov, Staking, etc.) so the reference is navigable.

**Caveat (upstream):** the chain's swagger config does not register every module, so concentrated-liquidity, poolmanager, cosmwasmpool, protorev, and gov v1 are still absent — the node's published swagger omits them too. Tracked as an osmosis-repo follow-up (MTN-147); not fixable in this docs PR.

## RPC.yaml (29 → 28 paths)
- Removed `/events` and `/remove_tx` (CometBFT main/v1.x only, not deployed v0.38; both 404 live). `version: "Master"` → `CometBFT v0.38`. Dead `godoc.org` links → `pkg.go.dev/cometbft`.
- Dropped methods that can't work from the public node: the websocket-only `/subscribe`, `/unsubscribe`, `/unsubscribe_all`; the unsafe ops `/dial_seeds`, `/dial_peers`, `/unsafe_flush_mempool`; and `/broadcast_tx`, which 404s (the canonical methods are the three `broadcast_tx_{sync,async,commit}` variants, which all work and stay).
- Annotated the methods that are firewalled (403) on the public node but valid against your own: `/net_info`, `/genesis`, `/genesis_chunked`, `/dump_consensus_state`.
- Final surface: **28 paths** across Info/Tx/ABCI/Evidence; everything else returns 200 or only 500s on a missing required param.

## IBCGO.yaml
- Fixed the malformed `ClientParams` path `/ibc/client/v1/params` → `/ibc/core/client/v1/params`. `version: 1.0.0` → `ibc-go v8`.
- The spec declared a relative server (`url: /`), so Try-it resolved against the docs site and failed. IBC REST is served by the LCD / gRPC-gateway, so the server is now `https://lcd.osmosis.zone` (mainnet) + `lcd-test.osmosis.zone` (testnet).
- Re-tagged the flat `Query` list by IBC sub-module.
- **Removed the ICS-29 Fee group (8 paths).** Every `/ibc/apps/fee/v1/*` endpoint returns `501 Not Implemented`: Osmosis v31 does not wire the ibc-fee middleware (no fee keeper in `app/keepers`), so the whole group is dead. Final surface: **35 paths** in 5 reachable module groups (Channel / Client / Connection core, Interchain Accounts / Transfer apps).

## docs/build/chain/gov/README.md — fix two broken proposal-type anchors
The proposal-type list linked `cancel-software-upgrade` to `#submit-proposal-cancel-software-upgrade` (no such heading; the slug is `submit-proposal-cancel-upgrade`) and `remove-superfluid-asset` to `#submit-proposal-community-pool-spend` (a copy-paste error). Both fixed, and all eight links converted from absolute `docs.osmosis.zone/osmosis-core/modules/gov#...` URLs (which 301-round-trip back to this same page) to local `#` anchors, so they are now statically checked at build time. Found by a repo-wide broken-anchor audit; invisible to the build before because absolute external URLs are skipped by the link checker.

Found during the repo-wide accuracy audit. Build passes; each spec verified rendering in a headless browser (grouped sidebars, correct Base URL, zero network failures) and every path confirmed reachable on the deployed node.

Tracked in Linear: MTN-143 (RPC/IBC + the /api page fix), MTN-144 (LCD regen, folded in), MTN-147 (upstream module gap).

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Docs and client-side API reference UX only; no chain or auth logic.
> 
> **Overview**
> **API reference page (`/api`)** now switches OpenAPI specs reliably when users pick RPC/LCD/DATA/IBCGO or open a `?v=` deep link. Version is held in React state (SSR default, then synced from the URL after mount) to avoid hydration mismatches on static prerender. Navigation uses `/api?v=X` (no trailing slash), the dropdown is **controlled** via `value`, and `<elements-api>` gets `key={currentVersion}` so Stoplight remounts and reloads the YAML when the set changes.
> 
> **`SectionsMenu`** only passes `defaultValue` to Radix `Select.Root` when callers actually supply it, so controlled `value` from the API page does not fight a defaulted empty `defaultValue`.
> 
> **Gov build docs** replace external `docs.osmosis.zone` proposal-type links with local `#` anchors and fix wrong slugs for cancel-software-upgrade and remove-superfluid-asset.

author: maoxyzt
body:
## Summary

- Add `src/sql/probe.rs` with `probe_httpfs()`: opens a fresh in-memory DuckDB connection, runs `INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;` with a 5-second watchdog interrupt (same pattern as `query_handler`'s interrupt-handle), and returns `true`/`false`
- `ServerInfo` gains `httpfs_ready: Option<bool>` — `None` when `sql_enabled` is false, `Some(true/false)` from the live probe on every `GET /api/server` request
- Frontend shows an amber `Alert` banner in `ParquetSqlTab` and `TextPreview` when the active storage is S3 and `httpfs_ready === false`, with pre-install instructions matching `diag.rs` Rule 4's hint

## Motivation

The current system only diagnoses httpfs failures **after the fact** (`diag.rs` Rule 4): users have to run an S3 SQL query, hit an error, and only then learn the extension is missing. This is especially painful on air-gapped or offline deployments. This PR switches to **proactive detection** — the warning appears before the user ever clicks Run.

## Technical notes

- httpfs is not statically bundled; first use requires a network download (cached to `~/.duckdb`). Once cached, the probe costs ~10 ms
- `useServerInfo` uses `staleTime: Infinity`, so the probe fires at most once per page session
- `#[cfg(feature = "duckdb")]` ensures non-duckdb builds always return `httpfs_ready: null` with no DuckDB linkage

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --features duckdb` and `cargo build` (no feature) both pass
- [x] `cargo test --features duckdb`: 186/186 pass, including new `probe_completes_promptly`
- [x] `tsc -b`: zero type errors
- [x] `npm test`: 318/318 pass
- [ ] With network: `curl /api/server` returns `"httpfs_ready": true`
- [ ] Offline / cleared `~/.duckdb` cache: returns `"httpfs_ready": false` within 5 s, amber warning banner visible in the SQL tab for S3 storages

author: vladimircharkot
body:
# Rework de sesiones: esquema de auth por sala, config inmutable y planilla de asistencia

## Contexto

Reorganiza cómo una sala autentica a sus estudiantes y cómo se modela su presencia. Tres cambios encadenados:

1. El método de auth pasa a ser una propiedad **de la sala** (`esquema`), no del cliente.
2. Ese `esquema` es **inmutable** una vez creada la sala.
3. La lista de estudiantes deja de destruirse en cada listado y se convierte en una **planilla durable** con log de asistencia.

## Cambios

### 1. Segregación de métodos de autenticación

- La config de la sala expone `esquema: 'nombre' | 'dni' | 'google'` (enum `MetodosLogin`), reemplazando los viejos booleans `pedir_dni` / `permitir_anonimo`.
- El **pasaporte** del estudiante es ahora *method-agnostic*: una bolsa floja de campos de identidad opcionales, sin `metodo`. El cliente solo manda lo que la sala le pidió recolectar.
- El `metodo` se inyecta en la sesión **server-side** al construirla, a partir de `config.esquema`. Cada esquema valida su propio campo de identidad y resuelve el `userId` sin adivinar (`nombre` → nombre, `dni` → dni, `google` → email).
- Errores de sesión actualizados: se agregan `EmailNoPermitido` y `EmailRequerido`; se eliminan `DniYaConectado` y `SesionYaActiva`.

### 2. Config inmutable vs. actualizable

- `actualizarConfig` ahora valida contra un subconjunto **mutable** (`configActualizable`, hoy solo `solo_invitados`). El `esquema` ya no se puede cambiar tras crear la sala (`.strict()` rechaza intentos de incluirlo).
- La lista de invitados sigue siendo mutable vía los eventos `sala:permitidos_*`.

### 3. Planilla de estudiantes + log de asistencia

- La planilla (`sala:${id}:estudiantes`) pasa a guardar la **sesión** keyed por `userId` (registro durable de quiénes pasaron por la sala). La presencia **no se almacena**: se deduce de los sockets vivos al listar.
- Se elimina `limpiarEstudiantesSinSesion`, que destruía la planilla en cada listado. `listarEstudiantes` ahora incluye desconectados, anotando `conectado` contra los sockets vivos.
- `limpiarEstudiantes` (purgado explícito del profe) borra solo a los desconectados que **no** están en la lista de invitados.
- Nuevo **log de asistencia** append-only (`sala:${id}:asistencia`): eventos de conexión/desconexión que se reconstruyen en intervalos por usuario. Expuesto vía el handler `sala:pedir_asistencia`. Todavía no tiene consumer. 

### Fixes

- **Multi-clientId**: al desconectarse de una pestaña, ya no se notifica "desconectado" al profe si al estudiante le queda otro socket vivo.
- **Leak de nombre de Google**: el estudiante ya no hereda el nombre/email de la sesión de Google del navegador (que en el navegador del profe era la suya). El passport queda limpio (`{ idSala, nombre, dni, clientId }`) y el nombre es siempre el tipeado.

## Deploy / breaking changes

- ⚠️ **Migración de datos requerida antes de deployar en prod**: el runtime ya asume el shape nuevo de la config.

## Vad

Agenter med säljbias kan nu shorta tokens — lånar dem, säljer direkt och köper tillbaka senare. Om priset fallit tjänar de på spreaden. Öppnar för market neutral trading.

## Mekanik

| Steg | Detalj |
|---|---|
| **Öppna short** | Lås 150% collateral, ta emot försäljningsintäkter. Nettokostnad: 50% av positionsvärdet |
| **Daglig avgift** | 0,3%/körning av collateral → Börskassan |
| **Take-profit** | Stängs automatiskt vid +30% vinst |
| **Likvidation** | Stängs automatiskt när förlust > 80% av collateral |
| **Frivillig stängning** | 10% chans per körning |

| Agent | Sannolikhet | Max antal | Symbol-filter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kryptoanalytiker | 8% | 3 | Alla |
| Den sura | 6% | 2 | Alla |
| Konservativ debattör | 5% | 2 | Alla |
| Journalist | 5% | 2 | Alla |
| Nationalekonom | 4% | 2 | Alla |
| Miljöaktivist | 4% | 2 | Bara NOVA |
| Den stressade | 3% | 1 | Alla |

En agent kan simultant vara lång DBT och kort NOVA — P&L beror på spreaden mellan de två, inte absolut marknadsriktning. Möjliggör pairs trading och hedging.

author: sandymr3
body:
@
## What

Honours `prefers-reduced-motion` across the whole app for motion-sensitive users — the first slice of the post-plan a11y/perf pass.

- **Root `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">`** (in `app/layout.tsx`) makes *every* Framer Motion component respect the OS "reduce motion" setting: transform/layout animations become instant while opacity/colour transitions are preserved. This covers the bulk of the apps motion (page transitions, card entrances, overlays, cinematic moments) without editing each component.
- **Extended the `globals.css` reduced-motion block** to silence decorative, always-on CSS loops that Framer doesnt own: `loading-bar-fill` shimmer, `pulse-ring`, `rec-dot`, `warroom-wave-*`, and `dynamic-scenario-border` glow/spin.

## Deliberate choice: spinners keep spinning

Functional loading spinners (`@keyframes spin` / `.animate-spin`) are **intentionally left running** — a frozen spinner reads as "stuck", whereas a still-rotating one communicates progress. Only *decorative* motion is removed. The new CSS block is placed last (wins by source order) with `!important` as an a11y-override guard.

## Why MotionConfig over per-component edits

Several components already check `useReducedMotion()` manually, but many `motion.*` usages dont. `MotionConfig` at the root is the canonical Framer Motion solution — one provider, global coverage, and the existing per-component checks still work (now redundant, not conflicting).

## Verification

- `tsc` + `eslint` clean.
- Dev server: landing renders fully with **no server or console errors**, confirming `MotionConfig` works rendered from the server-component layout.
- Note: the actual reduced-motion rendering cant be emulated with the local preview tooling (no `prefers-reduced-motion` emulation), but both mechanisms used here are canonical and the integration is verified non-breaking.

## Scope

Independent of the other open PRs; additive/cosmetic — no logic or contract changes.

author: hecris10
body:
## Summary

Two related changes to `/home/dashboard`:

### 1. Wire mocked dashboard panels to real data (`feat(dashboard)`)
Previously several panels rendered hardcoded mock arrays. They now pull live, user-scoped data:

- **Device Usage**, **Scan Locations**, **Recent Scan Activity** — derived from `QrCodeController` rows (user-agent / accept-language / referrer parsed at query time via a new `scan-analytics.utils`).
- **Your QR Codes** grid/list — the user's real QR codes with live scan counts, plus working **search**, **type filter**, **CSV export**, and **edit / copy-link / delete** actions.
- **Scan Activity** period selector now actually drives the chart (7d / 30d / 90d / year).

New JStack queries: `getQrCodesWithScans`, `getRecentScans`, `getDeviceUsage`, `getScanLocations`. No DB schema/migration needed — everything derives from existing columns.

Also fixes `getQrCodeStats` mutating `now` while computing week bounds, which corrupted the month-over-month comparison windows.

### 2. Enforce per-user data isolation (`fix(api)`)
Audit of how the routers read from the DB surfaced a cross-user exposure vector:

- All authenticated queries scope by `auth?.session?.user.id!`. The `!` is compile-time only — if `user.id` were ever `undefined`, Prisma **drops** `where: { userId: undefined }` and returns **all users' rows**. `authMiddleware` now requires a resolved `session.user.id` and **fails closed (401)**, guaranteeing a concrete id for every scoped query.
- `controller.delete` wasn't scoped to the caller at all (`userId: (input.id, input.id)!` — a comma-operator typo). Switched to a `deleteMany` scoped by the owning `qrCode.userId`, so a user can only delete their own scan records.

## Test plan
- `bun run build` passes (compile + types + lint, all routes generated).
- Dashboard panels show proper empty states until controlled QR codes are scanned.

## Notes
- Location granularity is country-level (inferred from `accept-language`); no GeoIP is stored.
- Scan-derived panels populate only once **controlled** QR codes are scanned (that's when `QrCodeController` rows are created).

author: cstuncsik
body:
DX tooling — a Stylelint setup that **automates the CSS-authoring conventions** I'd been hand-enforcing (and the adversarial reviews kept catching), so they hold as the library grows. (Per your call: no `0.x→1.0` codemod — few existing users.)

## The config
Convention-only — Prettier owns formatting, so `stylelint.config.mjs` has **no stylistic rules**, just the house guardrails (CLAUDE.md "CSS authoring"):
- **Floor rules (all source CSS):** ban the `lh` unit and `:dir()` (both above the Chrome 99 / FF 97 / Safari 15.4 floor).
- **Component CSS:** tokens-only colors (no raw hex / `rgb()` / `hsl()` — use `--re-color-*` or `color-mix()`) and logical properties (no physical `width`/`height`/inset/`margin`/`padding`/`border-*`; `text-align: start/end`).
- `tokens.css`/themes (which *define* the palette) and `base`/`reset` (foundational) are exempt from the tokens/logical rules.

Wired into `pnpm lint` (and `pnpm lint:css` standalone), so it runs in the existing lint CI job.

## It already caught real drift
The rule flagged **`drawer.css` + `tooltip.css` using `:dir()`** — which needs Safari 16.4, so their RTL silently degrades below the documented floor (older Safari keeps the LTR slide/offset). These predate the `[dir="rtl"]` convention and were deliberate (graceful degradation), so they're **grandfathered** with a documented `stylelint-disable` + a tracked follow-up to convert them to `[dir="rtl"]` for full-floor RTL (drawer's tuned RTL-specificity dance wants its own test-backed PR).

## No-op cleanups
Two horizontal-rule `border-top` → `border-block-start` (identical in our writing mode — visual baselines pass unchanged); the steps check-glyph's *intentional* physical borders now carry a disable comment documenting why.

Mostly repo tooling — the only published delta is the no-op logical-property swap, hence the `patch` changeset.

author: carlos-verdes
body:
Closes #9.

Confirming a suggested classification. When the app suggests an unlabeled issue looks like a PRD or a Slice, a Confirm action in the "other open issues" bucket adds the corresponding `prd`/`slice` label via a GraphQL mutation and re-polls, so the issue is reclassified onto the board (or as a PRD) from then on. This is the manual tagging mechanism used while the upstream planning skills remain unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Suggested issues offer a confirm action — a Confirm button on `SuggestedPrd`/`SuggestedSlice` cards.
- [x] Confirming adds the `prd` or `slice` label via a GraphQL mutation (`addLabelsToLabelable`).
- [x] The board re-polls and the issue is reclassified accordingly (tier-1, leaves the bucket).
- [x] Confirmation failures surface a clear error and leave the issue unchanged (banner above the board; no mutation on failure).
- [x] The confirm-and-label use-case is tested against a fake `GitHubPort`.

## Layering

- **domain:** `IssueClassification::suggested_label` (pure) maps `SuggestedPrd → prd`, `SuggestedSlice → slice`, `None` otherwise.
- **application:** new `GitHubPort::add_label` seam + `BoardService::confirm_classification`, which derives the label, rejects a non-suggestion as `InvalidInput` before any call, and chains `repo`/`issue`/`label` context onto failures.
- **infrastructure:** `GitHubClient` resolves the issue and label node IDs then runs the mutation (mirroring `assign_self`). A label the repo does not define maps to a clear `NotFound` naming it (the planning skills don't emit `prd`/`slice` labels yet); a `FORBIDDEN` names the Issues read/write permission to grant without leaking GitHub's raw text.
- **presentation:** a `Confirm` button (with `aria-label`) emits `(number, classification)`; the board adds the label, re-polls, and surfaces failures in a banner.

## Tests

- domain: `suggested_label` table test.
- application/infrastructure: `confirm_classification.rs` against a fake `GitHubPort` — label forwarded per suggestion, non-suggestion rejected without a port call, failure surfaced with context.
- infrastructure: offline parser unit tests for the id/mutation responses and FORBIDDEN/missing-label error mapping.

Quality gate green: `cargo fmt`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `clippy -p zfirot --release -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`. No new Tailwind utilities (the button reuses existing classes), so `assets/tailwind.css` is unchanged.

author: tainan404
body:
### What does this PR do? Fixes the chat **reply preview** dropping text that comes before a link. When you reply to a message like `Hello https://example.com`, both previews — the "replying to" banner above the input and the quote inside the sent reply — showed only `https://example.com`, silently dropping the `Hello`. The culprit is `getFirstVisibleLineHtml` (`bigbluebutton-html5/.../chat/chat-graphql/service.ts`), which extracts the first line of the original message. It walked the message's nodes **in reverse** and treated the inline tags `` and `` as block-level, so it kept the *last* block (the link) and removed everything before it. This also affected text before inline code, text on both sides of a link, and lists (showed the last item instead of the first). The fix rewrites the extraction to walk the DOM **in document order** and truncate at the first real line break (a `\n` in a text node, a `
`, or the end of the first block element), keeping all inline content of the first line intact. ### Closes Issue(s) Closes bigbluebutton/bigbluebutton#25251 ### How to test 1. Send a public chat message: `Hello https://example.com` 2. Hover the message and click **Reply** 3. Check the "replying to" preview above the input → should show the full `Hello https://example.com`, not just the link 4. Send the reply, then check the quote inside the sent reply → should also show the full `Hello https://example.com` Automated: `npx playwright test chat/chat.spec.ts --grep "Reply to a message with text followed by a link"` (new scenario covering both previews).

Fixes #101.

`Atomic.judge()` skips the weld when the word after `and`/`then` ends in an adjective/adverb suffix. The suffix alternation omitted `-ate`, so `approximate` (and `appropriate`, `separate`, `accurate`) were mistaken for a second verb and the line welded.

## Change
- Added `ate` to the suffix alternation in `src/rules/atomic.js:42`.

## Trade-off
A genuine second verb ending in `-ate` (e.g. `validate`) will now be skipped — the inherent limit of the suffix heuristic, as noted in the issue.

<!-- Authored with Coder Agents on behalf of @Emyrk -->

Pre-parse realm scan + per-dataset game data wiring. Before full parsing, identify the realm from the combat log header, resolve it to a dataset, and pass a dataset-scoped `GameDB` to the parser.

- **`scanRealmName(logFormat, data)`** — format-aware pre-scan reads first ~200 lines to extract realm name from all 4 log formats: `REALM_INFO:` (v1), `|HEADER|` (v2), `H:` companion header (WoTLK), `CHRONICLE_HEADER` (AzerothCore). Skipped when `job.Args.RealmID` is already set (e.g. AzerothCore server-side uploads).
- **`Chronicle.resolveDataset`** — func field wired to `servicedataset.ResolveDatasetForRealm`. Follows server > tenant > default chain.
- **`Chronicle.gameDBForRealm(ctx, realmID)`** — resolves realm → dataset → `ForDataset()`. When resolver is nil or realm unknown, returns default WoWDB (zero overhead).
- **Vanilla v1 parser** widened from `*gamedb.WoWDB` to `gamedb.SpellFetcher` (safe: only passed to `synthetic.New()` which already accepts the interface)
- **`parseCombatLog()`** param changed from `*gamedb.WoWDB` to `gamedb.GameDB`
- **`resolveRealmByName()`** extracted so pre-scan can share the 3-tier resolution logic

<details><summary>Regression safety</summary>

All `default_dataset_id` columns are NULL → resolution always returns `DefaultDatasetID` → `ForDataset(DefaultDatasetID)` returns `w` itself (same pointer, same caches). Feature only activates when an admin assigns a non-default dataset to a server/tenant via the UI from PR #138.

</details>

<details><summary>Stack context</summary>

PR 5 of the dataset line. After dataset CRUD (#131), assignment (#138), per-dataset WoWDB (#139), and logparse refactor (#140), this wires the full path: log → realm scan → dataset resolution → scoped game data → parser.

author: ujeenet
body:
Closes #1040. `AggregateQuery` now carries a `joins` field, so Django's most common reporting shape — **group by a related column** (`values("author__name").annotate(n=Count("id"))`) — is expressible.

```rust
Post::objects()
    .join(Join { target: Author::SCHEMA, alias: "author", kind: Inner, on: aliased("author","id").eq(aliased("post","author")), .. })
    .aggregate()
    .group_by("author.name")
    .annotate("n", AggregateExpr::Count(None))
    .fetch(&pool).await?;
// SELECT "author"."name" AS "author__name", COUNT(*) AS "n"
// FROM post JOIN author AS author ON ... GROUP BY "author"."name"
```

## Implementation
- **IR**: new `AggregateQuery.joins` (+ `PartialEq`). The ~17 construction sites get `Vec::new()`; the scalar-aggregate path (`values.rs`) carries the compiled SELECT's joins so a scalar aggregate over a joined queryset also resolves.
- **Writer**: extracted the SELECT path's JOIN loop into a shared `write_model_joins` (emitted between FROM and WHERE — no duplication). New `write_agg_group_col` qualifies group/projection columns: dotted `alias.col` → `"alias"."col" AS "alias__col"`; bare col with joins present → `"table"."col"`; bare col, no joins → unchanged.
- **Builder**: `AggregateBuilder::compile` threads `qs.ad_hoc_joins` into the query and skips base-model validation for dotted group keys.

No new public API — the existing `.join().aggregate().group_by("author.name").annotate(...)` chain flows through.

## Tests

author: acgtun
body:
### Type of Change

- New Proposal

### Description

Proposal 148: make connectivity-affecting listener changes (type change, port change, adding or removing a listener) safe to roll out and roll back, for all listener types that provision per-broker Kubernetes resources (`nodeport`, `loadbalancer`, `cluster-ip`, `route`, `ingress`).

Today `KafkaReconciler` reconciles every per-broker listener resource up front (`listeners()`) and then rolls the pods one at a time. That leaves a window where a not-yet-rolled broker's `Service`/`Route`/`Ingress` already points at a listener the broker is not yet serving, so clients fail for the whole roll. On `nodeport`, a type-change rollback also re-allocates random node ports, which can move a port onto a different listener and cause SASL-mechanism mismatches that do not self-heal.

The proposal reconciles each broker's listener resources in lockstep with that broker's own restart, so each broker's resources always match the listener it is serving. It covers the `KafkaRoller` hook point, a per-broker convergence guard for idempotency/resumability, bootstrap-last handling, the internal-listener precondition, the KRaft-only correctness argument, an implementation sketch, a feature gate, testing, and rejected alternatives.

AI assistance was used to help structure and edit this proposal; the problem, design, trade-offs, and reasoning are my own (the work comes from a real listener-rollout incident).

## Problem D1→Postgres replication push fails on Deno Deploy with HTTP 500: ``` Cannot create proxy with a non-object as target or handler ``` This hits all replication streams (`users`, `admin_settings`, etc.) because ingest uses `db.prepare().bind().run()`, which previously called `postgres.js` `sql.unsafe(text, args)`. Health checks pass (`SELECT 1` uses tagged templates / no-arg `unsafe`), but any parameterized write — including replication upserts — fails under Deno Deploy's `npm:postgres` compat layer. ## Fix - Route parameterized D1 SQL through postgres.js **tagged template** emulation (`splitQuestionMarks` + `sql(strings, ...args)`) instead of `sql.unsafe(text, args)`. - Keep `unsafe()` for no-parameter statements (migrations DDL, etc.). - Apply the same path to failover write-log inserts. ## Files changed | File | Why | |------|-----| | `packages/api-node/src/bindings/db.ts` | `executeTranslatedSql()` helper; parameterized queries use tagged templates | | `packages/api-node/src/bindings/sqlDialect.ts` | `splitQuestionMarks()` for template string parts | | `packages/api-node/test/sqlDialect.test.ts` | Tests for placeholder splitting | ## Verify after deploy 1. Redeploy api-node to Deno (production). 2. Admin → **Push DB to Deno Postgres** (or wait for replication cron). 3. Expect `applied > 0`, `errors: []` in the ingest response.
  
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Refactor** * Improved database query execution by strengthening how SQL parameters are handled during prepared statement execution, improving reliability and consistency across read/write operations. * **Tests** * Added coverage for SQL placeholder parsing to ensure `?` tokens are correctly identified only when they appear outside quoted string literals, including proper handling of escaped quotes.

author: nbbshaw
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #441. With the scan moved to a background job, it still **overwhelmed the server** on real data — intermittent `502 Bad Gateway` on socket.io and the dashboard's `scan_status` polls while a scan ran. This makes the scan complete quickly without pegging the box.

## Root cause
Against the real dataset (~1,350 unlinked customers, ~600 projects, ~770 opportunities vs. the whole Shared Drive), the scan:
- fuzzy-matched **every record against every folder** — O(records × folders), millions of `SequenceMatcher` calls;
- re-resolved each project/opportunity's customer folder **per record**; and
- committed **thousands of inserts in a single transaction**.

That pegged CPU and held DB connections long enough that web/socket workers couldn't respond → 502s (including the dashboard's own status polls).

## Fix
- **Inverted token index** (`drive_match.token_index` + `blocked_candidates`): each record is scored only against folders that **share a word** with it, rarest token first so the cap never drops the likely match. Turns O(records × folders) into roughly linear.
- **Cache customer-folder resolution** per customer (many projects/opportunities share one).
- **Batched commits** (every 200 inserts) instead of one giant end-of-job transaction.
- The pure indexing/blocking logic is **unit-tested bench-free** (8 new tests in `tests/test_drive_match.py`).

## Verification
- 25 matcher/placement unit tests green; `py_compile` clean; version-sync at `1.34.5`.

## Deploy notes
- Pull + restart **workers** (so the queued job runs the new code). No `bench migrate`.
- A scan from the old code is currently stuck `running` on the server — the worker restart on deploy clears it; re-run **Scan** afterward (it clears prior un-applied rows first).
- Heads-up: this still stages ~2,700 candidate rows (one per unlinked record). The scan is now fast, but if that volume is noisy to review, a follow-up can add a **matched-only** mode (skip no-match records).

body:
Phase 3 (final) of the channel-UI coherence pass. Wires the five surfaces to each other along the lifecycle (configure channel → spawn agent → watch/chat), removes first-run dead-ends, and polishes the chat transcript. Branch off current `main`; do not merge until reviewed.

## Part A — lifecycle cross-actions
- **Agents spawn form** (`agents-ui.ts`): reads `?channel=<name>` on load, pre-selects that channel in the wake-channel `<select>` and auto-fills the agent name — so "Spawn" links from other surfaces land ready-to-go.
- **Config channel rows** (`admin-ui.ts`): each row gains **Spawn agent** (→ `MOUNT + /agents?channel=<name>`) and **Chat** (→ `MOUNT + /ui?channel=<name>`) ghost link-buttons (`.btn .btn-sm .btn-ghost`); Remove unchanged.
- **Home channel rows** (`home-ui.ts`): each row gains **spawn →** (→ `/agents?channel=<name>`) beside the existing chat →.
- **Agents running-agents table** (`agents-ui.ts`): rows gain **chat →**. `GET /api/agents` returns `{ name, session, attached }` — it does **not** carry the agent's wake channel — so chat links to `?channel=<agent.name>` (the default one-agent-one-channel case, where the spawn form auto-names the agent after its channel). No fabricated data.

## Part B — first-run / empty-state CTAs
- **Chat** (`daemon.ts`): when no `http-ui` channel is configured, the transcript shows a forward CTA ("Add a channel →" to Config, plus Home) and disables the composer — no dead-end.
- **Agents** (`agents-ui.ts`): when no channels exist, the spawn area surfaces a "Configure a channel first →" CTA.
- Home + Terminal already had forward CTAs — left as-is.

## Part C — chat message polish
- **Markdown**: `renderMarkdown(text)` added to `SHELL_JS` (`ui-kit.ts`) — a SMALL, XSS-safe subset: `escapeHtml` **first**, then fenced + inline code, bold, italic, http/https links (validated; `javascript:` rejected to inert text), and line breaks. No raw HTML passthrough. Chat bodies render through it. Reusable by Phase 4. `SHELL_JS` stays backtick-free (fence/inline markers built from char code 96). **7 unit tests** added to `ui-kit.test.ts` (escapes `<script>`, bold/italic, inline+fenced code, code-spans untouched by inline rules, link rendering, `javascript:` rejection, newlines).
- **Attachments** ⚠️: a reply's `files[]` is a `string[]` of **daemon-host file paths** (the bridge documents reply files as absolute paths). There is **no endpoint that serves a reply attachment as a downloadable blob** — `POST /api/download` goes the *other* direction (Telegram `file_id` → server-local path) and requires `channel:write`, which the chat token (`channel:read channel:send`) lacks. So names render clearly (basename shown, full path in `title`) with a code comment; downloadability is left for a backend follow-up rather than inventing a route.
- **Permission approve/deny** ⚠️: permission bubbles gain Approve / Deny buttons. **There is no verdict endpoint today** — the existing `/api/permission` is the *outbound* prompt (bridge → channel, `transport.sendPermission`, `channel:write`), not a verdict sink; the verdict path (`ctx.emitPermissionVerdict` → bridges/MCP sessions) has no HTTP route the browser can call. And the chat token is `channel:read channel:send` only. So the buttons record the choice in-UI and explain that submitting needs a verdict route + a `channel:write` token — **flagged, not faked. The auth gate is not weakened.**

## Flagged for follow-up
1. **Permission verdicts from chat** need (a) a daemon verdict endpoint that calls `ctx.emitPermissionVerdict`, and (b) a token scope that authorizes it. The chat's `channel:send` token can't drive `channel:write`.
2. **Attachment downloads** need a `channel:read`-scoped blob-serving route for reply file paths; the current `/api/download` is the wrong direction + scope.

## Verification
- `bun run typecheck` → only the 2 pre-existing `src/bridge.ts` TS2589 errors.
- `bun test` → **426 pass / 0 fail** (telegram/vault 401/ECONNREFUSED/500 = documented fixture noise).
- Page-integrity probe → all five pages start `<!doctype`, end `</html>`, include `app-nav`, length > 5000. `SHELL_JS` backtick-free; `renderMarkdown` present.
- Terminal CONTENT pane untouched (still `--term-bg` / `#000000`).

## Problema
Ecrã preto após merge do PR #31 — o `createClient` do Supabase crasha ao arrancar sem variáveis de ambiente (GitHub Pages não as tinha injectadas no build).

## Correções

### Crítico — ecrã preto e perda de dados
- **`supabase.ts`**: fallback `'placeholder'` evita crash ao arrancar sem env vars; a app fica em modo local-only sem erros visíveis
- **`deploy.yml`**: passa `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` e `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` ao build via GitHub Secrets (tens de as adicionar em Settings → Secrets → Actions)
- **`sync.ts`**: deleções locais propagam ao Supabase — após upsert, faz `DELETE` das rows que já não existem localmente (evita itens apagados ressuscitarem no próximo pull)
- **`useAuth.ts`**: no `SIGNED_IN`, inverter ordem para `pullAll` → `pushAll` — evita sobrescrever dados remotos com dados locais vazios num dispositivo novo

### Alta prioridade
- **`useAuth.ts`**: URL de redirect inclui `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` — corrige o path `/new-life/` no GitHub Pages
- **`sync.ts`**: `getSession()` em vez de `getUser()` — evita chamada de rede em cada `saveJSON`
- **`sync.ts`**: guard `if (pulling) return false` — evita race condition em chamadas concorrentes a `pullAll`
- **`schema.sql`**: PK `(user_id, id)` em vez de `(id, user_id)` — índice eficiente para queries por `user_id`

### Média prioridade
- **`sync.ts`**: comparação de datas via `Date.getTime()` em vez de string lexicográfica
- **`sync.ts`**: log explícito de erros no pull (separado do `continue`)
- **`ProfilePage.tsx`**: estado `isSigningIn` desactiva botão e mostra spinner durante envio do OTP

## Action necessária
Adicionar os secrets ao GitHub:
1. Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret
2. `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` = `https://hrlcgsbmwdcuxbbojage.supabase.co`
3. `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` = (a tua chave)

Depois do merge, o deploy vai reconstruir com as variáveis correctas e o sync vai funcionar.

Adds the `cicd/packer-build` Crossplane Configuration — the Packer sibling of `cicd/ansible-run`. This is **layer 3** of stuttgart-things/stage-time#51 (layers 1 & 2 — the Tekton task/pipeline + KCL modules — are in stuttgart-things/stage-time#52).

## What it does
Turns a namespaced `PackerBuild` XR (`resources.stuttgart-things.com/v1alpha1`) into a Tekton `PipelineRun` (`build-packer-template`) that runs Packer to build a VM template / golden image. The PipelineRun is rendered by `function-kcl` from `oci://ghcr.io/stuttgart-things/kcl-tekton-pr-packer` and wrapped in a `kubernetes.m.crossplane.io/v1alpha1` Object applied via provider-kubernetes.

- **`apis/definition.yaml`** — `PackerBuild` XRD. Separates pipeline-definition refs (`pipelineRepoUrl`/`pipelineRevision`/`pipelinePath` → stage-time) from template-source refs (`gitRepoUrl`/`gitRevision`/`gitWorkspaceSubdirectory` → `stuttgart-things/stuttgart-things`), with `osVersion`/`lab`/`provisioning` selectors. Status surfaces `templateName`.
- **`apis/composition.yaml`** — `load-environment → render-pipelinerun (kcl-tekton-pr-packer:0.1.0) → derive-status → ready`. `derive-status` reads the PipelineRun's `template-name` result onto `status.templateName`.
- **`examples/`** — `xr`/`xr-min`/`xr-max`, `functions`, `configuration`, `environmentconfig`.

`render-pipelinerun` pins `kcl-tekton-pr-packer:0.1.0`. author: dakejahl
body:
## Summary

After mavlink-router's StartLimit give-up (added in v1.0.2/v1.0.3) leaves a service in `failed`, the web UI offered no way to restart it. This restores that.

## Problem

The Services page rendered a Start button only for `service.active === 'inactive'`, so a `failed` unit — e.g. mavlink-router after giving up with no flight controller — showed neither Start nor Stop, and couldn't be recovered from the UI. And even with a button, `systemctl start` is refused on a unit that hit its StartLimit until `reset-failed` runs, so the start path would have no-opped anyway.

## Solution

Show the Start button for any non-running state (`service.active !== 'active'`), and have `start_service` run `systemctl reset-failed` before `start`. Verified on the device that `reset-failed` is authorized for the service user via the existing per-unit `manage-units` polkit grant, and that the sequence relaunches a given-up unit with its restart counter reset to 0.

author: clovenbradshaw-ctrl
body:
## What this is

A design note (`docs/document-explorer.md`) capturing the pivot from a **chat-with** app to an **explore** app: the rich graph the engine already induces is rendered as an **x-ray of the document**, navigable on two axes, and a new **graph of significance between documents** develops as a corpus accretes.

No code changes — this is the architecture/spec, written to lock direction before building.

## The core idea

- **Vertical axis = resolution.** A dial over the engine's three existing domains (Existence → Structure → Significance) — from raw segmentation at the floor up to relations and LLM-level inference at the ceiling. Chooses which strata of an already-computed graph are drawn; re-runs nothing.
- **Horizontal axis = time, which *shifts*.** One scrubber pointing at three clocks depending on selection: ingestion time (graph assembling), reasoning time (the existing per-turn MRI), and corpus time (how the between-document graph grew).
- **The new layer = a corpus significance graph.** Cross-document entity reconciliation plus weighted edges. Four edge signals, phased: shared entities + citations (phase 1, already computable), thematic gravity via `embed.js` (phase 2), contradiction (phase 3).

## How it maps onto what exists

Most of this is latent in the codebase already — the operator ladder, the per-turn scrubber in `eomri.jsx`, the append-only `_events` log, per-doc `graphSnapshot`. The genuinely new work is the cross-document layer. Proposed as additive: a fourth `explore` layout mode, a new `explorer.jsx` view, and one pure dependency-injected engine module `corpus.js` (mirroring the `composition.js` precedent — Node-testable with fakes, no WebGPU, byte-exact parity preserved).

## Build order

Five shippable slices: corpus engine (phase-1 edges, no UI) → static Explore view → vertical axis → horizontal axis → deeper edges. Chat folds back in at slice 2 as a per-node lens rather than the front door.

See the doc for the data model, the seams, and the open questions (edge thresholds, scale/level-of-detail, corpus-time provenance).

author: agentydragon
body:
Builds on the PR 2250/2251 work (selector candidate index + recursive minimizer start) into a working minimizer for `debundle spec synthesize-selectors`.

## What this does
Turns rebuild-fragile `binding.name` minified-name pins into minimal, forward-compatible structural `source_match` / `binding_groups` selectors: keep the meaningful, stable anchors (literals, method/callee names, config `key: value`s) that uniquely identify the target among its chunk siblings; hole the incidental/volatile rest (`ANYTHING`/`STMT_LIST`/`OBJECT_PROPS`/`CLASS_REST`/`DECLARATORS_*`).

## Architecture
- **Holing is an AST→AST prune, not a hand-written serializer.** `hole_expr`/`hole_stmts`/`hole_object`/`hole_class_members` clone the target's swc subtree and drop in marker nodes; the selector is serialized by swc codegen (`js_ast::emit_module_source`). Selector and code are the same AST.
- **Anchor selection** is a tiered minimum set cover (`cover_competitors` + `min_set_cover` B&B): shallow literals → structural key/member presence → deeper literals. Each anchor's exclusion set comes from the production matcher, so discrimination is exact; the chosen union is proven once.
- Covers function bodies, object literals, class bodies, var declarator groups, and group-vs-standalone partitioning.
- Source-match hole keyword constants factored into a shared `source_match_holes` library.

## Tests
- `selector_minimizer_expectation_test`: 7/7 motivating cases, compared **through swc** (parse + re-emit, so formatting-agnostic).
- `selector_codemod_test`: swc-native property test (gate 1: every synthesized selector re-matches uniquely to the intended target).
- `selector_codemod_cli_test` green (anchor-quality guarantees preserved).

## Dogfood
First run over a large real spec (see `debug/selector_minimizer_dogfood.md`): ~84% of name-pins convert to proven structural selectors. Follow-ups in flight: whole-document-serde apply (replacing the buggy text-edit path), path unification + legacy-renderer retirement, `perf`-pinpointed index-prefilter for scale, a `--full-ast-fallback` (default off) switch, and broader property coverage.

author: aadsit7
body:
Fixes a false positive: Randy answered an incomplete utterance — "how does recast…" — that trailed off before the actual question landed. A solution engineer waits for the whole ask. This stops it in three layers:

1. **`isTruncatedQuestion()`** flags fragments that trail off on a dangling word (interrogative / auxiliary / modal / article / preposition / conjunction) or match `"<wh> <do|modal> <subject>"` / `"<do|modal> <subject>"` with no predicate ("how does Recast", "what can Intune", "does Intune"). Copulas (is/are/was/were) are intentionally **excluded** so genuine short questions survive — "what is Recast", "is it supported".
2. **Longer quiet-gap** (`DEBOUNCE_SLOW_MS = 2600ms`) when the buffer still looks truncated, so the rest of the question can arrive and assemble before flushing.
3. **Hard gate in `flushAssistBuffer`**: a still-truncated candidate is neither answered nor classified — the continuation comes through as its own utterance.
4. **Classifier prompt** gains a completeness rule as defense-in-depth for semantically-incomplete asks the regex can't see ("how does Recast deploy").

## Testing
Unit-tested the heuristic:
- Truncated (correctly blocked): "how does recast", "what can intune", "why would configmgr", "…handle patching for", "tell me how", "can you explain the", "what about the".
- Complete (correctly allowed): "what is recast", "how does recast handle third party patching", "can right click tools remote control a device", "is it supported in hybrid environments", "how do I deploy a win32 app with intune".

Full-script Node syntax check passes. No change to wake-word/conversation routing or typed chat.

author: cleanunicorn
body:
## What & why

The single most-viewed pixels on the site — the hero — currently show a static role line. This turns it into a **signature terminal moment** that makes the page memorable in the first second and ties the whole "terminal theme" directly to your security identity:

```
~$ whoami
Security Researcher | Investor | Builder▮
```

The role line **types itself out** after the `~$ whoami` prompt, trailed by a blinking block cursor.

## How it's built (and why it's safe)

- **Progressive enhancement.** The full role text is in the HTML, so it's fully readable with **no JS** and indexable by crawlers. The script only *animates* what's already there.
- **Accessibility.** The prompt and cursor are `aria-hidden`; screen readers just read the role line. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, both the typing and the blink are disabled (text shows instantly).
- **Tiny & dependency-free.** `static/js/hero-type.js` is ~900 bytes of vanilla JS, loaded `defer`.

## Files

- `layouts/index.html` — prompt / roles / cursor markup + deferred script tag (home only).
- `static/js/hero-type.js` — the typewriter (new).
- `assets/css/z-home.css` — prompt color + blinking-cursor styles, reusing theme variables.

## Relationship to the open WebGL PRs (#1, #2)

This is intended as a **lighter, accessible alternative** to the full-screen WebGL background in #1/#2: it delivers the "this site stands out / hackerish" goal with a few hundred bytes, no GPU shader, no full-page canvas, and clean reduced-motion behavior — rather than a sitewide animated background. Happy to take whichever direction you prefer; they're not mutually exclusive.

## Verification

Local `hugo` build (extended 0.140.2): hero renders the prompt, role line and cursor; `/js/hero-type.js` is served and referenced; cursor CSS is compiled into the bundle. Touches only homepage assets — no conflict with the 404, structured-data or stats PRs.

author: resistor52
body:
## What

`--search` supports Grok (xAI) web search since #2092, but `fabric --help` still shows:

```
--search    Enable web search tool for supported models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini)
```

The capability works (`-V GrokAI -m grok-4.3 --search` grounds correctly), but the help text, shell completions, and README still omit Grok, so the support is undiscoverable.

## Root cause

`--help` renders flag descriptions from the i18n message catalog, not the go-flags struct tag. `internal/cli/help.go` maps the flag to a key:

```go
"search": "enable_web_search_tool",
```

#2092 updated the struct tag in `internal/cli/flags.go` (`...Gemini, Grok)`) but not the catalog value, so the rendered help kept the old vendor list.

## Change

Append `Grok` to the `enable_web_search_tool` value in all 11 locales (matching each locale's list separator, including the full-width `、` for `ja`/`zh` and the Arabic comma for `fa`), the zsh and fish completions, and the generated README help block. No functional change; 14 files, one line each.

## Test plan

- `go build ./cmd/fabric && ./fabric --help | grep -- --search` now shows `(Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Grok)`.
- `go test ./internal/i18n/...` passes.

**SpecialistAvatar:** `SPARK_COLORS` hex array replaced with `CX_REWARD`, `CX_ACCENT`, `CX_ACCENT_BRIGHT` imports from `cx-tokens`.

## Before / After
- **Before:** `style={{ color: "var(--cx-accent, #7C6CFF)" }}` — canonical value duplicated as a fallback in every component
- **After:** `style={{ color: "var(--cx-accent)" }}` — single source of truth in `console-tokens.css`, no duplication

grep -r '#7C6CFF\|#0B0B0F\|#131319\|#F4F4F7\|#34D399\|#F4607D' src/

- Replaces `ProviderFactory` + `Registry` with a `Pool` that manages lazy insecure gRPC connections keyed by endpoint, with a name→endpoint index so existing reconciler call sites are unchanged

- `internal/provider/pool.go` — connection pool with `Get(endpoint)`, `Register/Unregister(name)`, `GetByName(name)`, `Release`, lifecycle via `manager.Runnable`
- `internal/provider/provider.go` — `Registry` type removed

author: hybridthegamer
body:
Elements marked [data-reveal] were staying invisible on mobile because
useScrollReveal only used IntersectionObserver with a 0.15 threshold
and never checked whether elements were already in the viewport on mount.
Anything above the fold (login hero, Dinner Night card) remained at
opacity 0 indefinitely.

Fix A — useScrollReveal: immediately reveal elements whose top edge is
already inside window.innerHeight on mount; switch to threshold 0.08
and rootMargin 0px 0px -40px 0px for off-screen elements; apply the
hidden state via JS inline styles (not only CSS) so the hook owns the
full reveal lifecycle; add SSR-safe fallback that forces all elements
visible if window is unavailable.

Fix D — GrainOverlay: replace `inset: 0` with explicit top/left/
width/height and add userSelect: none to match the required canvas
style spec.

No changes to lib/, app/api/, bam-tokens.css, or any business logic.
Build: zero TS errors, zero ESLint errors.

## Workstreams

**B — Sync/network errors surfaced (was: swallowed)**
New `SyncDiagnostics` records every previously-dropped failure; the server error body is captured in `OutboxReplayHttpException`; the global banner shows the reason ("Some changes didn't sync — HTTP 422: …"); `retry()` no longer swallows and drains inline; a debug "Sync log" screen sits under the More hub.

**C — Offline-first launch ("logs in every time")**
A returning user renders from the cached session immediately — even with a stale access token — and the refresh runs in the background. Only a *definitive* refresh-token rejection (401) bounces to sign-in; transient/offline failures keep the user in on cached data.

**D — Instant local-write reflection (no event bus)**
New `LocalWriteBus` emitted from every optimistic mirror write; the dashboard force-refreshes (debounced) so logging reflects without waiting for a TTL/resume.

## What

Tightens the `status` param on `list_kitchen_tickets` (`src/tools/kitchen.ts:45`) and `update_kitchen_ticket` (`:116`) from permissive `z.string().optional()` to `z.enum(...).optional()`, so agents can't send an arbitrary status string that the ERP API will reject downstream.

## Verified status set (NOT the assumed set)

The audit assumed `queued, preparing, ready, served, cancelled`. The **real** canonical set from the ERP is:

```ts
// Frihet-ERP/apps/kitchen/src/types.ts:15
export type KitchenTicketStatus = 'on_hold' | 'queued' | 'preparing' | 'ready' | 'served' | 'voided';
```

Two material differences vs the assumption:
- `on_hold` exists (was missing from the assumed set)
- The terminal cancel state is `voided`, **not** `cancelled` — confirmed by the ERP functions writing `status: 'voided'` (`functions/src/kitchen/aggregator-ingestion.ts:826`); `cancelled` appears nowhere in the kitchen ticket domain.

Used the verified set. Updated the `.describe()` bilingual text to match (the old text listed `cancelled`, which would now mislead an agent into sending a value the enum rejects).
