## Summary

Cost/speed optimizations for the ingestion pipeline plus support for Microsoft Office documents, on one branch.

### #311 — First-pages enrichment (cost/speed)
Cheap LLM enrichment tasks now read only the first pages of a document instead of a flat character slice, via a page-aware `_head_pages` helper:
- `doc_metadata`: first ~2 pages / ~6k chars
- `doc_classify`: first ~3 pages / ~8k chars
Full text is still used for chunking/embeddings, the regex entity extractor, and NER. Budgets are in-code constants. Feature versions were intentionally not bumped, so this applies to newly ingested/reprocessed documents (no costly retroactive re-run).

### #312 — Drop low-value entity types
The regex entity extractor no longer emits MONEY, DATE, INVOICE_ID, CONTRACT_ID, DOCUMENT_ID (≈90% noise). It now emits only EMAIL and URL; NER still emits PERSON/ORG/GPE and the lexical extractor still emits CUSTOM_TOKEN. Enum values are kept for back-compat but marked not-extracted. One-time migration `0030_drop_low_value_entities.sql` deletes existing rows of the five dropped types.

### #313 — Office document support (docx/xlsx/pptx)
Office OOXML documents are converted to PDF on ingest by a local Gotenberg container (gotenberg/gotenberg:8, MIT, official Docker image) wrapping headless LibreOffice — fully local, no document egress. New `DocumentNormalizer` port + `GotenbergNormalizer` adapter; the extraction service routes office MIMEs through the normalizer to a PDF and reuses the existing PDF extract/OCR/render/thumbnail path.
- The original file is preserved immutably (`original.<ext>`); the converted PDF is the canonical viewable form (`normalized/searchable.pdf`, recorded as `system_document`).
- Preview shows office docs inline via their normalized PDF (like native PDFs); "Open in new tab" opens that PDF; "Download" returns the original file.
- Thumbnails, page images, and the OCR overlay all derive from `system_document`, so they work uniformly.
- New settings: `DOKTOK_GOTENBERG_URL` (default http://localhost:3000) and compose port override `DOKTOK_GOTENBERG_PORT`. `docker-compose.yml` adds a `gotenberg` service.

### Documentation
Architecture doc, new ADR-0019 (office docs via local Gotenberg), README (supported file types + entity changes), operations/running.md (Gotenberg startup), CHANGELOG, and milestones updated.

## Known follow-up
Issue #314 (structured_records silently truncates very long documents to the first 16k chars, dropping the tail of transactions) is a known follow-up and intentionally not addressed here.

Closes #311
Closes #312
Closes #313

body:
Seventh step of the CH→DuckDB migration. One-time per-model migration: streams every user table from the two ClickHouse databases (sem + raw) into a DuckDB file via Arrow zero-copy, then verifies row-count + per-column null-count parity. After a clean pass on every table, Phase 8's config flip is safe.

## What lands

### \`tools/migrate_ch_to_duckdb.py\`
- \`_list_user_tables\` — pull every non-View table from a CH database via \`system.tables\`.
- \`_migrate_one_table\` — COUNT in CH; \`query_arrow\` into \`pyarrow.Table\`; DROP/CREATE in DuckDB via \`FROM arrow_table\` zero-copy; COUNT in DuckDB; optional per-column null-count comparison.
- \`migrate\` — walk sem then raw; surface name collisions across DBs as errors on the second occurrence (no silent clobbering).
- \`TableReport\` dataclass: \`parity_ok\` is True only when no error and row counts match. Null mismatches are warnings.
- Click CLI: \`--model-dir\`, full CH connection options (env-resolvable), \`--tables\` filter for partial re-runs, \`--no-null-check\` for huge tables, \`--strict\` to promote null warnings to exit 2. Exit 1 on row mismatch or load error.

\`FakeCHClient\` holds \`{(db, table): pyarrow.Table}\` and parses the SQL the migration emits. Covers table discovery, scope-by-database, happy-path copy, stale-target drop, error capture, null parity, sem-then-raw ordering, \`--tables\` filter, cross-DB name-collision detection.

`_register_registry_blocks` iterates the live dispatch registry (`get_registry_for_type(Block)`) while `await`-ing DB writes. author: htownz
body:
## What

Implements the **"model later" half** of `weather-trader`'s hybrid forecaster: a learned per-station `bias_f` correction derived from accumulated forecast→actual residuals. Builds on the scaffold merged in #23.

## The closed loop

```
scan --log ──► forecasts.jsonl
                    │  (after each day settles)
backfill --out ──► residuals.jsonl
                    │
calibrate --out ──► calibration.json ──► scan/forecast --calibration
```

## How the correction works

Group residuals by `(station, metric)` and compute:

```
bias_f = clamp( mean(actual − predicted) )      # applied only when n ≥ min_samples
```

That's the additive correction that, to first order, minimizes the corrected prediction's squared error. The same residuals also yield a per-station `sigma_f` (residual spread).

- **`bias_f`** shifts *every* scenario (ensemble + synthetic paths), so it always applies.
- **`sigma_f`** only widens/narrows the *synthetic* fallback spread — a real ensemble keeps its own empirical spread.
- **Gated** by `--min-samples` (default 5) and **clamped** by `--clamp` (default ±8°F) so a couple of noisy days can't swing the model.
- Unit of correction is `(station, metric)`; lead-time / regime splits are a deliberate future refinement.

## Changes

- **`calibration.py`** (new): `derive_calibration()`, `Calibration` (with `bias_for` / `sigma_for` lookups + JSON save/load), `load_residuals()`.
- **`forecast.py`**: `forecast_for_station` gains a `forecast_sigma_f` passthrough so a calibrated spread reaches the synthetic fallback. (`bias_f` was already plumbed.)
- **`cli.py`**: new **`calibrate`** command (rich report + `--json`); **`--calibration`** flag on `scan` and `forecast` resolves `bias_f`/`sigma_f` per station+metric and threads it through the *same* scenario interface — zero changes to pricing/grading.
- **README**: documents the calibration loop and the updated "blend now, learned correction on top" section.

## Tests

```
46 passed   (38 prior + 8 new)
```

New offline tests cover: bias = mean residual, min-sample gating, clamping, sigma from spread, unknown-station → 0, JSON round-trip, residuals reader, and an integration test asserting a learned +2°F bias shifts a bracket's fair probability.

## Safety / behavior

Inert until real residuals exist: with no calibration file (or sub-threshold samples) `bias_f = 0`, so **blend-mode behavior is unchanged** by default. The learned correction only kicks in once you've accumulated live runs and explicitly pass `--calibration`.

> Still gated on egress (`api.weather.gov`, `api.elections.kalshi.com`, `ensemble-api.open-meteo.com`) to gather the live residuals that feed this. Draft until then.

author: javiercm1410
body:
## Why

Many projects often share same secret value (an API key, a shared credential, a connection string) in more than one service. Previously a service could only reference its own `<app>/<env>` secret, which forced teams to duplicate the same value into every service's secret: extra copies to keep in sync, manual copy steps, and rotation that has to touch N places instead of one.

External secret references let any service point an env var at a shared secret by name and key (`KEY = { secret = "shared/name", key = "JSON_KEY" }`). The value is stored once and consumed by as many services as need it, keeping a single source of truth (typically Terraform-managed), eliminating manual duplication, and making rotation a one-place change.

## What changed

**New inline-table syntax in `[<env>.secrets]` / `[global.secrets]`:**

```toml
[stage.secrets]
# Existing form (unchanged) — resolves to <app>/<env>:<key>
SESSION_SECRET = "SESSION_SECRET"

# New form — references a named secret in Secrets Manager
CLAUDE_API_KEY = { secret = "anthropic/stage", key = "CLAUDE_API_KEY" }

# Full ARN passthrough (for cross-account or legacy ARNs)
SOME_KEY = { secret = "arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:123456789012:secret:my-secret", key = "SOME_KEY" }
```

**`pkg/app/config.go`** — new `SecretRef` struct; `NormalizeSecretRefs` handles both the string form and the new inline-table form. `NormalizeSecrets` (the old entry point) now delegates to `NormalizeSecretRefs` and rejects external refs at call sites that don't support them (build-time secrets path unchanged).

**`pkg/ecs/config.go`** — new `secretValueFrom` helper builds the ECS `ValueFrom` ARN:
- no `secret` field → `arn:...:secret:<app>/<env>:<key>::` (existing behavior)
- `secret` is a bare name → `arn:...:secret:<name>:<key>::`
- `secret` starts with `arn:` → used as-is

`ResolveSecrets` updated to call `NormalizeSecretRefs` so both `[global.secrets]` and `[<env>.secrets]` blocks can carry external refs.

Build-time secrets (`build_secrets`) explicitly reject external refs with a clear error.

Backward compatible: all existing `KEY = "JSON_KEY"` string entries resolve identically to before.

## Testing

1. **Unit tests:**
   ```
   go test ./pkg/app/... ./pkg/ecs/...
   ```
   Key tests to watch: `TestNormalizeSecretRefs`, `TestNormalizeSecretsRejectsExternalRef`, `TestLoadAppConfigExternalSecretTOML`, `TestResolveSecretsExternal`.

2. **Manual — resolve a secret reference:**
   Add an external ref to any `deploy/config.toml`:
   ```toml
   [stage.secrets]
   MY_KEY = { secret = "my-shared-secret", key = "MY_KEY" }
   ```
   Then run:
   ```
   ops ecs secrets -a <app> -e <env>
   ```
   Confirm the `ValueFrom` column shows `arn:aws:secretsmanager:...:secret:my-shared-secret:MY_KEY::` (the named secret ARN), not the service-scoped `<app>/<env>` ARN.

3. **IAM note:** The ECS execution role must have `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` on the external secret ARN. This is a Terraform concern — no IAM code is touched in this PR. Without the permission, the ECS task will fail to start at runtime.

## Evidence

**Unit tests — `pkg/app` (all passing):**

```
$ go test -v ./pkg/app/... 2>&1 | grep -E 'RUN|PASS|FAIL|ok'
=== RUN   TestNormalizeSecrets
=== RUN   TestNormalizeSecretRefs
=== RUN   TestNormalizeSecretsRejectsExternalRef
=== RUN   TestLoadAppConfigExternalSecretTOML
...
--- PASS: TestNormalizeSecretsRejectsExternalRef (0.00s)
--- PASS: TestLoadAppConfigExternalSecretTOML (0.00s)
--- PASS: TestNormalizeSecretRefs (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestNormalizeSecretRefs/nil_input (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestNormalizeSecretRefs/inline_table_with_no_key_defaults_to_envVar (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestNormalizeSecretRefs/external_inline_table (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestNormalizeSecretRefs/key-only_inline_table (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestNormalizeSecretRefs/string_map (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestNormalizeSecretRefs/slice_of_strings (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestNormalizeSecretRefs/unknown_field_in_inline_table (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestNormalizeSecretRefs/non-string_secret_field (0.00s)
--- PASS: TestNormalizeSecrets (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestNormalizeSecrets/nil_input (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestNormalizeSecrets/string_slice (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestNormalizeSecrets/string_map (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestNormalizeSecrets/external_secret_ref_rejected (0.00s)
```

author: byk
body:
## Problem

Warm-up overhead vastly exceeds recorded savings on the costs dashboard (user observed e.g. **\$8.19 warmup cost vs \$0.37 savings**). Root cause was **two cost-accounting bugs**, not warming aggressiveness — confirmed empirically against production data.

### Evidence (production DB)
| Finding | Value |
|---|---|
| Phantom savings: hits + \$ where `totalWarmups`=0 | **56 sessions, 725 "hits", \$350 (77% of all warmup savings)** |
| cost-tracker `warmup_hits` vs `warmup_state.warmupHits` | 1067 vs 361 (~3× divergence) |
| Savings per real hit (recorded) | **\$0.30** |
| Savings per real hit (expected, 168K Opus prefix) | **~\$2.90** (~10× higher) |

## Bugs & fixes

**Bug A — phantom savings via session-identity mismatch.** Hit attribution gated only on `lastWarmupAt`, which rides in the persisted/inherited `warmup_state` blob. A session that never fired (nor paid for) a warmup could book savings while the matching cost lived under a different session ID. **Fix:** only credit a hit when the session provably paid — `totalWarmups > 0 && lastWarmupRefreshTokens > 0`.

**Bug B — ~10× savings undercount.** Savings were credited against the returning turn's `cacheReadInputTokens` (often a tool-use continuation with a small read), not the full prefix the warmup refreshed. **Fix:** persist the warmup's refreshed `cache_read` tokens and credit against that.

## Changes
- Add optional `lastWarmupRefreshTokens` to `WarmupState` (carried in the existing `warmup_state` JSON blob — **no schema migration**).
- Extract a pure, testable `creditWarmupHit()` helper; pipeline calls it.
- Defense-in-depth: scrub stale credit on restore when `totalWarmups===0`.
- Persist warmup state on **eviction** (was only persisted by the 30s flush; eviction could drop a just-earned refresh credit).
- `recordWarmupHit` warns (does not drop) on zero in-process warmup cost — observability backstop that tolerates cross-restart attribution.

## Notes
- Existing corrupt historical rows are left as-is (the true payer can't be rejoined post-hoc); new sessions self-correct.
- Underwent an adversarial review pass; M1/M2/M3 findings (test discrimination + eviction persistence) addressed in this PR.
- **Bug C** (tool-call fast path over-firing — 24 sessions, 74 warmups, 0 hits) is a separate follow-up, not included here.

## Testing
- `pnpm run typecheck` clean; **2989 tests pass** (6 skipped); `biome` clean.
- New/extended tests: pure `creditWarmupHit` (phantom guard, token source, consume/no-double-credit), `executeWarmup` producer (full/partial/uncached refresh credit), savings formula scaling, and eviction persistence regression.

💡 What: Refactored `getAdminAnalytics` in `backend/src/controllers/analytics.controller.js` to batch independent database queries (e.g. `User.countDocuments`, `History.aggregate`) and execute them concurrently using `Promise.all()`.
🎯 Why: Running these queries sequentially causes cumulative I/O latency, delaying the overall request response time unnecessarily.
📊 Impact: Expected to reduce the I/O blocking time and overall latency of the analytics dashboard fetch by executing them concurrently.
🔬 Measurement: Verify by measuring the request duration for `/api/analytics` via an API testing tool or profiling before and after the change.

author: thecsdoctor
body:
⚡ **Bolt: [Memoize GraphTheme to JSON conversion]**

💡 **What:** Added a module-level cache in `react/theme/toEngineTheme.ts` to memoize the conversion of a `GraphTheme` object to its engine-ready JSON format. It caches the last seen theme reference and returns the same JSON object if called again with the exact same reference.

🎯 **Why:** Even though `GraphScene` uses `useMemo` to memoize the output of this function within its component lifecycle, identity drops (e.g. if the parent component re-creates the reference or if the component unmounts and remounts, or the function is called across multiple component instances simultaneously) can still cause unnecessary, deep object conversions of the exact same configuration, causing performance overhead in the bridge communicating with the WASM engine. Module-level caching guarantees no duplicate work for stable configuration objects.

📊 **Impact:** Reduces object creation and garbage collection pressure when the GraphScene re-renders frequently (such as during hovering, panning, or parent state updates) while the underlying theme hasn't changed.

🔬 **Measurement:** Verified that all existing unit tests in `react/theme/toEngineTheme.test.ts` still pass identically without regressions.

Added documentation of the anti-pattern and optimization to the Bolt playbook (`.jules/bolt.md`).

author: youw
body: The RTP static source built a gortsplib rtpreceiver.Receiver with UnrealiableTransport enabled but never called Initialize(), so the reorder buffer was inert. Initialize it by default (buffer size 64, matching the RTSP and WebRTC sources) and expose a new path-level parameter rtpReorderQueueSize: unset = default size (64); 0 = reordering disabled (previous behavior); N = explicit buffer size (power of two, <= 16384). Applies to udp+rtp and unixgram+rtp; the deprecated unix+rtp source is left unchanged (never reorders).

author: csakos1
body:
## Summary

End-to-end manual "mark rounded" (*bója megvan*) control: a phone button **and**
a watch hold-to-confirm page that advance the active mark on demand,
independently of GPS coordinates. Implements ADR 0024.

## Why

On the 2026-06-06 Balaton test the race committee gave imprecise buoy
coordinates (~100–150 m off). The boat rounded the *real* buoy, so its closest
approach to the *entered* point stayed above the `MarkRoundingDetector`'s 50 m
gate — the detector never fired and the app navigated to mark 1 for the entire
race. A coordinate-independent manual advance fixes this; a proper auto-fix
(bearing-sweep) is deferred to Phase 9.

## What changed

**Domain / engine**
- `RaceEngine.applyRoundMarkCommand()` — the manual counterpart of the auto
  `_maybeRoundMark`: resets the detector and `roundCurrentMark`s; no-op when not
  active (auto-finishes on the last mark).

**Phone**
- "Bója megvan" button on `LiveRaceScreen` (active only, confirm dialog) →
  `sendDataToTask({type:'roundMark'})`.
- The engine-isolate `RaceEngineTaskHandler` also subscribes to the round-mark
  `EventChannel` and applies the command — so the watch button works with the
  phone pocketed / screen-off (the UI isolate is suspended then).
- l10n keys for the button + dialog.

**Native bridge (`wearable_bridge`)**
- Now bidirectional: watch → phone `MessageClient` on `/round-mark` (fire-once
  command, not a latched `DataItem`); the phone registers the listener only
  while the round-mark `EventChannel` has a subscriber (the service isolate).

**Watch UI**
- New third PageView page (C): a circular teal press-and-hold (~1 s) button with
  a filling ring. Send-tick haptic on hold-complete, a stronger haptic once the
  next payload's mark name changes (round-trip aware), "Nincs kapcsolat" + haptic
  on send failure, ~2 s debounce. A<->B<->C navigation, three page dots.

**Docs**
- ADR 0024 + ARCHITECTURE.md sync: §8.9 command protocol (adds `roundMark`,
  fixes the documented key `kind`→`type`), §10.4 third view, §10.7 bidirectional
  bridge, new §10.9 reverse command channel.

**Tests**
- `RaceEngine.applyRoundMarkCommand` guard behaviour: advance when active,
  detector-reset (the next mark is auto-rounded cleanly), finish on the last
  mark, no-op when not active.
- `RoundMarkView` widget tests: hold → send, mark-name change → confirmed,
  send failure → no-connection, ambient static button.

## Key decisions (ADR 0024)
- **D2** `MessageClient` (fire-once) over `DataItem` (latched state).
- **D3** the command lands in the **service** isolate (FGS), not the suspended
  UI isolate — this is what makes the pocketed-phone case work.
- **D5** deliberate hold + round-trip-aware confirmation haptic.

## Testing
- `melos run analyze && format-check && test:dart && test:flutter` green locally.
- Kotlin is not analyzed by melos — verified via `flutter build apk --debug` for
  both apps.
- **Pending on-water validation:** the real round-trip over Bluetooth (watch
  button with the phone pocketed → engine advance → new `markName` → confirm
  haptic), alongside the next-water-test validation of ADR 0020/0021/0023.

## Known limitations
- The confirmation haptic relies on the `markName` changing (v1 simplification,
  no explicit ack); two consecutively identically-named marks would not produce
  the round-trip feel, but the advance still happens.
- `activeMarkIndex` is not persisted across an engine restart (existing v1 trait,
  ADR 0024 D7).

body:
The onboarding suggestion engine only fired for 3 scripted archetypes (email/project/ops). The llm_driven path (novel Agents like Jodin) produced a great interview but none of the canonical intent_tags, so the curated schedule/tool tables matched nothing: a clear "6:30am EDT daily" + named integrations -> 0/0/0.

New `interview-extract.ts` LLM pass reads the actual interview when the session finishes:
- **schedules**: parse the stated cadence into a real, validated cron + IANA tz (6:30am EDT daily -> `30 6 * * *`, America/New_York). Merged with curated; invalid crons dropped.
- **integrations**: extract the external services the Agent needs (Spotify, Instagram, X, Threads, ...), record each as a catalog gap (demand signal), and surface them in the preview as "needed integrations" instead of a blank 0.

Best-effort (malformed response -> empty, never blocks the preview). `SessionPreview` carries `needed_integrations`; the answer endpoint returns the preview raw so the web reads it directly. `parseExtraction` is pure + unit-tested. verify:all green (runtime 2158 + web 111).

Note: onboarding still SUGGESTS schedules (does not auto-write) ... auto-applying on confirm is a flagged follow-up.

author: msarson
body:
## What & why

The debugger could only stop at a planted breakpoint or a crash — there was no way to interrupt a program that's busy, looping, or sitting in an event loop. This adds a **pause** (break-into), modelled on the CA debugger's implementation.

## Engine

- `DebugSession.Pause()` injects a breakpoint via `DebugBreakProcess` (safe to call from the UI thread while running).
- The injected break arrives as an `EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT` on a throwaway OS thread. When a pause is pending and the break isn't one of our planted/temp breakpoints, the debug loop routes it to `HandlePause`, which picks a thread **actually in Clarion code** (`PickPauseThread`, falling back to the first readable thread, then the break thread) and stops there with reason `"paused"` — reusing the existing `Stop`/`ReportStop`/resume path. The whole process is frozen while the event is held, so every thread's context is stable to read.
- Hardening: any stop clears a pending pause request, so a breakpoint firing first can't leave a stale request that fires a spurious pause on the next continue.

## App

- **Pause** toolbar button + **F6**, enabled only while running. On the resulting stop the call stack, locals, globals and source populate exactly as for any other stop (if the picked thread is in Clarion code the source view jumps there; if it's in runtime/OS code the top frame shows as `[runtime]` and the stack is still walkable).

## Testing

Engine/App/Probe build clean; the existing breakpoint stop / stack walk / locals path is unchanged and verified against `sample/dbgtest` (no regression). The pause mechanism reuses that same proven stop/resume path — the only new pieces are the `DebugBreakProcess` injection and routing the resulting break.

⚠️ **Pause itself is not runtime-verified here:** triggering it needs a long-running / blocking target, and all the bundled samples run to completion in microseconds (none block on I/O or a window). @robertorenz please test against a real interactive Clarion app — run with no breakpoint set, hit **Pause/F6** while it's idle in its window loop, and confirm it stops with a usable call stack.

Two small, durable pieces:

- **Timeout-takeover race test.** When a demand read waits on an in-flight full-group prefetch, hits the `wait_for_group` deadline, and takes over with its own range GET, a later-completing stale prefetch must not overwrite the fresh foreground frame. Adds a deterministic test driving that race (stale full GET pending, replay epoch advanced, foreground serving fresh range bytes) and asserts the fresh frame wins and the stale GET is cancelled. This is the only deterministic coverage of that takeover path.
- **Range-GET validation hardening.** Extract `validate_range_get_result` and extend its test to reject both short and overlong range responses (was overlong only).

Full tiered suite green (588).

author: brunodmsi
body:
## Summary

Fixes two distinct embedded-wallet (email/Google login) bugs found via Sentry `GAP-FRONTEND-23C` and a Privy production scan. Neither touches `defaultChain` or any global default — both are scoped to the wallet/signer flow.

## Problem

### 1. Attestations fail with "still on chain 1" (`GAP-FRONTEND-23C`)
Embedded wallets initialise on mainnet (chain 1), which the GAP SDK rejects for attestations (`gapUnsupportedChainIds = [mainnet.id]`). Every embedded attestation must switch off chain 1 first — but `embeddedWallet.switchChain()` resolved **before** the provider actually reported the new chain, so the SDK received a still-on-chain-1 provider:

> Failed to obtain signer from embedded wallet: Couldn't switch your wallet to the required network (chain 8453); it is still on chain 1.

A read-only Privy lookup confirmed the affected user had a **single** embedded wallet — not a duplicate-wallet symptom.

### 2. Google signups still create duplicate embedded wallets
A scan of 3,901 Privy users shows that after the previous dedup fix shipped (release `c05e5dc`, 2026-06-12), duplicates are **still created for Google logins** — date-split: 5 post-fix dupe accounts, all `google_oauth`, 0 email (newest email dupe was 2026-06-10, pre-fix). The two wallets are minted 1–2s apart.

The difference is Google's **OAuth full-page redirect**, which reloads the page and wipes the in-memory module-level guard. Email's OTP flow stays in one JS context so its guard holds. Post-redirect, the hook created a second wallet before the first hydrated, because it checked only `user.linkedAccounts` (which hydrate late), not the live wallet list.

## Solution

- **`hooks/useZeroDevSigner.ts`** — new `switchEmbeddedWalletChain()`: switches, then polls raw `eth_chainId` with backoff until the provider confirms the target chain (ethers `getNetwork()` caches the first-detected network and masked the real chain), re-fetching the provider each attempt. Used by both the gasless and embedded-direct signer paths. `defaultChain` is **intentionally left unchanged** — the confirmed switch is the fix, so no user's default network selection is affected.
- **`hooks/useEnsureEmbeddedWallet.ts`** — takes `hasEmbeddedWallet`; skips when a live embedded wallet already exists, and waits for wallet state to settle before creating, re-checking once an existing wallet has had time to appear (a decision that survives the OAuth redirect, unlike the in-memory guard). Aborts and releases the slot if the user logs out or switches accounts during the settle window. Latest-value refs are synced in an effect (not mutated during render).
- **`components/Utilities/PrivyWagmiProviders.tsx`** — passes `hasEmbeddedWallet` to the hook.
- **`utilities/wait.ts`** — small shared `setTimeout`-promise helper (was duplicated in both hooks).

## Testing Steps

- Embedded (Google/email) user creates a project on Base → signer is obtained and the attestation succeeds (no "still on chain 1").
- New Google signup → exactly one embedded wallet (verify in Privy / via `getUsers`).
- Unit suites (59 tests) cover: switch success / propagation-race recovery / permanent-stuck error / transient `switchChain` rejection / provider can't report chain / numeric `eth_chainId`; and create / guard / embedded-exists / wallet-or-link appears mid-settle / logout / user-switch mid-settle / retry / exhaust.
- Scoped coverage of changed source: stmts 98 / branch 90 / funcs 100 / lines 98 (gate 60/60/70/70). `build`, `test (1)`, `static-checks`, `react-doctor` green in CI.

## Risk

Low. No schema, API, or global-default changes. The chain-switch helper adds bounded retries (≤5 attempts, ≤2.5s) only on the slow path; the happy path returns on the first poll. The settle window adds a one-time ~2.5s delay before *creating* an embedded wallet for brand-new signups (not before login or any existing-wallet flow).

## Notes

- Duplicate findings were verified with read-only Privy diagnostics (`getUserByWalletAddress` / `getUsers`), not committed here.
- Privy can only `deleteUser` (whole account), not unlink a single embedded wallet — this PR prevents *new* duplicates; it does not clean up existing ones.

author: sdebruyn
body:
## Root cause

`Shared/` is compiled into **both** the `OneLake` host target and the `OneLakeFileProvider` FPE target. Without an explicit `@objc(Name)`, Swift mangles each class's ObjC runtime name with the module prefix:

- host: `_TtC7OneLake15XPCEngineStatus`
- FPE: `_TtC18OneLakeFileProvider15XPCEngineStatus`

NSXPCInterface compares the reply-block class encoding on **both** ends of the connection. The mismatch causes `getEngineStatus` to be rejected as an undecodable message (`incompatible reply block signature`), dropping the XPC connection and leaving the Settings pane stuck on "Loading…".

## Fix

Added an explicit, stable ObjC name to each NSSecureCoding class that crosses (or is nested within a type that crosses) the XPC boundary:

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `Shared/XPCEngineStatus.swift` | `@objc public final class XPCEngineStatus` | `@objc(XPCEngineStatus) public final class XPCEngineStatus` |
| `Shared/XPCAccountInfo.swift` | `@objc public final class XPCAccountInfo` | `@objc(XPCAccountInfo) public final class XPCAccountInfo` |
| `Shared/XPCPausedWorkspace.swift` | `@objc public final class XPCPausedWorkspace` | `@objc(XPCPausedWorkspace) public final class XPCPausedWorkspace` |

With these annotations, both targets expose the ObjC class name `"XPCEngineStatus"` (etc.), so the reply-block encoding matches on both ends and the message decodes correctly.

## Shared/ audit

`OfemClientControlProtocol` exposes:
- `getEngineStatus(reply:)` → `XPCEngineStatus?` — fixed
- `XPCEngineStatus.pausedWorkspaces` contains `[XPCPausedWorkspace]` — fixed
- `XPCAccountInfo` is declared in `Shared/` and will cross XPC — fixed

No other `NSObject`/`NSSecureCoding` types are declared in `Shared/`. The `@objc public protocol OfemClientControlProtocol` uses module-agnostic selectors and does **not** need an explicit name.

Only the class declaration annotations were changed. Coding keys, NSSecureCoding logic, and `setClasses` whitelists are untouched.

## Verification

`make build-ci` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**, no new warnings in touched files (pre-existing `NSXPCConnection` Sendable warnings are in `OfemFPEClient.swift`, unrelated to this change).

Closes #254

author: jbailes
body:
## Summary

Fixes a wedge where **all** background delegates (roundtable reviews,
`aimee delegate --background`, coord jobs) get stuck in `pending` forever until
the server is restarted — and a restart only defers it.

## Root cause (this PR fixes the permanent-leak vector)

A background delegate whose request carries no timeout reaches the server with
`timeout_ms = 0`. Combined with an agent that has no configured `timeout_ms`
(`claude`/`codex`/`my-*` zero-init to 0), the per-call HTTP timeout is 0. In
`agent_bridge` `conn_open`, `timeout_ms <= 0` sets `deadline_ns = 0`, and
`conn_read` then loops on its 30 s per-recv timeout **forever**
(`conn_past_deadline` is false when `deadline_ns == 0`). A provider that accepts
the TLS connection but never responds (rate-limited / flaky) blocks the
compute-pool worker indefinitely, leaking its thread + provider concurrency
slot. Cancellation and the stale-monitor only update DB rows; neither can
interrupt a blocked `recv`.

**Live forensics:** server had worker threads blocked in `wait_woken` on `ESTAB`
provider TLS connections (recv-q = 0) while jobs sat `pending`.

## Fix

`delegate_effective_timeout_ms(request, agent_config)` — pure helper resolving
`request > agent-config > AGENT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`, guaranteeing a positive
timeout so a delegate run always returns (a timeout error then marks the job
`failed` via the existing result path). Applied in `delegate_worker`; scoped to
the delegate path — chat/streaming untouched. Unit-tested
(`test_delegate_effective_timeout`, incl. the `(0,0) -> default` case).

## This is a safety fix, not the architectural cure

The deeper issue (tracked separately): background delegates run on the global
compute pool, which defaults to **2 threads** (`CONFIG_DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_THREADS`).
Delegates are I/O-bound (≈100% network wait, ~0 CPU/RAM), yet each holds a whole
CPU-sized worker thread for the full remote call — so even *non-hung* slow
delegates saturate a 2-thread pool and queue everything behind them. The real
fix is to decouple delegate I/O concurrency from the CPU compute pool (dedicated
elastic I/O pool, or async provider calls). This PR stops a hung call from
holding a thread *forever*; it does not raise the effective concurrency.

## Test

`unit-test-agent` passes (incl. new regression). Changed TUs compile clean under
`-Werror`.

## Superseded

This draft is replaced by #19, the independently landable correctness layer. The unwind preplanning experiment moved to stacked draft #20.

#19 consolidates the supported ownership, migration, rollback, and publication work from #14, #16, and #17; #20 stays separate until its reverse-transition fallback is resolved.

---

## Summary

- extend Mach-O ownership proofs for Rust archive/member migration, local symbol retargets and renames, const/data sections, unwind metadata, symbol tables, and chained fixups
- persist direction-specific unwind transaction versions and validate exact member identities, reserve geometry, physical FDE ownership, and rollback bytes before reuse
- recover changed `__TEXT,__const` and relocation-bearing `__DATA,__const` owners from unique normalized archive records, including stale rustc invocation suffixes
- scope validated local retarget and rename evidence to its exact source input and archive/direct ownership domain
- reuse hardlinked Rust inputs after ctime-only churn only after stable content and identity validation
- collect exact incoming local-cohort edges and perform one fail-closed whole-input liveness plan instead of rebuilding the graph for every retarget

## Motivation

Small edits in uv, Ruff, and ty can repartition Rust codegen units, rename local symbols, exchange archive members, and move owned text, const/data, and unwind content. SLD previously fell back even when persisted state contained enough information to prove several of those transitions. This stack extends the proof model without treating a matching name, layout, or fingerprint as ownership by itself.

This PR is stacked on #16 and extends its mixed-CGU ownership and publication foundation; it does not supersede #16.

## Validation

- ty A/B/A/B incremental builds completed in 2.03-2.08s after the initial build, patched exactly one input and section per transition, converged to stable A/B hashes, and passed marker, version, check, codesign, and clean-oracle validation with zero retries or fallbacks

## Known limitations

- exact proofs intentionally fall back when archive identity, section ownership, relocation coverage, unwind hints, or rollback state is missing or ambiguous
- uv still falls back for the measured const/data transition because the data-relocation proof is incomplete; this stack improves the pre-fallback planning cost but does not claim a general direct-link uv speedup
- the measured Linux root-CGU mutations lack patch metadata and therefore full-relink; no Linux changed-link performance improvement is claimed for those cases
- retained-layout outputs can contain additional unreachable text, local-symbol, or compact-unwind metadata relative to a fresh link; live unwind and runtime semantics are validated independently

### Motivation
- Recursive `rm -rf` materializes child whiteouts but could double-count lower-layer files that were already hidden by upper-layer copy-on-write overrides, allowing quota bypass. 
- The goal is to preserve the child-whiteout behavior while preventing duplicate deductions from the aggregate `lower_hidden` counters. 
- Keep change minimal and local to overlay accounting logic so existing semantics stay intact.

### Description
- Introduce a path-keyed set `lower_hidden_paths` to track which lower entries have been accounted as hidden and initialize it in `OverlayFs::with_limits`.
- Change `hide_lower_file` and `hide_lower_dir` to accept a `&Path` and consult `record_hidden_path` to avoid incrementing `lower_hidden` twice for the same normalized path.
- Update all call sites (writes, CoW metadata paths, recursive delete child traversal) to pass the child path when hiding lower entries and preserve child whiteout materialization.
- Add a regression test `test_recursive_delete_skips_cow_hidden_children_for_limits` that reproduces the copy-on-write + recursive-delete quota case and ensures the write-limit check fails as expected.

author: chaliy
body:
### Motivation

- The default-enabled `tool_output_distillation` hook performed unbounded full-JSON serialization, cloning, per-array serialization checks, and pretty-printing on untrusted MCP/web_fetch results, creating a TM-DOS risk. 
- The change aims to prevent large attacker-controlled tool outputs from forcing excessive memory and CPU work in the pre-hard-limit capability hook. 
- Preserve distillation's reversibility and functionality for reasonable-sized results while ensuring worker stability under malicious/oversized inputs.

### Description

- Add a hard upstream ceiling `MAX_DISTILL_INPUT_BYTES = 1 MiB` and gate pre-processing via `serialize_json_bounded` so the hook refuses to work on inputs that would exceed that bound and avoid unbounded allocations. 
- Reuse the bounded serialized JSON for persistence instead of producing a second pretty-printed string, and avoid cloning/pretty-printing the full original after the size gate. 
- Remove per-array full-serialization checks during traversal and sample arrays by element count only, and add `BoundedJsonWriter` to implement the bounded serialization. 
- Update the durable spec `specs/tool-output-distillation.md` to document the bounded size gate, array-sampling behavior, and the new cap, and add unit tests covering the new behavior.

### Testing

- Ran `cargo fmt --check` which succeeded. 
- Ran targeted unit tests `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.96.0 cargo test -p everruns-core tool_output_distillation --all-features` and all tests passed (`22 passed`).

author: remcovanmook
body:
## Summary

Sharpens the network policy language and builds the kernel-enforced ACLs the design (07-5 §7.5.4/§7.5.7) prescribed but left unbuilt. The motivating case — `net.deny = 10.0.0.0/8` + `net.allow = *:443`, **deny wins** — is now expressible and enforced at the socket layer.

- **Policy language split (breaking, pre-release):** `[net]` → `[net.proxy]` (user-space egress: by-name+cidr allow/deny, resolve-and-pin) + `[net.bpf]` (the kernel/syscall ACL: cidr+ports only, no names, deny-first). `[net.bpf]` carries both `connect` and `bind`. A `[net.proxy]` rule under `mode = host` is a compile error. `cidr = "*"` = any host. Templates migrated + re-signed.
- **Connect ACL:** `[net.bpf].connect` enforced via the cgroup connect4/6 BPF + Landlock, deny-first, per mode (allow base in `host`; deny in every mode: invariant floor + author `[net.bpf].connect.deny` + `[net.proxy].deny.policy`).
- **Bind ACL (§7.5.7):** `[net.bpf].bind` enforced via bind4/6 BPF — dedicated `bind_{allow,deny}_v{4,6}` LPM tries, deny-first, default-deny. INADDR_ANY/`::` rewrites to the kennel loopback first, then the ACL gates the real address; the kennel's own `/28`/`/64` is seeded so in-subnet binds stay allowed by default; single-port allows get a Landlock `BIND_TCP` grant. Host-side inbound mirror remains roadmap.
- **Map-capacity validation:** over-cap deny/allow sets are a compile error naming the per-family limit (256 deny / 1024 allow, src/bpf/maps.h) rather than an opaque ENOSPC at spawn.
- **Verbose logging:** `log_level` in system.toml + a spawn-path Tracer threaded through kenneld, the privhelper factory, and kennel-bin-init (over the supervision wire). Documented that the trace spans two journals (kenneld → user; inside-kennel → system).
- **facade-socks5:** a bare connect/close (readiness probe) is now a clean disconnect, not a "failed to fill whole buffer" error.

## Tests

- Authored test-first per CODING-STANDARDS §7 (`test:` → `feat:`). Unit/integration cover policy translate (split, `*` expansion, host-mode reject, map caps), plan encode (connect+bind ACL, loopback seed, Landlock grants), the Plan + privhelper BPF wire round-trips, the LogLevel/Tracer contract, SOCKS5 greeting.
- BPF compile gate: all 8 programs clean under `clang -Werror`.
- **Hardware e2e** via the installed `kenneld.service` (standard toolchain), each a self-checking signed policy: `net-none`, `net-constrained`, `net-isolated` (per-kennel net-ns containment), `net-host-deny-wins` (connect deny beats allow), `net-bind-deny-wins` (bind deny beats allow — the BPF verifier accepted the new bind code).

## Gate

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` — all green.

author: rodesai
body:
## Summary

Switch the stored term postings to use ascending doc id order, and use a single in-memory representation (lazy-decode columnar) when reading term postings
- Postings, blocks, and merge operands now ascend: base_id is the lowest id, the skip block's last_id the highest, and the merge operator appends operands in delivery order (plain concatenation, no reversal). The scoring logic was already processing in ascending order as its more intuitive, so this just changes the storage format to do the same. There's no added cost on the storage side - the merge operator just concatenates postings in the opposite order from before.
- PostingListView is the canonical decoded representation: the old aos decode path (TermPostingsValue::decode_from_bytes/iter_entries, PostingsBlock/SkipBlock decode) is removed.
- TermPostingsValue is renamed to TermPostingsEncoder and is used to encode new postings from the indexer.
- The compaction filter streams postings block by block and copies blocks whose id range holds no deleted id verbatim — no decode, no re-encode, impacts preserved — so sparse deletes only pay for the blocks they touch.
- RFC-0006 Term Postings section updated to match.

| lang | kind | RAW_CE | STRUCT_CE | Δ | Δ-vs-shuffle |
|------|------|--------|-----------|------|------|
| **ko** | hangul | 2.90394 | 2.69189 | **+0.21205** | +0.10003 |

body:
**PR-LEDGER-5** — the last of the four ledger fixes. Books real payment-processing fees into the P&L.

## The defect (verified)
P&L net profit = `revenue − payroll − (manual expenses + AI cost)`. The **cost of collecting** revenue — card/ACH processing fees — was never an expense, so net profit was overstated by the processing fees on every collected invoice.

## The fix (real captured data, no estimate)
The fees are **already captured**: every paid invoice writes a `transaction_fee` org-ledger entry with the **actual computed amount** (ACH 1.0% capped $10 / Card 2.9% + $0.25) in `stripeWebhooks` (`:1079`, `:1325`). This folds them in:
- `calculateProcessingFees(workspaceId, start, end)` → `SUM(orgLedger.amount) WHERE entryType = 'transaction_fee'` over the period (real amounts, **no estimated rate**).
- `netProfit = grossProfit − (manualExpenses + aiOperations + processingFees)`; surfaced as `expenseBreakdown.paymentProcessing`, included in `expenseTotal`.

Same no-migration pattern as LEDGER-6 (per-line split not separately persisted → cached reads show 0 for the line while the total stays correct).

## Flagged for follow-up (not this PR)
`transaction_fee` is written from **both** `payment_intent.succeeded` and `charge.succeeded` handlers — if both fire for one payment, the captured fee would double. That's a **capture-side** concern; this P&L fold faithfully sums the canonical ledger (as the existing finance dashboard already does). Worth a Merger check (LEDGER-5b).

## Verification
Server `tsc` → **3567 (≤ baseline 3568; no new errors)**. Server-only, finance lane.

## Ledger Authority — all four done
LEDGER-6 (#558 ✅) · LEDGER-4 (#559 ✅) · LEDGER-3 (#560, in flight) · **LEDGER-5 (this)**. After these, P&L net profit reflects platform AI cost **and** payment-processing cost, refunds reconcile invoice paid totals, and disbursed payroll no longer double-counts the org ledger.

author: dp-web4
body:
The hub's Local-mode identity stored the Ed25519 **private key as plaintext JSON** — the sharpest exposure. Production now never writes a plaintext key.

## The security posture (per dp)
- **Fail-closed, not plaintext-default.** `gen-lct` always `save_encrypted` via `require_passphrase()`. There is no silent-plaintext path — that's exactly what could propagate and erode the trust foundation.
- **NULL passphrase is a deliberate first-class choice, never a default.** `env_passphrase()` returns `Some("")` for an explicit empty `HUB_PASSPHRASE` (≠ unset = `None`); the interactive prompt treats Enter as NULL. An empty passphrase **still encrypts** (uniform, re-keyable format) — never plaintext.
- `require_passphrase`: `HUB_PASSPHRASE` env (incl. empty) → TTY prompt (`rpassword`) → else error. The systemd daemon uses the env; humans get the prompt.

## Mechanism
- `save_encrypted`/`load_encrypted` via `web4_core::vault` (W4VT); `load_auto` sniffs W4VT vs legacy JSON — a pre-vault hub keeps loading (migrate once); reading plaintext OK, **writing** plaintext refused.
- All production load sites (serve/rest, mcp, session, init, CLI) use `load_auto`; library `save()`/`load()` remain for test fixtures only.

## Tests
Encrypted round-trip with a **private-key-never-on-disk** assertion; empty passphrase still encrypts; `load_auto` sniff incl. "explicit empty unlocks, *unset* does not." **145 lib + 13 daemon.**

## Scope
Covers the Sovereign **identity** (the catastrophic exposure). Hub **state** at rest is the follow-on — FileBackend sealing ports cleanly, but the live fleet hub is **Sqlite** (→ SQLCipher / FileBackend migration next).

Completes the QAppsWiki structure and tooling so populating content becomes a fill-in-the-blanks job, and ingests two curated quantum-error-correction catalogs.

body:
## Summary

- Snapshots were local Docker commits, so a sandbox created from a snapshot that placement landed on a **non-source node** failed to pull the image — UC-21 fails in cluster mode. The push-to-AOCR feature existed in code but was deployed nowhere (`mirror.push_host` empty, `SB_SNAPSHOT_PUSH_ENABLED` never emitted by Terraform).
- Wire `SB_SNAPSHOT_PUSH_ENABLED` (+ reconcile interval / max-in-flight) through the config chain that was missing it: `config/cluster.yml` → `locals.tf` → `nodes.tf` → `bootstrap.sh.tftpl`; set `mirror.push_host = aocr.aerol.ai`. Added a plan-time precondition so enabling push without push_host/cluster_id/PAT fails at `terraform plan`.
- Added an optional AOCR retention tag suffix (`SB_SNAPSHOT_PUSH_TAG_SUFFIX`, default empty = durable plain `latest`) so ephemeral clusters auto-reap snapshots. Applied to **both** the push ref and the cross-node pull ref (`DestRefFor`) since AOCR suffixes are real tags.
- Integration: cluster scenarios enable snapshot push with `--ttl-1h` (auto-reap), reuse the PAT's bound `cluster_id` (AOCR only authorizes pushes to the PAT's own `cluster/<id>/` namespace — confirmed in `aocr` `evaluateClusterPatScope`), and UC-21 retries the derived create to absorb the push-propagation window.

## Sandbox boot impact

`NormalizeCreateImageDistribution`'s cross-node branch now builds the AOCR pull ref with the configured tag suffix via `snapshotAOCRRef`. **This is pure string construction — no added DB query, HTTP round-trip, file I/O, or lock on `CreateSandbox` or its callees.** The background snapshot push runs off the create path (reconciler goroutine), unchanged. When `SB_SNAPSHOT_PUSH_ENABLED=false` (default) the create path is byte-identical to before.

## Idempotency

No new API surface. Snapshot push remains idempotent: re-pushing the same `cluster/<id>/snapshots/<name>:latest<suffix>` tag is a no-op at the registry (layers already present), and `DestRefFor` is a pure function of `(host, clusterId, name, suffix)`. The new `TagSuffix` only changes the tag string deterministically, so retries and concurrent pushes resolve to the same ref.

## Failure-path consistency

N/A — no multi-step write path touching both caddy and the store was changed. Snapshot push failures leave the row in `pending`/`error` for the reconciler to retry (existing behavior, unchanged).

## L4 / host-port-pool changes

N/A - neither touched.

## Test plan

- `go build ./...` — clean.
- `go test ./internal/service/ ./internal/config/` — pass, incl. new `TestSnapshotPusher_TagSuffix` (asserts suffix on push dest + `DestRefFor`, plain-`latest` default, malformed-suffix rejection).
- `terraform fmt -check .` + `terraform validate` — clean.
- `bash -n integration-tests/run.sh` — clean; simulated the cluster overlay yq to confirm `mirror.push_host`, `snapshot_push_enabled`, and `snapshot_push_tag_suffix=--ttl-1h` render correctly.
- Docs: added `SB_SNAPSHOT_PUSH_TAG_SUFFIX` to the snapshots config table (no curl, no new page).

> **Pre-merge / pre-apply check:** AOCR's `AUTH_CLUSTER_PAT_TOKENS` must bind the token in `config/secrets.yml` to cluster_id `prod-aerolvm-us-east-1` (the id the cluster scenarios use unchanged), or pushes will 403. Needs a real `terraform apply` against a cluster to verify push end-to-end.

author: k-pz
body:
## What

A "lazy senior developer" simplification pass (the best code is the code you never wrote). After vetting the whole codebase, this lands the one change that is unambiguously simpler *and* behaviour-preserving: `earliest_date` in `comic_metadata.py` was a hand-rolled minimum-tracking loop with a manual `None` sentinel. The standard library already expresses exactly this with `min(..., default=None)`:

```python
# before — 7 lines, manual sentinel
earliest: str | None = None
for value in values:
    if len(value) < 4 or not value[:4].isdigit():
        continue
    if earliest is None or value < earliest:
        earliest = value
return earliest

# after — 2 lines, stdlib
qualifying = (value for value in values if len(value) >= 4 and value[:4].isdigit())
return min(qualifying, default=None)
```

Same contract: the earliest year-prefixed value, or `None` when nothing qualifies. Covered by the existing `test_earliest_date_picks_minimum_and_ignores_undated` test (including the empty / all-undated cases that exercise the `default=None` path).

## Why only one change

I scanned both backend and frontend for over-engineering. Most candidate "simplifications" were rejected because they would have *added* code or changed behaviour, against the spirit of the pass:

- Inlining shared helpers like `_str` / `coerce_optional` duplicates logic at call sites (more code, not less), and `str(value or "")` is not equivalent to `_str` for falsy non-empty values like `0`.
- `(cursor.rowcount or 0) > 0` is a deliberate `None`-guard, not redundant — dropping it risks a `TypeError`.
- Frontend ideas like replacing `.find()` over a small options list with a generated lookup map, or swapping `.filter(Boolean)` for `.filter(x => x)`, add surface area without reducing it.

The codebase is already lean and passes strict lint / typecheck / format / tests, so restraint is the correct outcome.

## Heads-up (no change made)

Several `except` clauses use the unparenthesised multi-type form, e.g. `except OSError, ValueError:`. This **looks** like a Python-2 error but is valid, canonical syntax under the repo's pinned **Python 3.14**, and `ruff format` actively prefers it (it rewrites the parenthesised form back). Left as-is intentionally — flagging it because tooling running on Python < 3.14 will mis-report it as a syntax error.

## Verification

`ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `ty check`, and the full `pytest` suite (502 passed) are all green.

author: vanceingalls
body:
## What

Extends SDK shadow-dispatch visibility past the property-edit path and turns it on by default. Stacked on `main` (Stage 7 step 3b / #1450 merged); **PR 2/2** (`shadow-ext-gsap-fidelity`) builds on this.

- **Default shadow ON** — `STUDIO_SDK_SHADOW_ENABLED` now defaults `true` (disable via `VITE_STUDIO_SDK_SHADOW_ENABLED=false`). Server stays authoritative; no user-visible change.
- **Delete shadow** — `removeElement`, parity = element gone from the SDK session.
- **Timing shadow** — `setTiming`, parity = snapshot `start`/`duration`/`trackIndex`.
- **GSAP-add shadow** — `addGsapTween`, parity = `can()` + dispatch + returned tween id.

## Why

The property-path shadow (#1450) only saw style/text/attribute/html-attribute edits — it gave no visibility into delete, timeline trims, or GSAP edits. These ops don't flow through `persistDomEditOperations`, so each needs its own tap. Defaulting shadow on means we collect `sdk_shadow_dispatch` parity telemetry from all traffic with zero behavior change.

## How

- `sdkShadow.ts`: `can()`-first shadow core (pure addressing/validity pre-check) + `runShadowDelete` / `runShadowTiming` / `runShadowGsapTween`.
- Wiring: delete via `onElementDeleted` (`useDomEditSession` → `useDomEditCommits` → `useElementLifecycleOps`); timing in `useTimelineEditing` (moved `useSdkSession` above it to share the single session); GSAP-add in `useGsapAnimationOps`.
- Telemetry tagged `op: property|delete|timing|gsap`.

## Test plan

- `sdkShadow.test.ts` — 17 tests: delete (parity / no-hf-id / not-addressable), timing (snapshot parity), gsap-add (success / `E_NO_GSAP_TIMELINE`), plus existing property tests.
- typecheck + 600-line studio gate clean.

Phase 1 of **RepoRadar** — a local-first Typer CLI that mines GitHub for AI/LLM/QA/dev-tool repos, dedupes against the local project portfolio, scores opportunities with an explicit weighted model, clusters by theme, and emits ranked build ideas as Markdown + JSON reports plus Kanban task drafts (drafts only — never auto-created).

## Highlights
- uv + Python 3.12, Pydantic v2, httpx (DI/mockable), rapidfuzz, Typer/Rich, Jinja2
- Deterministic, no LLM keys required; every idea cites fetched repos
- Word-boundary tag inference, shared-tag-gated dedupe, monotonic weighted scoring
- Per-day SQLite search cache (`~/.reporadar/cache.db`) with prune; `mine --dry-run`
- Idea blueprints externalized to `configs/blueprints.yaml`

## Quality
- **115 tests, ~97% coverage** (gate 90%)
- ruff + mypy strict clean; CI runs lint/format/type/test + `pip-audit`
- All findings from 4 rounds of engineering review (B1–B14, H3) resolved

author: garethpaul
body:
## Summary

Popup actions can no longer read or redirect a tab through the content script after losing message or document ownership. Content-script requests now require the exact popup extension page, and a delayed redirect is ignored when the tab has navigated to a different origin.

## Baseline

The content-script listener accepted `geturl` and `redirect` from any sender that could address the tab. A popup could also persist an origin, wait for the asynchronous acknowledgement, and then redirect a newly loaded unrelated document using the stale callback.

## Improvements

- Authenticate the exact popup extension URL and extension ID before dispatching content-script actions.
- Require the current document's normalized origin to equal the persisted blocked origin before redirecting.
- Keep invalid, unauthorized, malformed, unknown-action, and stale-origin requests side-effect free.
- Add a real-script Node VM suite and mutation-sensitive portable contracts without changing permissions, storage, background routes, or Manifest V2 behavior.

## Validation

- Pre-fix focused test reproduced unauthorized URL access.
- Repository-root and external-directory `make check` passed the baseline plus all five real-script suites under Node 20.
- JavaScript and POSIX-shell syntax checks passed.
- Five isolated hostile mutations were rejected for sender authorization, document-origin ownership, wrong-extension fixtures, guidance, and completed plan evidence.
- Security review found one malformed-message coverage gap; commit `9ce42d7` added it and the full gate remained green.
- Exact diff, artifact, dependency/permission/workflow, whitespace, conflict-marker, and credential-pattern audits passed.
- Unpacked-extension browser execution remains `not run`: `agent-browser` is unavailable and this flow requires loading an extension rather than navigating to a served route.

## Risk

The intentional compatibility change is that non-popup extension contexts can no longer invoke content-script URL reads or redirects, and stale redirects are dropped after cross-origin navigation. The popup's valid add/block flow and existing origin normalization remain unchanged.

## Follow-Ups

This PR is stacked on PR #13 and must retain base-first ordering. The broader Manifest V3 and `declarativeNetRequest` migration remains separate architectural work.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

For the first unpacked-extension verification session, inspect Chrome extension errors for `runtime.lastError`, confirm popup add/block still redirects the same synthetic origin, and confirm a tab navigated before mutation acknowledgement is not redirected. Healthy signals are successful same-origin popup flows with no extension errors; any valid popup flow losing URL access or redirect capability is the rollback trigger. The maintainer owns the exact-head browser matrix before merge or release.

author: apermo
body:
## Problem

`config/application.php` set `$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'] = DOMAIN_CURRENT_SITE` for **every** WP-CLI invocation. WP-CLI derives the target host from `--url` *before* `wp-config` loads, so this overwrite clobbered it — and every `wp` command ran against the main site (blog 1) regardless of `--url`.

Verified on prod: `wp option get blogname --url=https://translate.chrdm.de/` (and `kb.chrdm.de`, `freunde.…`) all return the **main** site's `blogname`/`siteurl`.

### Impact
- The translate.chrdm.de Traduttore queue can't be drained — `wp cron event run --url=https://translate.chrdm.de` runs on the main site, so blog 6's `traduttore.update` / `traduttore.generate_zip` events never fire (breaks #78's cron).
- `wp traduttore project update|language-pack build --url=…` can't target the subsite (blocks #80/#82/#84 onboarding).
- Latent: the deploy's `for url in $(wp site list …); do wp cachify flush --url="$url"` loop only ever flushed the main site.

## Fix

Guard the default with `empty($_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'])` so it only applies as a fallback when WP-CLI did **not** set a host (i.e. no `--url`). `--url`-derived hosts are preserved, so subsite targeting works; plain `wp` commands still get the main-domain fallback and behave exactly as before.

```php
if (defined('WP_CLI') && WP_CLI && empty($_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'])) {
    $_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'] = Config::get('DOMAIN_CURRENT_SITE');
}
```

## Verification after deploy

`wp option get blogname --url=https://translate.chrdm.de/` should return the translate subsite (not "Christoph Daum"), and `wp traduttore info --url=https://translate.chrdm.de/` should run. `php -l` clean. Part of #74.

body:
## Problem

The Dockerfile runner stage copies from `.next/standalone` and runs `server.js`, but this directory is never created because `output: 'standalone'` was missing from `cms/next.config.ts`. This caused the build to fail with `"/app/.next/standalone": not found`.

## Solution

Added `output: 'standalone'` to the `nextConfig` object in `cms/next.config.ts`. This instructs Next.js to produce the `.next/standalone` directory with `server.js` and all required dependencies, which is exactly what the Dockerfile's runner stage expects to copy and execute.

### Changes
- **Modified** `cms/next.config.ts`

body:
## Summary

Adds a spec-driven development workflow for working with Claude, plus a documented worktree branching convention. Tooling and docs only; no application code changes.

## Changes

- **Spec-driven loop** as four slash commands in `.claude/commands/`, where the GitHub issue body is the single source of truth:
  - `/spec` turns an idea into a structured issue (problem, acceptance criteria, scope, tasks).
  - `/plan` reads the issue, plans against `.claude/rules/`, posts the plan, and cuts the branch.
  - `/implement` builds task-by-task with tests and runs the gates.
  - `/ship` runs the `code-reviewer` agent and opens a PR with `Closes #N`.
- **Feature request issue template** reshaped into an implementable spec: adds Acceptance Criteria (required), Scope / Out of scope, Implementation Tasks, and Affected areas.
- **CLAUDE.md** gains a Spec-Driven Workflow, Working with AI, and Agents section, turning it into a workflow guide rather than only a reference.
- **Worktree workflow rule** at `.claude/rules/worktrees.md`: documents GitHub Flow with one worktree per branch (cut from `main`, merge via PR) and a list-confirm-remove cleanup process for merged worktrees. Referenced from CLAUDE.md.
- **Permissions**: allow `gh issue/pr/project/label` in `.claude/settings.json` so the loop runs without re-prompting.

## Testing

- [ ] Tested on macOS
- [ ] Tested on Windows
- [ ] Tested on Linux

Not platform-specific: this PR only touches `.claude/`, `.github/`, and `CLAUDE.md`. Verified the feature request template parses as valid YAML and `settings.json` parses as valid JSON.

author: hiltonfam
body:
## Summary

This PR implements Phase 3 of Sentinel by adding an optional Reticulum/LXMF helper-backed sender.

The LXMF sender is implemented as a narrow synchronous helper integration rather than a native Reticulum/LXMF protocol implementation. This keeps Sentinel modular, dependency-light, and aligned with the existing best-effort fan-out architecture.

## Changes

- Added optional LXMF sender support.
- Added `src/lxmf_sender.rs`.
- Added CLI flags:
  - `--lxmf-command <PATH>`
  - `--lxmf-destination <DESTINATION>`
  - `--lxmf-config <PATH>` optional
- Registered LXMF as a best-effort sender only when both command and destination are provided.
- Added clear validation for partial LXMF configuration.
- Sent alert message text to the helper over stdin.
- Added deterministic helper command construction.
- Added tests for registration, command construction, stdin message delivery, failure behavior, and spool integration.

## Helper Contract

Sentinel invokes the configured helper as:

`<lxmf-command> --destination <destination> [--config <config>]`

Sentinel writes `Alert.message_text` to the helper process stdin.

- Exit code `0` means success.
- Non-zero exit means best-effort failure.
- Failures do not block Meshtastic delivery.
- Failures are recorded through the existing opt-in spool path when `--spool-path` is configured.

## Validation

The following checks passed:

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check`
- `cargo test`

Test results:

- 41 passed
- 0 failed

## Compatibility

This PR preserves existing Sentinel behavior:

- Meshtastic remains primary and required.
- Discord remains optional and best-effort.
- Failure spool remains opt-in.
- SAME decoding unchanged.
- County filtering unchanged.
- National alert override unchanged.
- Test alert behavior unchanged.

## Out of Scope

This PR does not include:

- Native Reticulum/LXMF protocol implementation
- MeshCore integration
- Replay workers
- Background workers
- Async runtime
- Dashboard functionality
- CAP ingestion

## Summary

- **HNSW ef_search fix**: pgvector's default `hnsw.ef_search = 40` capped search results at 40 regardless of `--limit`. Fixed by wrapping the similarity search in a transaction and issuing `SET LOCAL hnsw.ef_search = max(40, limit*2)` before the query so the candidate count scales dynamically.

body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/cfy-mesgna616-hotel-react/agent-runs/6a307e5bf122f8a0946d4943

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** fix the error i see on the brsower

✅ **Result:** Fixed three browser-blocking errors in the React hotel app.

**OpenSSL build failure (primary error)**

The app was failing to compile entirely because `react-scripts` v3 uses an older webpack that relied on a legacy OpenSSL API removed in Node.js v17+. The environment runs Node.js v24, so webpack threw `ERR_OSSL_EVP_UNSUPPORTED` on startup — preventing any code from loading in the browser. Fixed by adding `NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider` to both the `start` and `build` scripts in `package.json`.

**Broken bookings data source with no fallback**

The bookings table fetched from `https://cyf-react.glitch.me/delayed`, an external Glitch.me endpoint that is no longer available. This left the table permanently empty or in an error state. The fetch now falls back to the local `fakeBookings.json` when the remote API is unreachable, so the table always has data. The search function was also fixed to filter against the full original list (not the already-filtered list), so searching multiple times works correctly.

**Unhandled fetch in CustomerProfile**

`CustomerProfile` was issuing a fetch on every render — including the initial render with an empty customer ID — with no error handler. This caused unhandled promise rejections in the console. The component now skips the fetch when no ID is provided and catches any network errors gracefully.

**Missing table header column**

The bookings table had 8 header columns (`<th>`) but 9 data columns (`<td>`) because the "Show Profile" button column had no header. A "Profile" header was added to align the table correctly.

author: numnx
body:
## Summary

Investigation + fixes for sprint-orchestration issues found in the CODUX-4/CODUX-5 sprints, where Jules sessions completed **without producing a PR** yet tasks settled as `completed`.

### Root cause
The `completed_task_without_pr` QA safety net **failed open**: once the retry budget was spent, the merge gate returned `mergeAllowed: true` (`retries_exhausted`) and the task settled as completed with no PR. Compounded by the QA reviewer crashing on a sandbox auth error — each infra crash burned a retry (default `maxTaskReviewRuns` is 1).

### Changes
- **Fail-closed QA gate** — exhaustion blocks the merge instead of allowing it. Reviewer infra crashes (no verdict) don't consume the verdict budget (`countDecisiveTaskRuns`); they're bounded by an infra ceiling before escalating.
- **Human escalation** — a terminally-unverified code-complete task is parked in `QA_REVIEW_FAILED` with a `human_escalation_required` attention item (block-for-human).
- **Valid run state** — `QA_REVIEW_FAILED` is a task/planning status, not a run state; persist run state as `COMPLETED` (`toPersistedTaskRunState`) so `task_runs.state` stays valid.
- **Correct status on rerun** — a reactivated session (rerun/continuation of a non-merged completed task) now surfaces as `RUNNING` instead of staying stuck on `completed`; merged and `QA_REVIEW_FAILED` tasks are protected.
- **Rerun resets QA state** — a manual rerun clears prior QA history + guardrail so the fresh attempt is reviewed instead of inheriting the exhausted budget.
- **No QA on merged tasks** — `completed_task_without_pr` no longer triggers when a task has merge evidence (`is_merged` / `worker_branch` / `pr_url`); fixes QA misfiring on already-merged tasks after a sprint reload.

### Tests
- New coverage for the gate / escalation / session-reactivation / rerun-reset / merged-task paths.
- Fixed two slow flaky QA follow-up tests that shelled out to real docker/git (~25s hang each) by stubbing `fastForwardResumedWorkspace` — that file went from 53s to ~1s.
- Full suite green: **3480 passing**, typecheck clean.

author: nalutripician
body:
## Summary

Go port of [azure-cosmos-dotnet-v3#5844](https://github.com/Azure/azure-cosmos-dotnet-v3/pull/5844), addressing [azure-sdk-for-go#26649](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-go/issues/26649) (the Go sibling of dotnet #5805).

### The bug (proven before fixing)
In `sdk/data/azcosmos/cosmos_client_retry_policy.go`, the transport-error branch of `clientRetryPolicy.Do` honored the caller's `ctx.Err()` **before** consulting the cross-region failover decision. When an unhealthy preferred region consumes the caller's deadline while a read is in flight, the policy returned the cancellation immediately — **no attempt against the next preferred region, and the unhealthy region was never marked unavailable**, so subsequent callers were affected too.

A new test (`TestCallerCancellationDoesNotPreemptCrossRegionFailover`) reproduces this: against the unfixed code it failed with `context canceled` and the failover region received zero requests.

### Key architectural finding
`clientRetryPolicy` is a **PerRetry** policy, below azcore's built-in retry policy, which unconditionally overrides the result with the caller's `ctx.Err()` on the response path (`runtime/policy_retry.go`). A cancelled caller therefore can never observe a "rescued" success — which matches .NET #5844's documented semantics: *the caller surfaces cancellation immediately while the detached task runs to completion for its side-effects*.

### The fix
On caller-cancel during a retryable **read** connection error with a genuine cross-region target, the policy now:
1. **Synchronously** applies the cross-region failover bookkeeping (`performCrossRegionFailover`, extracted from `attemptRetryOnNetworkError`) — marking the unhealthy region unavailable so **subsequent callers fail over**.
2. **Launches a detached, internally bounded background attempt** (`spawnDetachedFailover`) against the next preferred region on a `context.WithoutCancel` + grace window (`metadataFailoverGraceWindow`, 10s) — completing the failover read and warming the connection pool / downstream state. Single bounded attempt, panic-recovered — no unbounded background work.
3. Returns the caller's own cancellation, as before.

Writes and single-region accounts retain their existing fail-fast behavior.

## Changes
- `cosmos_client_retry_policy.go` — caller-cancellation handling in `Do`; new `performCrossRegionFailover`, `hasCrossRegionTarget`, `spawnDetachedFailover`; `retryContext.detachedGraceUsed` one-shot flag; `metadataFailoverGraceWindow` (test-overridable var). `attemptRetryOnNetworkError` refactored to reuse `performCrossRegionFailover` (behavior unchanged).
- `cosmos_client_retry_policy_test.go` — proof/regression test + a cancelling mock transport.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — Bugs Fixed entry.

## Testing
- New test passes; pre-fix it fails (bug proven).
- Full `azcosmos` unit suite green; `go vet` and `gofmt` clean.
- Self-reviewed: confirmed no goroutine race (clone shares read-only `opValues`; write happens-before spawn, no concurrent writer), no context leak (`defer cancel()`), and faithful refactor of the cross-region branch.

author: cporcellijr
body:
## Summary

Fixed a bug in EPUB CFI (Canonical Fragment Identifier) parsing where spine items with an index of 6 were incorrectly discarded. The parser was using value-based logic to skip the package marker (`/6`), which caused CFIs with a spine step of 6 (e.g., `/6/6!/...`) to be misparsed.

## Changes

- **Refactored `_parse_cfi_components()` logic** in `src/utils/ebook_utils.py`:
  - Replaced value-based loop logic with positional-based step identification
  - For CFIs with a redirect: the spine item is now identified as the last package step (by position), not by skipping non-6 values
  - For CFIs without a redirect: the spine item is now identified as the second indexed step (if present), or the first step otherwise, rather than looping until a non-6 value is found
  - Added clarifying comments explaining the package marker and spine item identification strategy

- **Added test coverage** in `tests/test_cross_format_normalization_locator_priority.py`:
  - `test_parse_cfi_components_supports_spine_step_six()`: validates parsing of `/6/6!/4/232/2/2/2:0` correctly identifies spine step as 6
  - `test_parse_cfi_components_supports_minimal_cfi_with_spine_step_six()`: validates minimal CFI `/6/6!/:0` correctly identifies spine step as 6 with no element steps

## Implementation Details

The fix distinguishes between the package marker (the leading `/6` representing the spine container) and the spine item index by using positional logic rather than value matching. This allows CFIs where the actual spine item happens to be 6 to parse correctly without being filtered out.

author: eramusa
body:
## Summary

Makes the Rust engine (`softhsmrustv3`) **fully PKCS#11 v3.2 compliant via its native C ABI**: `p11_v32_compliance_test -c all` goes from **28 → 315 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 SKIP**, and the per-test results are **byte-for-byte identical to the C++ engine** (`libsofthsmv3.dylib`, also 315/0/0 — diff of the 315 result lines is empty).

**Root cause:** the C ABI was 32-bit/WASM-shaped — it marshaled pointers/templates/mechanism params as `u32`, which works in WASM (32-bit pointers) but truncates on native 64-bit (`CKR_FUNCTION_FAILED`). The validated KMIP/ACVP path was unaffected (it bypasses the C ABI via `softhsmrustv3::native::*`). This PR re-plumbs the C ABI to native width (`usize` == u32 on wasm32, u64 on native) and completes the v3.2 mechanism/conformance set.

## What changed (per-commit table in `rust/CK_ABI_NATIVE_COMPLIANCE_PLAN.md`)

- **Width re-plumb** `u32 → usize`: templates, `CK_MECHANISM`/params, nested `CK_*_PARAMS` (GCM, ECDH, PSS, SP800-108, auth-wrap) at `size_of::<usize>()` offsets, `store_ulong` at native CK_ULONG width (fixes `C_FindObjects` byte-exact matching), and the `C_GetAttributeValue` length write-back (`CK_UNAVAILABLE_INFORMATION` = `usize::MAX`).
- **Mechanisms/behaviors completed:** raw `CKM_RSA_PKCS` sign/verify, AES-CBC(-PAD) key wrap, ChaCha20 keygen, AES-CMAC SP800-108 PRF, RIPEMD-160, SHA3-384-RSA (PKCS#1 v1.5 + PSS), the 4 dual-function ops, ML-DSA/SLH-DSA/EdDSA multi-part, X25519/X448 derive, **HSS/LMS + XMSS^MT keygen+sign**, the v3.0 message-based API, generic-secret KCV via **SHA-1** (was SHA-256), `CKF_ASYNC_SESSION` rejection, RSA private-component sensitivity, keygen `CKA_KEY_TYPE` validation, SPKI on private PQC keys, 36-char UUID `CKA_UNIQUE_ID`, `C_LoginUser` parity.
- **Function exports:** all `C_*` exported as `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` (standard module behavior), lighting up async, session-cancel, ML-KEM encap/decap, authenticated-wrap, and the message API.
- **WASM:** rebuilt the tracked `rust/pkg_bundler` at the 315-level and added `rust/build-wasm-bundle.sh` to automate the `__wbg_get_memory` post-build shim.

## Test evidence
- **Native compliance: 315 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 SKIP** — identical per-test to the C++ engine.
- **KMIP interop + KAT replay: 15/15** (kat_replay 8 + interop_kat 2 + pqc_interop_engine 5) — held green after every commit.
- **`cargo test --lib`: 201 / 0.**
- **WASM:** `cargo check --target wasm32` clean; conformance harness 188/0; KAT parity 12/12 byte-exact.
- Every `CK*` constant added was verified against `src/lib/pkcs11/pkcs11t.h` (the normative header), not guessed.

## Reviewer notes
- **Run the interop gate single-threaded** (`cargo test ... -- --test-threads=1`) — the parallel run hits a known concurrent-compile flake on `ml_kem_decap_byte_exact` (passes single-threaded).
- The validated `rust/` tree was never touched on `main` during development (this branch is the only place the changes live).
- Isolated, additive work; no behavioral change to the KMIP native path.

author: alexremn
body:
This adds **finalizer-doctor** — a kubectl plugin that safely diagnoses and clears finalizers on resources stuck in `Terminating`.

It pinpoints the blocking finalizer and the dead controller / APIService, cleans truly-orphaned resources first, and clears finalizers only as a gated last resort (dry-run by default, evidence-based verdict, proof-bound apply).

- Repo: https://github.com/alexremn/finalizer-doctor
- Release: https://github.com/alexremn/finalizer-doctor/releases/tag/v0.1.0
- License: Apache-2.0

Both `kubectl finalizer-doctor` and a short `fid` are shipped as binaries; this krew plugin installs `kubectl finalizer-doctor`.
